# Readings by line

*Which lines of the record's argument each reading in force serves, and
which readings no line yet builds on. Generated from `record/theory.d/` and
the entries that cite it: edit those, not this page.*

A reading (THEORY) is the record's account of what a work holds. It
carries no `line` of its own. A reading serves a line when an entry of that
line uses it: a claim or argument grounds on it, it corroborates a claim
or marks the limit of one's scope,
it answers or bears on a question, it reports a case, or a case or term
draws on it. Its lines are the
first lines of those entries, as [ADR-085](../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md) reads a relation, and entries
that are Superseded or Rejected do not count. They are read off the
relations when this page is built, so a reading gains or loses a line as
the argument around it changes.

Of 929 readings in force,
761 serve at least one line and 168
serve none.

## Distributed agency

- [THEORY-004](../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md): A representation is determined by its centred kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal transformation, and the rotation-aligned distance between two representations equals the Bures distance between their kernels *(used by 6; also pragmatic-transport, formal-apparatus, learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-027](../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md): Two individually decisive people, weak Pareto and an unrestricted domain cannot all hold, even when choice need only yield a best element; unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability *(used by 5; also will-organization, organizational-affect, formal-apparatus, authenticity)*
- [THEORY-028](../record/theory.d/THEORY-028.md): The expected bias of any data-dependent choice, and the expected generalisation error of any learning algorithm, is at most √(2σ²·I) for σ-subgaussian losses, where I is the information the output carries about the data *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-031](../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md): The likelihood-ratio detector is optimal under the payoff, Neyman–Pearson and posterior criteria, which differ only in its threshold, so performance is an ROC and the criterion a point on it; d′ is criterion-free only for equal-variance normal signal and noise *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-066](../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): A Markov-blanket partition is defined relative to a chosen internal set, so a graph has one around almost any set of nodes, and the formalism alone does not say which set is the system *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-068](../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md): In a two-alternative choice made by two competing leaky accumulators, the decision is optimal only when leak and mutual inhibition balance, so that the network integrates the difference of the evidence without loss; imbalance bounds accuracy at any fixed time and weights early or late evidence *(used by 7; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-073](../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md): In Friston's 2013 formulation and the applications the record holds, a Markov blanket does not individuate a system: where it falls is fixed by modelling choices made before it is traced (the coupling graph, the internal set and the time at which steady state is assumed), and a blanket read from a fixed graph is the same whether the system produced the boundary or it was imposed *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-081](../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md): The evidence of any model formed from a full model by changing only its prior is the full evidence times the full posterior expectation of the prior ratio, so the Savage–Dickey ratio is its point-mass case and choosing which parameters to keep is evidence maximisation over the prior *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-082](../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md): Steepest descent is defined only relative to a metric, and Amari's proof that natural-gradient learning is Fisher efficient needs the Fisher information at the optimum to be invertible, the condition whose failure WBIC calls singular; in a multilayer perceptron it fails wherever an output weight is zero *(used by 4; also learned-structure, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-087](../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md): The Bayesian complexity penalty grows as (d/2) log n in a regular model, where the curvature at the optimum sets the Occam factor, and as λ log n in a singular one, where λ is the real log canonical threshold; with the prior positive on the optimal set, λ falls below d/2 when that set is infinite or has a point of degenerate curvature, and equals d/2 when it is finitely many points of non-degenerate curvature *(used by 5; also pragmatic-transport, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-124](../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md): In Posani et al.'s analysis of the IBL Brainwide Map, recorded while trained mice performed one visual decision task, the eight-variable selectivity profiles of neurons within one cortical area clustered beyond a covariance-matched Gaussian null only in VISp, AUDp and SSp-ul of about 20 areas tested, while profiles pooled across areas clustered along anatomical lines; and over the task conditions each area distinguishes, at least 95% of random balanced dichotomies were linearly decodable above a label-shuffled null in 15 of 16 areas, a lenient criterion *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-127](../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md): On the court agenda, and on any agenda in which every proposition reaches every other by conditional entailment and some minimally inconsistent triple stays consistent with two of its members negated, a group whose judgments are robustly rational under universal domain and respect unanimity cannot form its judgment on each proposition from its members' judgments on that proposition alone unless one member dictates; its judgments must supervene on the members' whole sets of judgments, and so can depart from what the members judge on the same proposition while being wholly fixed by them *(used by 4; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-132](../record/theory.d/THEORY-132.md): Stability, a system's speed of return to equilibrium after disturbance, and resilience, its capacity to absorb change and persist within its domain of attraction, are distinct properties that can trade off, so a system can be highly unstable and highly resilient, and managing it for constancy can erode its resilience *(used by 4; also will-organization, nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-133](../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md): In List and Menzies's account of causes as difference-makers, a higher-level property that makes a difference to an effect is its cause, and its realizer is not, exactly when in some nearest situation without that realizer the property is realized differently and the effect still occurs; which holds depends on each causal system's counterfactual structure, not on levels a priori *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-134](../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md): Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time *(used by 12; also will-organization, nucleating-argument, realizability, readiness)*
- [THEORY-136](../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md): A persistent or abrupt change is not evidence that a system has alternative stable states: field patterns such as jumps, multimodality and dual relationships also arise from a stepwise driver or a simple threshold, and only hysteresis, initial-state dependence or a lasting shift after a temporary disturbance, with slow return excluded, comes close to showing one *(used by 7; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-138](../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md): X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-140](../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md): The Columbia Accident Investigation Board found that the institutional causes of the Challenger accident had not been fixed and recurred in Columbia's: in both, evidence that the design was not performing as expected was repeatedly reinterpreted as acceptable, each decision seeming correct in itself and each survived anomaly justifying the next flight, while budget and schedule pressure, consensus sign-off, a hierarchy that kept dissent from rising and a safety organization dependent on the program it oversaw sustained the pattern for twenty years and undid post-Challenger reforms *(used by 6; also organizational-normativity, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-146](../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md): In Holman and Bruner's bandit model of honest Bayesian researchers whose beliefs funding cannot touch, who differ in method and whose influence and training of newcomers follow productivity, industry funding of those whose methods already favour its drug lowers, in the runs their figures report, the share of the community on the better treatment, and has no effect without methodological diversity; at the one setting reported, an independent funder that counts industry-funded trials toward its merit threshold lowers that share further, and one that excludes them raises it *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-149](../record/theory.d/THEORY-149.md): Users can govern a shared resource durably without either privatisation or central control, and the institutions that last are marked not by particular rules but by structural regularities: user-made and user-monitored rules, graduated sanctions, cheap local conflict resolution, recognised rights to self-organise, and nested layers of governance *(used by 3; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-194](../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md): On Monte Carlo samples of the 2D Ising model and of the 2D dimer model with added noise spins, a block coarse-graining trained to maximize mutual information with the system beyond a buffer recovered the variables renormalization already uses (Kadanoff block spins; the dimers' low-momentum electric fields, with no weight on the noise), and iterated on 128 × 128 Ising samples gave the flow away from the critical point, locating it to about 1% and giving ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a restricted Boltzmann machine trained by contrastive divergence on the noisy dimer data coupled to the noise and to columnar patterns instead *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-198](../record/theory.d/THEORY-198.md): For a finite-range lattice Hamiltonian, a block coarse-graining that keeps all the mutual information the block shares with the system beyond a buffer makes the coarse measure factorize across the block, in 1D and, in D dimensions, when capture by a hyperplane of blocks amounts to capture by each block; barring exact cancellation of existing couplings, the renormalized Hamiltonian then gains no range, and in 1D product disorder gains no correlations across the block. The coarse-grainings actually optimized fall short of that condition, and for them the link is computed only for two-spin blocks of 1D Ising chains *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-202](../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md): In variational renormalization over general Boltzmann machines, neither a matched partition function nor Kadanoff's exact trace condition makes a coarse-graining a renormalization: the first holds for joint Hamiltonians whose marginal is not the data, the second for hidden variables that do not interact with the system, so the variables a renormalization keeps must be fixed by a further stated condition *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-205](../record/theory.d/THEORY-205.md): For a short-range lattice model on a cylinder with a symmetric transfer matrix whose leading excited eigenvalue is non-degenerate, with block and environment as slabs L_B transfer steps apart, the uninformative information-bottleneck encoder first loses stability at β = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B), in the direction of the boundary weak value of the leading excited eigenvector, which by the cited conformal finite-size relation is the lowest-dimension primary at large circumference; the uninformative encoder can stop being optimal at a smaller β, and nothing is shown for blocks inside a buffer shell or for the fixed-alphabet RSMI optimum *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-214](../record/theory.d/THEORY-214.md): On the 2022 r/place canvas, the abrupt overthrow of a crowd-built image from a stable period is predicted up to hours ahead, on held-out images and on the 2023 edition, by a combination of many image-level series far better than by any generic slowing-down indicator; the series the predictor relies on include low past restoring of attacked pixels as well as attack outrunning restoration, and about a quarter of overthrows give no warning at the 20-minute range *(used by 9)*
- [THEORY-215](../record/theory.d/THEORY-215.md): A Hawkes process with a Lipschitz rate function and signed kernels has a unique stationary regime, which suitably started versions approach, when the Lipschitz-weighted absolute kernel mass is below one (a spectral radius below one, for a network) or when the rate is bounded *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-216](../record/theory.d/THEORY-216.md): On the 2017 r/place log, with coalitions recovered from co-placement, which coalitions survive is barely predictable early from their size, area, start time and colour entropy, the size distribution of recovered coalitions shifts toward large ones as the event proceeds, and some lasting artworks were held by coalitions that kept working under sustained overwriting *(used by 6)*
- [THEORY-218](../record/theory.d/THEORY-218.md): In one case study of the 2017 r/place Mona Lisa, what was added to or removed from the image was, once its forum opened, decided off the canvas, in a forum of 161 accounts negotiating through linked design images, where a few central members admitted or refused additions, and the forum's changes then appeared in a region where about 77,000 accounts placed tiles, most of whom never posted; how many placers followed the designs is not measured, and the authors argue that the placement record alone cannot show who directed the image or who cooperated *(used by 6)*
- [THEORY-222](../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md): With uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a coarse-grained macro description of a known discrete mechanism can have more effective information than the micro description it supervenes on, so the level at which effective information is highest can be a macro level *(used by 6; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-239](../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md): For any joint law of an input and a context, symmetric or not, the top-d left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator attain the minimum, over d-dimensional spans, of worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1 − ε, namely (s₁² − (1 − ε)²)/(s₁² − s²_{d+1}) when s_{d+1} < 1 − ε ≤ s₁, though other spans can tie *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-242](../record/theory.d/THEORY-242.md): A spiral of silence can make a small, fixed minority opinion look far more widespread than it is without any member changing belief, and in the model that shows it the network's direct distortion of what members see is small *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-259](../record/theory.d/THEORY-259.md): For a recursive family of likelihoods and the universal prior, the Bayesian two-part code length −log Pr(D|H) − log m(H) equals the ideal-MDL length K(D|H) + K(H) plus the randomness deficiency of D for H, up to a constant fixed by the family; so ideal MDL and MAP selection agree to within a constant among hypotheses for which the data are random, and can part where they are not *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-265](../record/theory.d/THEORY-265.md): In Tissot et al.'s minimal model of bistable deciders in a modular coordination game (thirty modules of ten, couplings 1 within modules and 0.01 across), phase synchronisation within modules, driven only by each unit's local payoff, makes each module respond to the others as a single unit, and synchrony matched to the modules is needed: global synchrony does not *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-267](../record/theory.d/THEORY-267.md): In Rasooly and Rozzi's pre-registered randomised experiment on 817 Manifold play-money markets, about 59% of a ±5-point price shock that no trader's information supported was still present after 60 days in unresolved markets, with about 25% undone in the first week and reversion slowing after it; their model of finitely many risk-averse traders gives such partial, slowing reversion even with no learning, and the data cannot tell that from learning *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-275](../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md): In two optically trapped beads with a symmetric hydrodynamic coupling, one trap moved by a recorded noise drive, time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy follow the drive's path rather than the coupling's symmetry: the flow between the beads reads two-way under moderate drive, in experiment and numerics, and one-way under strong drive, in numerics of the fitted model only *(used by 5)*
- [THEORY-276](../record/theory.d/THEORY-276.md): In a network of identical units with identical couplings, the orbits of the graph's symmetry group are synchronization clusters, and a cluster moved only by its own factor of the group can lose synchrony while the others keep it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-285](../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md): In an illustrative active-inference simulation of post-traumatic context inference, run once per phenotype, a prior that one is in a harmful context, made overly precise by a run of harmful trials under the "vulnerable" learning and forgetting weights, makes exploratory sampling look uninformative, so the agent attenuates the periphery, never receives the evidence that would correct the prior, and the belief sustains itself; lowering precision makes the attenuation policy less vigorous without correcting the prior, and the policy returns when precision is restored *(used by 5; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-290](../record/theory.d/THEORY-290.md): In a two-debater, three-proposition model of deductive debate whose payoff trades true beliefs against changes of mind, the most truth-conducive equilibrium can fall short of the truth-optimal profile because one debater free-rides on the other's belief-disrupting arguments, and in a narrow band of mixed equilibria a higher weight on truth gives lower equilibrium accuracy *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-295](../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md): In a community whose consensus model is replaced whenever a single sound pairwise model comparison favours the challenger, which models get proposed can hold the consensus on a false model while results reproduce almost perfectly, so reproducibility need not track convergence to truth *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-299](../record/theory.d/THEORY-299.md): Structured and translational knowledge-graph embeddings are 0-cochains of a cellular sheaf of vector spaces pulled back from the schema, each triple scored by a norm of the coboundary on its edge and, in the squared-Euclidean form, the whole graph by the sheaf Laplacian; since the zero cochain is always a global section, what they learn is a contrastive margin, not the existence of a section *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-318](../record/theory.d/THEORY-318.md): A bound k on the max-information between a dataset and an analyst's chosen statistic multiplies by at most 2^k the probability that the statistic overfits that dataset, and an ε-differentially private mechanism on datasets of n points keeps k at most log₂e·εn, whatever the distribution on datasets *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-321](../record/theory.d/THEORY-321.md): Under repeated DeGroot averaging in a strongly connected society, the consensus converges to the truth as the society grows if and only if the largest influence weight vanishes, so network structure alone, not the members' common updating rule, decides whether the group belief is right *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-324](../record/theory.d/THEORY-324.md): A system adapts by trial and error to an environment whose effect on its essential variables it does not know only if a second feedback, through those variables, changes the parameters of its primary feedback; and if that feedback changes them whenever, and for as long as, an essential variable is outside its limits, every equilibrium the whole can reach is an adapted one *(used by 4; also organizational-affect)*
- [THEORY-327](../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md): Fricker, in her 2003 paper and her 2017 retrospective, holds that testimonial injustice is an ingenuous misjudgement of a speaker's credibility caused by prejudice, and that deliberate manipulation of credibility is a related but distinct wrong; and she accepts Anderson's structural form, which is pre-emptive: a speaker's word is never sought because of a structural prejudice, such as an un-refreshed list, that is no one's fault *(used by 4; also record-as-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-332](../record/theory.d/THEORY-332.md): For one index with no space limit, Bruno and Chaudhuri's online tuner, which builds the index once the savings it would have given have risen by its build cost above their last low and drops it once they have fallen by the build cost below their last high, is not three-competitive: when every statement's saving or loss is at most a fraction f of the build cost, a repeated workload makes it cost nearly 3 + 2f times the offline optimum, and one statement whose saving exceeds the build cost makes the ratio unbounded; no upper bound is shown *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-333](../record/theory.d/THEORY-333.md): Database cracking, which partitions a copy of a column in place as a side effect of each range query, measured in memory on 10^7 integers under uniformly random ranges, costs about 40% more than a scan on the first query and far less than sorting, gets cheaper per query with use, and stays cumulatively cheaper than sort-then-search until about 10^5 queries; that only the queried ranges get organized is not tested *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-334](../record/theory.d/THEORY-334.md): In copying a pattern of coloured blocks that stays in view, seven subjects told to work quickly looked back at the model about 1.3 times per block, and their commonest cycle, which looks at the model both before picking up a block and before dropping it, was the slowest per block in the authors' observed tallies (about 3 s, against 1.5 s for a cycle that copies from memory); looks fell to 1.0 per block with model and copy 70° apart and to 0.7 with one-colour patterns that could be chunked, and in three subjects a colour change made during a saccade raised fixation time by about 129 ms after pickup against about 50 ms before; no statistics are reported *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-338](../record/theory.d/THEORY-338.md): For a list searched from the front, where reaching the i-th item costs i, moving each found item to the front costs at most twice what any rule costs on the same sequence, including rules that know the future (four times counting its own moves), a fixed order by access frequency is within no constant factor, and paying to rearrange ahead of need never helps; for paging, no online rule beats the offline optimum by less than n/(n − n_MIN + 1), and LRU meets that bound *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-340](../record/theory.d/THEORY-340.md): For answering membership in a static set of n keys with the fewest worst-case cell reads, sorted order with binary search is optimal only when the key universe exceeds a Ramsey-number threshold and table cells may hold nothing but stored keys or pointer symbols; it is beaten for small universes, and by two probes once one cell may hold an encoded value *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-341](../record/theory.d/THEORY-341.md): Inferring not-P from failure to prove P is a deduction only under two separate conditions: Clark shows that when every branch of the search for a proof of P ends in failure, not-P is a theorem of the completed database, and a search that does not finish licenses nothing; Reiter's closed-world assumption, adding the negation of every ground atom the database does not entail, keeps a consistent Horn database consistent and can make a disjunctive one inconsistent *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-342](../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md): In AlphaZero on 9×9 Hex, at fixed playing strength, training compute and tree-search compute substitute along a straight line in log–log space, about 15× less search for each 10× more training over about two decades of training compute, down to a one-node search; the trade is measured for one search and counts no games played *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-344](../record/theory.d/THEORY-344.md): An access method's read, update and memory overheads, each a ratio to the base data alone with a floor of 1.0, are conjectured to trade so that bounding any two forces a lower bound on the third; the conjecture is unproved, its formal wording says no more than the floor already does, and the paper's extreme designs show conflicts between pairs, read against memory and update against read, not a symmetric three-way trade *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-345](../record/theory.d/THEORY-345.md): Choosing indexes for a known mix of queries and updates, to minimize query cost plus a per-index upkeep, is NP-hard as the number of attributes and query types grows, and the tools built for it choose one stored order and a set of secondary indexes per table by searching configurations costed with the query optimizer's own estimates, optimal at best relative to those estimates, with no proved guarantee for their heuristics and no term for the one-time cost of building *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-346](../record/theory.d/THEORY-346.md): When information stays in view at a known place, people consult it less and rely on memory more as the time to reach it rises, in a graded trend across added delays from 0 to 3.2 seconds, even where the memory is weak and the display perfect; in one copying task a model that prices memory and display access in time alone, with no preference for either source, fits how many items people encode per look *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-348](../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md): When staying in one state costs a fixed amount per request and leaving it costs a fixed one-time price, switching once the extra cost paid for staying equals that price is within 2 of the offline optimum on every request sequence, and no deterministic online rule does better; with a third option the best guaranteed ratio rises to 3 *(used by 2; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-349](../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md): For binary outcomes and a fixed representation of individuals, a predictor can pass every test in a bounded class without being close to nature: outcome indistinguishability to tests that see the sampled prediction is equivalent, with stated losses, to multicalibration over a closely related class of sets, a predictor meeting it exists at size polynomial in the tests' size and the tolerance whatever nature's complexity, and learning one is as hard as weak agnostic learning of the class *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-350](../record/theory.d/THEORY-350.md): Under a budget on maintenance time, a stored view's upkeep depends on which other views are stored, so upkeep is not additive and adding a view can lower it, and greedily adding the single view of best saving per unit of upkeep can be arbitrarily bad; on OR view graphs a greedy over inverted tree sets gets 1 − 1/e of the saving of an optimum given as much upkeep, using up to twice the budget, if no tree-piece of the optimum alone exceeds the budget *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-354](../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md): An observer's power to refute a predictor depends on its access to the predictor as well as on its budget: against tests that see only the sampled prediction a predictor of size O(s/ε²) always passes, but if fine-grained clique counting is hard, or BPP ≠ PSPACE, some cheap tests that may query the predictor adaptively pass only predictors about as costly as nature's own *(used by 3; also realizability, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-356](../record/theory.d/THEORY-356.md): When stored views are never updated, greedily storing the view of largest marginal saving in query cost gets at least 1 − 1/e of the optimal saving on a data-cube lattice or any OR or AND view graph, against the optimum for the same number of views or for the space the greedy ends up using, which may exceed the budget by one view *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-360](../record/theory.d/THEORY-360.md): In Kirsh and Maglio's Tetris keystroke data, rotation began in earnest by 400 to 600 ms after a piece appeared, sometimes before it was fully in view, and at each of three skill levels drops preceded by a move to the wall and back were longer than ordinary drops, about 19 to 20 squares against 13 to 16 *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-363](../record/theory.d/THEORY-363.md): For finding the top k objects under a monotone combining function from m lists each sorted by one attribute, with sorted and random accesses the only costs, the threshold algorithm is correct and on every database costs at most a constant times what any correct algorithm that makes no wild guesses costs; the constant is m + m(m−1)c_R/c_S, no deterministic algorithm does better when the function is strict, and once wild guesses are allowed no algorithm has such a guarantee on databases with ties *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-364](../record/theory.d/THEORY-364.md): When each cached value is an interval its source guarantees to contain the current value, and a query must return an answer interval no wider than R whatever the true values, choosing the cheapest set of exact reads for a SUM is a 0/1 knapsack problem, NP-complete in general and solved by taking the narrowest intervals first when read costs are equal, and for a COUNT with a selection predicate the cheapest choice is the ⌈|T?| − R⌉ cheapest undecided tuples *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-365](../record/theory.d/THEORY-365.md): In one study of a stack of proximity graphs on nested random subsets of the data, each element's top layer drawn geometrically, greedy search on uniform random data in 8 dimensions needed a number of distance computations that grew no worse than logarithmically with the number of items and stayed below a single-layer navigable graph's at every size tested, and in 4 dimensions the beam width needed for a fixed recall saturated; the logarithmic bound is derived only for exact Delaunay graphs of bounded degree, which the index does not build, and on 200 million SIFT vectors the measured growth departs from it *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-366](../record/theory.d/THEORY-366.md): With a fixed number of data points and a query drawn independently of them, if the variance of the p-th power of the query-to-point distance divided by its mean tends to zero, the farthest point comes within any factor 1 + ε of the nearest with probability tending to one; independent coordinates meet this condition, while data on a low-dimensional subspace, or queries that fall inside well-separated clusters, escape it *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-368](../record/theory.d/THEORY-368.md): On two-dimensional point sets constructed for the purpose, the authors' code for fast-preprocessing DiskANN, HNSW and NSG, at parameters from the original papers, in most cases found none or few of a query's five nearest neighbours until the search queue held about 10% of the points, for n from 10⁵ to 2·10⁶, and at that queue length ten graph indexes averaged recall@5 between 0.0 and 0.42; this is shown by experiment on one query per instance, and no theorem bounds these algorithms *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-369](../record/theory.d/THEORY-369.md): Under uniformly distributed, independent data and queries in the unit cube with Euclidean distance and a fixed number of points, an optimal nearest-neighbour search over any index that partitions points into blocks or convex clusters of at least two points must read a fraction of blocks that grows toward all of them as dimension rises; with a five-fold sequential advantage for scanning, estimates put the crossover at about 15–26 dimensions for rectangular and spherical bounding regions, and two tree indexes measured on 50,000 points lost to a scan beyond about 10 *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-372](../record/theory.d/THEORY-372.md): For c-approximate near-neighbour search over n points in Euclidean space, space n^{1+ρu+o(1)} and query time n^{ρq+o(1)} are achievable on any data set whenever c²√ρq + (c²−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c²−1) (c√ρq + (c−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c−1) in Hamming space), and no list-of-points structure, the model of known data-independent hashing, does better on random instances; without that model the curve is matched only at query time n^{o(1)} by one or two cell probes *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-374](../record/theory.d/THEORY-374.md): Given views with conjunctive definitions, deciding that they answer a conjunctive query exactly is NP-complete in the size of the query and definitions, while a maximally-contained rewriting can be built in time polynomial in that size without saying whether it is exact; and finding all certain answers from the stored contents is polynomial in their size under the open-world assumption when the views are conjunctive and the query conjunctive or datalog, but co-NP-hard in that size under the closed-world assumption even for conjunctive views and queries *(used by 3; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-375](../record/theory.d/THEORY-375.md): In one simulator evicting whole query-shaped cache regions, no replacement value function was best on every workload: a value based on distance from the current query beat LRU where queries clustered around a hot region or wandered with loops, while MRU was best on regular cyclic paths, by up to 2.3 times over the distance value and 9.6 times over LRU; none of the functions weighs what a region would cost to fetch again, and nothing is proved *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-377](../record/theory.d/THEORY-377.md): In Olston, Loo and Widom's simulations, a rule that multiplies a cached interval's width by 1 + α on a pushed refresh with probability min{ρ, 1}, and divides it by 1 + α on a query's exact fetch with probability min{1/ρ, 1}, settled within 1% of the best fixed width on one random walk and within 5% over eight walk settings; on a 50-host network-traffic trace, restricted to exact copies, it almost matched a tuned adaptive cache-or-not rule, and with a 50-value cache, where queries tolerated imprecision, it cost less; that it converges to the best width is argued, not proved *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-378](../record/theory.d/THEORY-378.md): When items change as independent Poisson processes with known rates and a fixed total refresh rate is shared among them, refreshing every item equally keeps the copy at least as fresh and at most as old, averaged over time, as refreshing in proportion to change rate, for any spread of rates; the freshness-optimal share rises and then falls with change rate and gives nothing to items that change too fast for the budget *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-379](../record/theory.d/THEORY-379.md): Fagin's Algorithm finds the top k of N objects held in m attribute-sorted lists under any monotone combining function, and when the lists' orderings are independent with at least m − 1 of them uniformly random it does so with O(N^((m−1)/m) k^(1/m)) sorted and random accesses with arbitrarily high probability; with dependent orderings the bound can fail *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-381](../record/theory.d/THEORY-381.md): In the cell-probe model, a near-neighbour structure on n random points that answers in t probes with m cells of w bits must satisfy m^t·w/n ≥ the robust expansion of the metric's neighbourhood graph at measure 1/m^t (and (mwt/n)^t ≥ its vertex expansion if deterministic), so in expanding spaces such as the hypercube fast queries need space polynomially larger than the data; the bounds are average case, approximate, and fall off exponentially in t *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-382](../record/theory.d/THEORY-382.md): When a web server keeps each page fragment either cached and invalidated by updates or stored and refreshed after them, materializing trades staleness for response time, and in one synthetic simulation with fixed costs a periodic greedy that moves a capped number of fragments between the two, to keep the share of fresh fragments served above a set threshold, tracked that threshold by the authors' reading of its curves, answered faster than caching alone and recovered from overload by materializing everything; no bound on its distance from the best plan is shown *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-383](../record/theory.d/THEORY-383.md): On one Apache and Informix server answering cheap indexed selections over 1000 pages, a page whose query result was stored in the DBMS and refreshed on every update answered more slowly than one recomputed on each request at five or more updates per second, which the authors explain by reading the stored result costing about as much as recomputing it and its refresh loading the same DBMS, while a finished page stored at the web server and rewritten on every update answered 10 to 230 times faster than either *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-385](../record/theory.d/THEORY-385.md): In HNSW over 10-dimensional data in 100 isolated clusters, linking each new item to its nearest neighbours leaves part of the bottom layer unreachable from the entry point and caps recall well short of 1 however wide the query search, while linking a candidate only when it is nearer the new item than to any neighbour already kept keeps that layer connected and reaches recall near 1 with about half the links; on uniform data at 10 and 64 dimensions the two rules differ little; shown in Malkov and Yashunin's own tests on 10 million points and in an independent re-run on 30,000, which found the nearest-neighbour rule capped at a recall@10 of 0.72 to 0.83 against 0.999, at matched build cost too *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-386](../record/theory.d/THEORY-386.md): When a cached interval of width W is kept valid by its source, which pushes a refresh at cost C_vr whenever the value leaves it, and queries fetch the exact value at cost C_qr whenever it is too wide, and the chances of the two per step go as 1/W² and as W, the expected refresh cost is least at W* = (ρK₁/K₂)^(1/3) with ρ = 2C_vr/C_qr, where ρ times the chance of a pushed refresh equals the chance of a fetch *(used by 2; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-389](../record/theory.d/THEORY-389.md): For conjunctive queries and views without comparison predicates, a stored view can be used in an equivalent rewriting of a query exactly when the view's body maps homomorphically into the query's, a minimal rewriting needs no more literals than the query, and deciding whether a rewriting shorter than the query or one using only the views exists is NP-complete in the size of the query and view definitions; with comparisons in both, deciding whether any rewriting uses the views is Π2p-complete *(used by 3; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-404](../record/theory.d/THEORY-404.md): With a common prior, a sender who commits to a signal the receiver observes can induce any distribution of posteriors whose mean is the prior, so an openly designed experiment moves a fully informed Bayesian receiver whenever the concave closure of the sender's value lies above its value at the prior; at the optimum, under the paper's tie-breaking, the receiver is certain when she takes the sender's worst action and indifferent when she takes another *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-408](../record/theory.d/THEORY-408.md): In a one-locus model with non-overlapping generations, random mating and weak selection, gene frequencies change as if each individual maximized its inclusive fitness, so a trait that costs its bearer spreads only if its effect on relatives exceeds 1/r times the cost; the increase of mean inclusive fitness is proved only for traits whose total effect on others is not negative *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-419](../record/theory.d/THEORY-419.md): In a structural causal model of autonomous equations, with intervention do(X = x) defined, as Pearl defines it, as a surgery that deletes X's own equation, sets X to x and solves the rest, and with observing X = x violating no equation and amounting to ordinary conditioning, models that agree on every observational distribution can disagree on the effect of an intervention, and in a structural equation y = βx + ε the coefficient β is the rate of change of E[Y | do(x)], which equals the regression slope of Y on X only when X is uncorrelated with ε *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-424](../record/theory.d/THEORY-424.md): Mutual-information measures of individuality that read a system's next state off its present one measure association, not propagation: I(S_{t+1}; S_t) can be positive when the environment alone drives the system, and conditioning on the environment does not recover the interventional quantity, which can be zero where the conditional measure is one bit *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-431](../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md): For classical systems with Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production of a trajectory obeys an exact finite-time symmetry against the time-reversed process, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^ω, wherever ω is odd under reversal; Jarzynski's work equality and the mean second law follow as corollaries, and the symmetry constrains fluctuations, not which steady state a system selects *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-466](../record/theory.d/THEORY-466.md): Among contestants of equal prowess with dangerous weapons, individual selection can favour conventional fighting backed by retaliation: an escalating Hawk is not evolutionarily stable, Retaliator is at most neutrally stable because Mouse ties it, and in a contest settled by persistence alone no fixed persistence is stable while an exponential mixture is *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-480](../record/theory.d/THEORY-480.md): Where a general-search monopoly was kept by exclusive distribution deals, the court in United States v. Google treated the user-interaction data that scale produced as a fruit of the violation and ordered the raw data and index metadata shared with qualified competitors, but not the engineered signals and models built from them, as a behavioural remedy while rejecting divestiture; that the sharing will let rivals compete is the court's expectation, not a finding *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-527](../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md): If agents are the systems that would adapt their policy were their actions to affect the world differently, then in mechanised causal games meeting Kenton et al.'s five assumptions (one agent per connected component of the decision–utility graph, best response to every mechanism intervention, a fixed tie-breaking order, terminal edges only into decision mechanisms, and mechanism interventions able to set any deterministic function) the game graph, with its decisions, utilities and agents, is recovered exactly from interventions on mechanisms *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-543](../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md): Diffusion can destabilise a homogeneous steady state of reacting chemicals that is stable without it: a disturbance of one finite wave-length grows while uniform and very short ones decay, so a stationary pattern appears whose spacing is set by the reaction and diffusion constants and only its phase by the disturbance; with two substances this needs them to diffuse at different rates, and the pattern lasts only while free energy is supplied *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-567](../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md): In the donation game, where a cooperator pays c for another to get b, defectors win in a well-mixed population, and each of five mechanisms makes cooperators evolutionarily stable above a benefit-to-cost threshold: kin selection r > c/b, direct reciprocity w > c/b, indirect reciprocity q > c/b, network reciprocity b/c > k and group selection b/c > 1 + n/m; the rules cover altruism only, not mutualism, coordination or conflict *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-582](../record/theory.d/THEORY-582.md): Causal coupling between a process and something outside it does not by itself make that thing part of the process, so an argument from coupling to extended cognition needs a further premise saying what makes a process cognitive *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-598](../record/theory.d/THEORY-598.md): Group interactions that enter a dynamical model linearly, as in diffusion on simplices or random walks on hypergraphs with edge-independent vertex weights, reduce to pairwise dynamics on a reweighted graph; the abrupt transitions, bistability and stabilised coexistence reported for higher-order systems come from group terms that enter nonlinearly, and whether the representation is a hypergraph or a simplicial complex is itself a modelling claim that changes the outcome *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-603](../record/theory.d/THEORY-603.md): In the Iowa gambling task, every one of ten controls and none of six patients with bilateral ventromedial prefrontal damage developed anticipatory skin-conductance responses, and three patients who could state the right strategy still did not switch to the good decks; the controls' preference for the good decks became significant only once they reported a hunch, so the study does not show advantageous choice or deck-specific bodily signals before any awareness *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-624](../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md): Orseau, McGill and Legg cast whether an identified system is an agent or a device as Bayesian model comparison between descriptions of the function it optimises and descriptions of its input-output mapping, so that the verdict is relative to the observer's prior; on seven toy gridworld trajectories goal-seeking comes out agent-like and wall-following device-like, and they argue that under a speed prior everything may look like an agent *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-659](../record/theory.d/THEORY-659.md): In the EEAS's 2024 sample of 505 foreign information manipulation incidents, the overt state voice is a small core: of the 2,055 channels that recur across incidents, 20% are attributed to Russia, 3.5% to China and 76.5% are not attributed, after some 28,000 disposable inauthentic accounts are set aside; the sample is not representative, and the four-tier Exposure Matrix used to grade channels' ties to a state is unvalidated *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-661](../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md): In a nearly decomposable system, where interactions within subsystems are much stronger than interactions between them, each subsystem's short-run behaviour is approximately independent of the others', and in the long run each depends on the others only through their aggregate behaviour; so a hierarchy defined by intensity of interaction separates fast dynamics inside its parts from slow, aggregate dynamics between them *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-672](../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md): In the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with a probability w of meeting again, no strategy does better against an established TIT FOR TAT than TIT FOR TAT does against itself if and only if w ≥ (T−R)/(T−P) and w ≥ (T−R)/(R−S); always defecting is stable for every w, a cluster of reciprocators can invade it, and a nice stable strategy resists clusters, but the stability is only neutral, since always cooperating ties *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-679](../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md): For dynamics obeying detailed balance in a heat bath, the heat released in a transition between observer-defined macrostates is bounded below by the log-odds against its reversal less the internal entropy change; where a replicator's likeliest way back is a copy decaying within one generation, the bound grows with the copy's durability and the speed of copying, not with the information copied *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-689](../record/theory.d/THEORY-689.md): A mobile robot built from parallel layers of simple finite-state machines, each linking sensing to action by itself and combined only by one layer suppressing or inhibiting another's signals, avoids obstacles, wanders and heads for distant places with no central world model, goal list or controller; shown at insect scale, on three layers of one physical robot *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-692](../record/theory.d/THEORY-692.md): Near equilibrium, steady states minimise entropy production and every fluctuation decays; far from it, the excess entropy production has no fixed sign, so a fluctuation can grow past an instability of the thermodynamic branch into a structure held up only by flows across the boundary, and thermodynamics supplies only a sufficient condition for such a state's stability, not a principle selecting which structure appears *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-700](../record/theory.d/THEORY-700.md): For jointly Gaussian stationary processes, Granger causality in Geweke's generalized-variance form is exactly twice the transfer entropy, conditional and multivariate, at the regressions' lags, because least-squares residual covariance is the partial covariance and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is half its log-determinant plus a constant *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-724](../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md): For a linear system du/dt = A(t)u, non-normality is necessary for time dependence to destabilize an operator that is uniformly stable at every instant, and a non-normal operator neutral at every instant can be asymptotically unstable under switching *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-725](../record/theory.d/THEORY-725.md): On the court agenda {P, Q, R, R iff (P and Q)} under universal domain, proposition-wise majority voting is not robustly rational, while the premise-based procedure is, and it makes the group's judgments a function of the members' whole judgment sets that the members' judgments on the conclusion neither fix nor need to enter *(used by 4; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-727](../record/theory.d/THEORY-727.md): For a fixed linear operator in an inner-product norm, growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound only from below; it starts at the numerical abscissa, which can be positive when every mode decays; and the forced response is bounded by the condition number of the eigenvectors over the distance to the spectrum *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-733](../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md): For a stable linear Gaussian VAR(p), a linear coarse-graining is exactly dynamically independent iff its row space is invariant under the transpose of every lag matrix, so for p ≥ 2 almost no parameter set has one at any scale, while for p = 1 they are the transpose's invariant subspaces, which exist on open sets but not generically at every scale *(used by 10; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-746](../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md): Over a fixed finite set of basis functions, slow feature analysis is a generalized eigenproblem: the outputs that minimize ⟨ẏ²⟩ under zero mean, unit variance and decorrelation are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the derivative covariance against the covariance, in order of slowness, and a stack of such stages, each of whose function spaces contains its inputs, can only keep or lower each of its first m slowness values on the training signal, and may keep them *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-748](../record/theory.d/THEORY-748.md): Block entropies, and so every lag-τ entropy rate of a stationary signal, are unchanged by the reflection x → −x and by time reversal, so they cannot detect the odd-order asymmetry the 4/5 law ties to energy flux; Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier's entropy rate conditioned on the sign of the increment breaks the reflection invariance, but h⁺ ≠ h⁻ shows only that the two-point distribution lacks central symmetry, which a skewed one-point distribution produces with exactly symmetric increments, so the test does not by itself detect skewed increments or an energy cascade *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-749](../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md): A weak solution of the incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box that lies in L³(0,T; B^α_{3,∞}) ∩ C([0,T]; L²) with α > 1/3 conserves kinetic energy, because the energy flux into scales below a mollification scale ε is bounded by Cε^(3α−1)∫‖u‖³ and so vanishes as ε → 0; this does not show that rougher solutions dissipate *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-750](../record/theory.d/THEORY-750.md): For a stationary Gaussian signal the lag-τ entropy rate with one-point embedding is h_τ = H(X) + ½ log(1 − c(τ)²), so where the normalized second-order structure function 1 − c(τ) is small and scales as τ^ζ₂, h_τ = (ζ₂/2) log τ + constant; the "scaling of information" that Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier measure in near-Gaussian wind-tunnel turbulence, slope 1/3 in the inertial range and 1 in the dissipative range, is the scaling of the second-order structure function written in nats *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-752](../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md): In optimal prediction of a Hamiltonian system with separable energy and canonical initial law, projected by conditional expectation, the t-model's leading-order memory term tPLQLx makes the effective Hamiltonian of the resolved variables non-increasing, so the eliminated variables' memory enters as a damping that grows linearly in time *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-754](../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md): If a velocity field's third-order increments obey ‖δu(r)‖₃ ≤ C u_rms (r/L)^σ at every separation r, with 0 < σ < 1, then for a smooth, rapidly decaying filter the space-averaged energy flux across scale ℓ takes at most a fraction of order (ℓ/Δ)^(1−σ) from strain at scales above Δ and of order (δ/ℓ)^(2σ) from stress at scales below δ, measured against u_rms³/L·(ℓ/L)^(3σ−1); so transfer between scales is local in scale, with a power-law decay and no gap *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-755](../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md): For a linear system x(t+1) = Ax and a partition of its variables, the vector of block sums evolves autonomously from every initial state iff the partition is column-equitable, every column of each block of A summing to the same value; the aggregate operator then keeps a subset of A's eigenvalues, and the blocks may interact as strongly as they like, so exact aggregation is not decomposition *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-756](../record/theory.d/THEORY-756.md): The growth rate of thermodynamic depth is the entropy rate of whichever macrostate process it is computed over, so the choice of macrostates sets it anywhere from zero up; among partitions of a stationary process's past that predict every finite stretch of the future as well as the whole past does, the causal states are the coarsest, so they have the least entropy and the least entropy rate *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-758](../record/theory.d/THEORY-758.md): For a self-adjoint diffusion operator T with spectrum in [0, 1], the diffusion-wavelet levels are spectral subspaces spanned by the eigenvectors with λ^s ≥ ε for an increasing sequence of powers s, so they form an exactly nested chain of T-invariant subspaces whose differences are bands of the spectrum, about one octave each, not spatial blocks; Coifman and Maggioni's compressed algorithm, which squares the operator on each orthonormal basis, thresholds T^{2^{j−1}} at level j and not T^{2^j−1} as the paper states; and since each level is T-invariant, each is an exactly closed linear coarse-graining whose localized basis is a choice the level does not fix *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-760](../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md): The finite-memory Mori–Zwanzig closure that Parish and Duraisamy take from Stinis, truncated at order m with one trapezoidal sub-interval and constant memory lengths, is a finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation: m + 1 auxiliary variables per resolved mode, each relaxing at rate 2/τ; at first order it replaces the memory integral by the kernel 2e^{−2s/τ₀} acting on the first-order term, which tends to τ₀ times that term, the t-model with t replaced by τ₀, when τ₀ is short against the resolved dynamics; its kernel is twice the true one at zero lag for every τ₀, so it is not exact even where the true memory is a single exponential, and nothing in the construction bounds its error *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-762](../record/theory.d/THEORY-762.md): For a reversible diffusion dX = −∇U dt + √2 dW in equilibrium, an eigenfunction ψ of its generator with eigenvalue −λ is closed in conditional mean with no memory: E[ψ(X_{t+s}) | the whole past] = e^{−λs}ψ(X_t), and so the same given ψ's own past; but ψ(X_t) is a Markov process in its own right only when |∇ψ|² is a function of ψ, since otherwise its own path reveals a noise intensity that its present value does not fix *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-764](../record/theory.d/THEORY-764.md): For a deterministic supervenient feature V of a Markov system, Rosas et al.'s practical emergence criterion Ψ equals the parts' whole-minus-sum information about V's next value minus V's one-step dynamical dependence I(V_t′; X_t | V_t), so dynamical independence raises Ψ but neither implies emergence nor is implied by it, and the paper's sufficient test for causal decoupling can pass a feature that is not dynamically independent *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-770](../record/theory.d/THEORY-770.md): In a closed population, any mapping of ancestors to descendants gives the Price equation: mean fitness times the change in mean character equals the covariance of fitness and character plus the fitness-weighted mean of the change in character, over any time interval and with no assumption beyond closure *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-771](../record/theory.d/THEORY-771.md): In a singularly perturbed system, fast states x̃ with dx̃/dt = f̃(x̃, y) + ε·δf and slow states y with dy/dt = ε·ḡ(y) + ε·δg, if f̃ is contracting in x̃ at rate β_f with x̃ = 0 an equilibrium for every y, ḡ is contracting at rate β_g, and |δf| ≤ d_f + α_f,x|x̃| + α_f,y|y|, |δg| ≤ d_g + α_g,x|x̃|, then for every ε below ε_c = β_f / [χ_f(α_f,x + χ_g α_f,y α_g,x / β_g)] the fast states stay within O(ε) of zero and, when d_g = 0, the slow states within O(ε) of the reduced trajectory, uniformly in time after a transient of order (1/β_f + 1/(εβ_g)) log(1/ε) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-773](../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md): In a singularly perturbed system ẋ = f(x, z, t), εż = g(x, z, ε), if g is contracting in z at rate λ_z for every x and ε, the reduced system ẋ = f(x, γ(x), t) on the slow manifold z = γ(x) is contracting at rate λ_x, f is α-Lipschitz in z, |∂γ/∂x · f| ≤ d and g is K-Lipschitz in ε, then for all t ≥ 0 the fast state is within χ_z e^{−λ_z t/ε}|z(0) − γ(x(0))| + εχ_z(d + K)/λ_z of the manifold and the slow state within χ_x|x(0) − x_γ(0)|e^{−λ_x t} + ε[C₁(e^{−λ_x t} − e^{−λ_z t/ε}) + C₂(1 − e^{−λ_x t})] of the reduced trajectory; partial contraction of f in x alone is not enough *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-818](../record/theory.d/THEORY-818.md): In two-scale Lorenz 96 without time-scale separation (ε = 0.5, K = 18, J = 20, F = 10), a discrete-time closure for each resolved variable that fits the one-step discrepancy of a fourth-order Runge–Kutta step as a NARMAX series, with one autoregressive lag, at most two lags of the resolved variable and at most one moving-average term, reproduces the mean, spread, distribution, autocorrelation and neighbour cross-correlation of x₁ (Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance 0.005) and, with observations every 0.05, extends the 20-member ensemble forecast lead time at anomaly correlation 0.6 from about 2 to about 4 time units over a polynomial-plus-AR(1) closure; the model structure was chosen by trial and error, differs between the two observation spacings, and carries no error bound *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-819](../record/theory.d/THEORY-819.md): For an invertible map with an invariant measure, projecting onto the closed span of the whole past of chosen functions of the resolved variables (a Wiener projection) turns the exact discrete Mori–Zwanzig equation into one with no memory term: the next resolved value is a causal linear filter of those past functions plus a residual orthogonal to all of them, so the memory is carried by the coarse variable's own history; a finite NARMAX form follows only by a rational approximation of the filter, uncontrolled in general but exact for a scalar coarse variable of a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-820](../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md): For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement *(used by 8; also formal-apparatus, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-822](../record/theory.d/THEORY-822.md): For a Markov chain and a partition of its states, strong lumpability, every state of a block sending the same probability into each block, is the column-equitability of the master-equation operator and makes the block label informationally closed; when the chain is irreducible, an informationally closed label that is itself Markov is strongly lumpable, with no aperiodicity needed; weak lumpability gives a Markov label that need not be closed; and the same holds on the causal-state chain of any stationary process *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-831](../record/theory.d/THEORY-831.md): For a system driven by a protocol fixed in advance, with microscopic reversibility and with forward and reverse processes started uniformly on their macrostates, the log-odds of two outcomes II and III reached from I equal the difference in their log state counts, plus the log-ratio of their reversal probabilities, plus the difference in minus the log mean of e^(−βQ) over the paths reaching each, where Q is the heat released; so when the first two terms are equal the likelier outcome is the one whose paths release more heat on average with less variation *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-833](../record/theory.d/THEORY-833.md): In a 2024 survey of a quota-matched online sample of 2,092 US adults and a convenience sample of 103 antitrust lawyers, the public weighed layoffs, worse product quality and more lobbying well above price reductions in judging whether a merger should be challenged, the consumer welfare standard's own objective, while support for replacing that standard was 42.6 points lower among the lawyers than among the public, against a partisan gap of 5.9 points *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-836](../record/theory.d/THEORY-836.md): Scored between Nicaragua's regime-owned outlets and its exiled or online opposition outlets, on the prevalence of topics relevant to the regime's legitimacy and on the tone of sentences mentioning Ortega, the three nominally independent national outlets with web output moved toward the regime pole in agenda over 2018–2022, Canal 14 most and Radio Corporación least, and Canal 14's tone score fell from about .8 to below .5 by early 2022 while Radio Corporación's stayed near 1 *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-837](../record/theory.d/THEORY-837.md): In Besley and Prat's model of an incumbent who can pay n identical outlets to suppress verifiable bad news, where one outlet's report informs every voter, each outlet's price for silence is what it would earn as the only one to break the story, so the media are captured exactly when n·τa < r; under capture voters, though fully rational and not deceived, learn nothing and never remove a bad incumbent *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-840](../record/theory.d/THEORY-840.md): When every log-likelihood a predictive family V can assign lies in [−B, B], the V-information estimated from N samples is within 4R_N(G_V) + 2B√(2 log(1/δ)/N) of the true V-information with probability at least 1 − 2δ, with R_N(G_V) the Rademacher complexity of the family's log-likelihoods; so usable information relative to a family of small complexity can be estimated in high dimension, and what is estimated is that family's information, not Shannon's *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-842](../record/theory.d/THEORY-842.md): Among 100 Chapel Hill voters not yet committed to a candidate in September–October 1968, the aggregate emphasis they gave the campaign's main issues correlated +.967 with the emphasis of the major news items, and +.979 with that of the minor items, in the nine media serving them; and voters leaning to a candidate agreed more with all the news than with news about their own side in 18 of 24 comparisons *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-844](../record/theory.d/THEORY-844.md): A designer who commits to how players are informed, and may condition on the state and on their prior information but cannot choose their actions, can bring about exactly the Bayes correlated equilibria, the joint distributions of states and actions in which no player told his recommended action wants to deviate, a polytope cut out by linear constraints; with one uninformed receiver who would lose 1 by investing in the bad state and gain x < 1 in the good, the most investment attainable is certain investment in the good state and investment with probability x in the bad *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-845](../record/theory.d/THEORY-845.md): In Weatherall, O'Connor and Bruner's network model a policy maker's credence depends on the evidence it has received only through the total excess of successes over failures of the new action, so a propagandist's effect is the excess of failures it adds; for the same pulls, running single-trial studies and publishing the failures adds at least as large an excess as any other division into studies, which is why biased production does best with the smallest studies *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-846](../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md): Information usable by a predictor restricted to a family V can be created by computing on the data, so the data-processing inequality fails for V-information: with Z the exclusive-or of two fair independent bits, linear and one-coordinate families extract nothing about Z from the pair and all of it from their exclusive-or; V-information computed from any function of the source is bounded by the source's Shannon information when the family's input-free predictions can match the marginal of the target, and can exceed it otherwise *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-850](../record/theory.d/THEORY-850.md): In Hungary, 1994–2016, state-owned firms' advertising, and not private firms', shifted sharply toward print and online outlets when they became connected to the governing right and away when the 2015 Orbán–Simicska fallout ended a connection, at all five such events studied; and the outlets' share of articles on corruption scandals moved the opposite way at the three events with content data *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-851](../record/theory.d/THEORY-851.md): In Argentina's four main national newspapers, April 1998 to December 2007, a newspaper's monthly front-page coverage of the federal government's corruption scandals was lower in months when it received more government advertising, within newspaper and month and within each newspaper-president pair (about 0.31 of a front page per standard deviation of advertising in the 2010 working paper); the association held for advertising placed through the presidency's agency and not for autonomous agencies, and not for scandals of non-political actors *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-855](../record/theory.d/THEORY-855.md): In Bala–Goyal network models of unbiased scientists testing a slightly better new action, a propagandist who forwards to Bayesian policy makers only those real results that favour the worse action can leave the policy makers near-certain of the false theory while the scientists converge on the true one; the effect weakens as the policy makers hear more scientists, as the better action's advantage grows and as each study gets larger *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-856](../record/theory.d/THEORY-856.md): In one laboratory study of a nine-period game between an infrastructure operator, two elected policymakers and three voters (59 groups), letting the first elected policymaker fix the price for all periods moved prices toward the efficient level when policymakers' payoffs were set equal to consumers', and moved them further above it when their payoffs were set equal to the operator's; under period-by-period regulation voters' pressure lowered the operator-aligned policymakers' prices without removing the gap *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-860](../record/theory.d/THEORY-860.md): In Szeidl and Szucs's model of two outlets competing for readers and advertisers, where state-owned advertisers reward only the connected outlet's slant, with weight δ, every equilibrium has the slant gap between the connected and the unconnected outlet equal to their owners' ideal-point gap plus a favor-exchange term (βδ/NT)·Σ over government advertisers of masⱼWⱼ, up to measurement noise; readers' preference for slant cancels from the gap, so equal observed gaps can come from different mixes of ideology and exchange *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-863](../record/theory.d/THEORY-863.md): In Arthur's model of two agent types arriving in random order, each adopting whichever of two technologies pays it more, with returns linear in previous adoptions, increasing returns make the adoption difference a random walk with absorbing barriers: one technology takes the whole market with probability one, A with probability Δ_R/(Δ_R + Δ_S) where Δ_R and Δ_S are the gaps at which each type switches, the winner need not be the better technology, and once it has locked in no small change in returns alters later choices; with diminishing returns the barriers reflect and the shares go predictably to one half *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-889](../record/theory.d/THEORY-889.md): In Acharya, Blackwell and Sen's analysis, white Southerners surveyed in 2006 to 2011 who live in counties where a larger share of the 1860 population was enslaved are, with state fixed effects and 1860 county controls, somewhat less Democratic, less supportive of affirmative action and more racially resentful, by about 0.09 to 0.13 standard deviations per standard deviation (about 20 points) of slave share, and in 1984 to 1998 survey data colder toward black Americans, by about 0.32; a cotton-suitability instrument gives larger estimates; the direct effect estimated with present black share held fixed is about as large; and in county presidential vote, which counts black voters until disenfranchisement, the difference appeared after Reconstruction rather than before the war *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-891](../record/theory.d/THEORY-891.md): In dyads of untrained dancers facing each other, shared music and visual contact each raised interpersonal movement synchrony, with no interaction detected, in different movement components: lateral and hand movements synchronized through seeing the partner, anteroposterior movements such as head bobs through the shared music, and vertical bounce through both; which factor drove a component's synchrony was classified from its spatial direction and not from the periodicity of the synchrony *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-894](../record/theory.d/THEORY-894.md): A flow of pairwise comparisons on a graph splits orthogonally and uniquely into a gradient part, the l2-best global ranking, and a cyclic part, which splits into curl (local) and harmonic (global) inconsistency; a finite game's flow of unilateral payoff differences has no curl part, so every finite game is uniquely a potential game plus a harmonic game plus a nonstrategic remainder, and potential games are exactly those with no harmonic part; the decomposition is cardinal *(used by 6; also formal-apparatus, organizational-affect)*
- [THEORY-896](../record/theory.d/THEORY-896.md): A finite game in strategic form has the finite improvement property, every path of strict unilateral improvements being finite, exactly when it has a generalized ordinal potential, a real function on strategy profiles that rises with every strict unilateral improvement; so in a finite game an ordering along which every improving move climbs exists exactly when there is no improvement cycle, and every sequence of improving moves ends at a pure equilibrium *(used by 5; also organizational-affect, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-898](../record/theory.d/THEORY-898.md): In Gangneung, South Korea, in 2022, people the authors observed by chance in beach-front cafés outwardly ignored routine retaliatory missile launches and military sites on the beach, while a missile malfunction at night under a news embargo was followed by tweets voicing fear of war with North Korea and blaming the government and military *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-899](../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md): In an infinite, well-mixed population whose members each sample the quality of their own type, imitation of success has the expected update of a single Cross Learning bandit agent (the Taylor replicator dynamic), and the weighted voter model, in which members broadcast their type in proportion to their sample and adopt the first type they perceive, has the expected update of Maynard-Cross Learning, π_a ← π_a + (r_k / v^π)(1[a = k] − π_a), the Maynard-Smith replicator dynamic; the population vector is the policy and no member learns *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-902](../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md): In Friedkin, Jia and Bullo's study of 30 four-person student groups discussing 15 choice dilemmas, a member's self-reported closure to influence on the next issue rose with their influence centrality on the previous issue, an effect constant along the sequence, and with their average centrality over all prior issues, an effect that grew along it; influence networks thinned and discussions shortened while the rate of consensus did not change. Closure and centrality both come from the members' own chip allocations, and prior closure is not controlled *(used by 2; also organizational-affect)*
- [THEORY-906](../record/theory.d/THEORY-906.md): In five formerly stable democracies selected because they later autocratized (South Korea, India, Hungary, Venezuela and Turkey), formal emergency powers, extraordinary powers functionally equivalent to them, and emergency rhetoric each contributed, on the authors' unsourced country accounts, to weakening democratic institutions *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-911](../record/theory.d/THEORY-911.md): Of 853 national states of emergency declared from 1949 to 2017, 115 were reported as unlawful in declaration, conduct or duration; 97 of those followed political turmoil and 14 natural disasters, democracies were less likely than autocracies to run one, and those so coded lasted 321 days on average against 115, a gap the coding of overlong emergencies as unlawful builds in part *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-924](../record/theory.d/THEORY-924.md): When Elo ratings generate a win-probability matrix they are the row means of its log-odds; some set of Elo ratings reproduces a win-probability matrix exactly when its log-odds have no cyclic component, batch Elo otherwise matches only the row sums, and adding a copy of one agent shifts the batch Elo ratings of the others *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-925](../record/theory.d/THEORY-925.md): In a cooperative stochastic game with decentralised actors and a centralised critic, a baseline for each agent that averages the critic's value over that agent's own alternative actions under its own policy, the other agents' actions held fixed, leaves the expected policy gradient unchanged, so each agent can be credited with the advantage of its actual action over that counterfactual average without a default action or an extra simulation; the counterfactual values come from the learned critic, not from the environment *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-926](../record/theory.d/THEORY-926.md): In a game where each player can transmit n bits before a win or a loss becomes unattainable, every antisymmetric pattern of wins and losses among ⌊2ⁿ⌋ strategies, a cycle through all of them included, is realized by some set of pure strategies *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-927](../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md): In a sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer trained without balancing losses, the gate came to give large weights to the same few experts, which the authors attribute to self-reinforcement, favoured experts being trained more and so selected more; in one 256-expert language model, the squared coefficient of variation of expert importance or load as an auxiliary loss reduced the peak-to-mean load from 17.8 to at most 1.47 and test perplexity from 39.8 to 35.6–35.7 *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-928](../record/theory.d/THEORY-928.md): Two softmax learners that update every action's reward memory each step with its average reward against the other's current play, the memories decaying at rate α, follow, in the limit of learning slow relative to play, coupled replicator equations plus a term α Σ x_j log(x_j / x_i) toward uniform play; in a two-player matrix game, without decay the dynamics preserve phase volume in log-ratio coordinates and are Hamiltonian when the game is zero-sum with an interior Nash equilibrium, and with decay the volume contracts at rate (N − 1)(α_X + α_Y) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-929](../record/theory.d/THEORY-929.md): A joint action-value that is a non-decreasing function of per-agent values, each conditioning only on its agent's own history, makes the profile of the agents' individually greedy actions a greedy joint action, which suffices for decentralised greedy execution and is strictly more expressive than a sum; it cannot represent a joint value in which an agent's best action depends on what the others do at the same step *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-932](../record/theory.d/THEORY-932.md): The replicator-plus-entropy model of Boltzmann Q-learning in two-player stateless games is, in the small-step limit, the expected dynamics of a learner that updates every action's value each step, and so of frequency-adjusted Q-learning wherever every action's probability is at least its adjustment parameter; it is not that of Q-learning, whose expected update carries an extra factor of each action's selection probability, so that its policy dynamics depend on the Q-values; in Kaisers and Tuyls's three 2×2 games at one temperature, compared by eye, Q-learning's trajectories departed from the model depending on initialization and the frequency-adjusted learner's followed it *(used by 3)*
