- [THEORY-933](../record/theory.d/THEORY-933.md): Individual-Global-Max, that the agents' individually greedy actions form a greedy joint action, is strictly weaker than additive or monotonic factorisation: every single-state matrix game with a unique optimum satisfies it, yet in 177 of 310 random three-by-three two-agent games value-decomposition and monotonic mixing failed to learn the optimal joint action that an IGM-only method found; a sufficient condition is that the sum of individual values, shifted by a state value, equals the joint value at the greedy profile and bounds it from above elsewhere *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-937](../record/theory.d/THEORY-937.md): When a mixture of experts is trained on the error of a single expert chosen stochastically by the gate, or on the negative log-likelihood of the mixture, the gradient raises the gate's logit for an expert that fits a case better than the gate-weighted average and lowers it for one that fits worse; on a four-class vowel task, mixtures of 4 or 8 linear experts learned in about half the epochs of backpropagation networks of roughly equal parameter count, at equal accuracy, and divided the task by class pair, leaving all but 2 or 3 experts with mixing proportions effectively zero *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-940](../record/theory.d/THEORY-940.md): In a finite symmetric zero-sum game, successive Nash clusters are weakly ordered by relative population performance, and a strategy that beats every member of a population containing a whole cluster lies in a strictly earlier cluster *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-942](../record/theory.d/THEORY-942.md): The α-Rank chain over pure strategy profiles, built from Fermi-imitation fixation probabilities in finite populations with rare mutation, has a unique stationary distribution at every finite ranking intensity; as the intensity grows without bound its transition matrix converges to that of a chain that moves only along weakly better unilateral deviations, whose closed classes are the sink strongly connected components of the game's weakly-better-response graph, on each of which it is a Markov-Conley chain, and each of which lies inside a single chain component of the replicator flow *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-943](../record/theory.d/THEORY-943.md): When a center with no ground truth pays each rater a strictly proper scoring rule on the distribution of a reference rater's report implied by her own report, under a common prior and a known signal model in which raters' signals are stochastically relevant to one another, truthful reporting is a strict Nash equilibrium, but not necessarily the only one: in the authors' two-signal example under the log rule, every rater always reporting h, or always reporting l, is also an equilibrium *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-944](../record/theory.d/THEORY-944.md): The value of the zero-sum game between two populations' evaluation matrices does not depend on which Nash equilibrium is used, is unchanged by adding agents that behave as mixtures of existing members, and is not positive for a population whose agents are all behavioural mixtures of the other's *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-946](../record/theory.d/THEORY-946.md): In the zero-sum meta-game on an antisymmetric evaluation matrix the maximum-entropy Nash equilibrium is unique; when the meta-game has only one Nash equilibrium, adding exact copies of an agent splits that agent's mass evenly and leaves every Nash average unchanged; the equilibrium is uniform exactly when every agent's mean log-odds is zero, and uniform on the top-rated agents when the matrix is a pure gradient *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-948](../record/theory.d/THEORY-948.md): On Stable Diffusion 2, MultiDiffusion's 512 × 4608 panoramas had crops closer in FID to the reference model's own samples than two outpainting baselines (10.3 against 18.4 and 45.5, fresh reference samples scoring 6.05) at equal CLIP score, over 8 prompts; and on 1,000 COCO layouts of two to four objects, the overlap of a segmenter's output with the target layout was 0.26 IoU against 0.16–0.17 for the baselines and 0.43 for the real images, of which region fusion alone gave 0.18 and an early phase showing each region's denoiser only its own region gave the rest *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-951](../record/theory.d/THEORY-951.md): For independent identically distributed observations, and neglecting how far the log-likelihood-ratio walk overshoots its boundaries, Wald's sequential probability ratio test accepts the null hypothesis with probability (A^h − 1)/(A^h − B^h), where h ≠ 0 solves E e^{hz} = 1, and takes on average [(1 − γ) log B + γ log A]/E z observations; no sequential test with the same error probabilities needs fewer on average under either hypothesis than Wald's lower bounds, which the test attains when the overshoot is zero, and for a normal mean it saves 47–63% of the fixed-sample test's observations at error rates from .01 to .05; the overshoot-free formulas are exact for Brownian motion with drift, which the paper never mentions *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-952](../record/theory.d/THEORY-952.md): In Wald's sequential probability ratio test, which samples until the likelihood ratio of two simple hypotheses leaves an interval (B, A), the realized error probabilities satisfy α/(1 − β) ≤ 1/A and β/(1 − α) ≤ B whenever the test terminates with probability one, with or without independent observations; so the boundaries A = (1 − β)/α and B = β/(1 − α), set with no distribution theory, give errors α′ ≤ α/(1 − β), β′ ≤ β/(1 − α) and α′ + β′ ≤ α + β, and they would be exact only if the ratio stopped on the boundary *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-954](../record/theory.d/THEORY-954.md): When the information a design yields depends on the unknown parameter, as in nonlinear models or nonlinear functions of linear ones, Bayesian design criteria are normal approximations to expected utility that average a local criterion over the prior, such as the expected log det of the Fisher information, and locally optimal design is the special case of a point-mass prior; a locally optimal design can leave the quantity of interest inestimable, as for the turning point of a quadratic regression on [−1, 1] with best guess ½, where the locally c-optimal design puts half its mass at 0 and half at 1 and identifies only θ₁ + θ₂ *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-955](../record/theory.d/THEORY-955.md): On 480 sets of two to five public LoRAs on two Stable Diffusion 1.5 checkpoints, GPT-4V's paired judgements, averaged over both presentation orders and three seeds, scored giving each LoRA its own denoising steps in rotation (LoRA Switch) and averaging every LoRA's guided noise prediction at every step (LoRA Composite) above merging the LoRAs' weights at 0.8 each, at every number of LoRAs, the composition gap growing from 0.04–0.11 points of 10 at two LoRAs to 0.92–1.32 at five as merging fell from about 8.7 to 5.2; two annotators rating 120 images agreed in direction; the design does not separate composing at sampling time from the merged update's scale growing with the number of LoRAs *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-956](../record/theory.d/THEORY-956.md): In the normal linear model with known error variance and a conjugate normal prior of precision R/σ², the design that maximizes the expected Shannon information of the posterior is the one maximizing det(nM(η) + R), Bayes D-optimality, and the design that minimizes expected quadratic loss with weight matrix A is the one minimizing tr A(nM(η) + R)^-1, Bayes A-optimality; both criteria depend on the design and not on the data, so in this model a sequential design gains nothing over the best fixed one *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-957](../record/theory.d/THEORY-957.md): When the signal law depends on the decision, Kwon and Perchet's approachability algorithm learns what each decision would reveal only from the stages on which it is played: it keeps every decision's probability at least γ/|I| and estimates the flag by importance weighting, an estimate that is conditionally unbiased with second moment Σ_i 1/P[i_t = i] ≤ |I|²/γ, with the tuned floor γ shrinking as T^-1/3; when the signal law does not depend on the decision, the raw signal is already unbiased for every component and no floor is used *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-958](../record/theory.d/THEORY-958.md): When each view takes pixels directly (a crop of a larger canvas, or the whole image under a region mask), MultiDiffusion's step, the least-squares reconciliation of several denoisers' proposed next states, is their per-pixel average weighted by the weights of the views covering that pixel; this is exact for 0/1 weights, the only ones the paper uses, while for other weights the loss as printed weights by their squares; with a deterministic update affine in the noise prediction it is one step taken with the per-pixel weighted mean of the views' noise predictions; and the guarantee that each view then follows the reference model's diffusion path holds only if the loss is zero at every step, which overlapping proposals that disagree do not reach *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-960](../record/theory.d/THEORY-960.md): In DeGroot's model, where each member repeatedly replaces its opinion by a fixed weighted average of all members' current opinions, F⁽ⁿ⁾ = PⁿF, the group reaches a consensus from every starting set of opinions exactly when the chain P has a single closed class of communicating members and that class is aperiodic; the consensus is then Σπᵢ Fᵢ with π the unique stationary vector, πP = π, which gives members outside the closed class no weight; two closed classes, or one periodic class, give no consensus *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-962](../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md): In a finite partial-monitoring game, the signals of a set D of actions determine the expected loss difference of actions i and j under every outcome distribution iff ℓ_i − ℓ_j lies in the sum of the row spaces of their signal matrices; when it does not, two outcome distributions differing along a vector in the common kernel give every action in D the same signal law and reverse the preference between i and j, so no amount of play restricted to D can learn the comparison *(used by 4; also will-organization, formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-968](../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md): In the Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark's causal-variable localization baselines on Gemma-2 2B and Llama-3.1 8B, features of the public Gemma Scope and Llama Scope sparse autoencoders, selected by a learned binary mask, never gave a higher mean interchange-intervention accuracy than the same mask over the model's own hidden dimensions, in all sixteen task–variable cells and by 1 to 14 points, while distributed alignment search, trained against the causal model it is scored on, gave the highest mean in fifteen of them *(used by 3; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-969](../record/theory.d/THEORY-969.md): In hierarchical LDA every document draws all its words from the topics on one root-to-leaf path of a tree drawn from the nested Chinese restaurant process, so the prior is a nested sequence of partitions of the documents, exchangeable in them, and two documents share a topic only by sharing the whole path above it: no document can draw on two sibling subtrees *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-972](../record/theory.d/THEORY-972.md): In the author–topic model the likelihood of a corpus depends on the topics Φ and the authors' topic distributions Θ only through the document–word matrix ΦΘA, A being fixed by the observed authorship, so LDA (each document its own author) and the topic-free author model (each author one topic) are special cases; and the likelihood leaves Φ and Θ unidentified not only up to the permutations of topics the paper names but along a continuum of changes of topic basis whenever every topic gives every word positive probability *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-978](../record/theory.d/THEORY-978.md): Causal scrubbing scores a hypothesis through the partitions of the dataset that its interpretation nodes induce, so two hypotheses that assign different features to a node but induce the same partition on the dataset, such as two features perfectly correlated on it, receive the same score *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-979](../record/theory.d/THEORY-979.md): On one prompt, a transformer whose MLPs are replaced by a cross-layer transcoder, with its attention patterns and normalization denominators frozen and each MLP's reconstruction error added back as a constant, reproduces the model's activations and outputs exactly and is linear between features, so each active feature's pre-activation is the sum of its attribution-graph edges and constants; a perturbation that clamps MLP outputs up to the target feature's encoder layer then confirms a direct edge by construction, and tests only knock-on effects and the output *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-981](../record/theory.d/THEORY-981.md): When a data distribution is unchanged by a group of orthogonal transformations under which a network is equivariant, the weights fixed by that group form a subspace that population gradient descent never leaves; for attention-only transformers on block-list inductive tasks, with fixed orthogonal write maps, Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann compute this subspace as the span of a few elementary token and position actions composed through the heads, and an elementwise optimizer such as sign descent keeps it only when those actions are aligned with the parameter coordinates *(used by 5; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-983](../record/theory.d/THEORY-983.md): In Geiger et al.'s three-layer feed-forward network trained on hierarchical equality and in BERT fine-tuned on monotonicity inference, interchange interventions on subspaces found by a learned rotation aligned the hypothesised two-variable causal models with interchange intervention accuracy of 1.00 on the rotation's training data, where the axis-aligned alignment closest to the learned rotation reached 0.73 and 0.51; in BERT, the learned lexical-entailment subspace was in turn aligned, at 0.97 to 0.98, with a model holding only the identities of the two words *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-985](../record/theory.d/THEORY-985.md): The beta process BP(c, B0) is the de Finetti mixing measure of the Indian buffet process: given n objects, the next has each existing feature with probability equal to the number holding it over c + n and a Poisson(cγ/(c + n)) number of new ones, so n objects hold Poisson(γ Σ_{i<n} c/(c + i)) distinct features, which is the IBP's αH_n at c = 1 and γ = α, and c alone sets how much objects share *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-987: In Claude 3 Sonnet's middle-layer residual stream, on two prompts for which every active sparse-autoencoder feature was ablated, how strongly a feature was active predicted its ablation effect on the answer poorly (correlation about 0.12) while its gradient attribution predicted it well (about 0.81), and on the multi-step prompt only three of the ten most active features were among the ten with the largest ablation effect *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-991: In a one-layer transformer whose MLP has 512 ReLU neurons, a sparse autoencoder with 4,096 features trained on that layer's activations yields features that a blinded rater and an automated pipeline judged far more interpretable than the neurons, that for the four features examined in detail correspond to no neuron, and whose effects on the output, which the autoencoder never saw, agree with their activations; splicing in the reconstruction recovers 79% of the loss reduction the MLP provides, measured against zero-ablating it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-993: In the mixed membership stochastic blockmodel the probability of an edge from p to q, given the memberships, is (1 − ρ)π_pᵀBπ_q, so the graph's likelihood given the memberships is unchanged by π ↦ Rπ, B ↦ R⁻ᵀBR⁻¹ for any invertible R that keeps the memberships on the simplex and B in [0, 1], a continuum around any solution with B's rates strictly between 0 and 1; and the sparsity parameter ρ enters only through (1 − ρ)B, so it is fixed by nothing but the bound B ≤ 1, and the paper's printed estimator of it is the fraction of absent edges whatever the fit *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- THEORY-994: In Ameisen et al.'s evaluations, the local replacement model of their 18-layer language model, built from a 10-million-feature cross-layer transcoder, responded to small perturbations much as the model did one layer after the intervention and increasingly differently over later layers, more in the size of the effect than its direction and slightly more for larger dictionaries, and over 20 prompts the graph's influence of one feature on another ranked the effect of ablating the first on the second with a Spearman correlation of 0.72 *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- THEORY-998: In GPT-2 XL, for 1000 facts the model knows, restoring single clean hidden states into a run whose subject tokens were noised recovers the most of the correct object's probability at two sites, middle layers at the last subject token, where MLP outputs carry most of the effect, and late layers at the last token, where attention does; and a rank-one edit of one middle MLP output matrix keyed on the last subject token inserts counterfactual facts that generalize to paraphrases and spare neighbouring subjects better than the fine-tuning, knowledge-neuron and hypernetwork editors tested, working best at that token and in middle layers *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-999: In the finite beta–Bernoulli feature model with prevalences Beta(α/K, 1), the expected number of occupied features among N objects is K(1 − (α/K)B(α/K, N + 1)), strictly below the Indian buffet process's αH_N for every finite K and tending to it as K grows, and each object holds Kα/(K + α) features on average rather than α *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1003: On NIPS papers (1,557 training and 183 test documents, 100 topics, fixed hyperparameters), the author–topic model gave test documents lower perplexity than LDA while sixteen or fewer of their words had been observed and higher perplexity beyond that; one fictitious author per document improved on the author–topic model throughout and lost to LDA after about 64 words, and an author model without topics did worst *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1006: In the dependent Indian buffet process each item's feature indicator is a Gaussian process thresholded at the quantile of a stick length that does not change with the covariate, so its prevalence is the same at every covariate value and its persistence is set separately by the covariance; the whole feature matrix at a covariate value is an Indian buffet process only when there is no shared feature-level process, and with one the items are correlated and fewer features are occupied *(used by 3; also learned-structure)*
- THEORY-1007: On four subject–verb agreement tasks in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, circuits of sparse-autoencoder features and autoencoder error nodes, selected by linear estimates of indirect effect, carried half or more of the behaviour on held-out pairs with about 100 and 500 nodes, where circuits of neurons needed about 1,500 and more than 30,000; with the error nodes removed, the same feature circuits carried little of it, under about a quarter in Pythia and almost none in Gemma *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- THEORY-1012: Latent features made dependent through a layer of categories, each observation's features being a function of how many of its categories carry each feature, stay finite on finite data when a feature carried by none of an observation's categories is always off; under that condition a category can switch features on and never off, so features depend on one another by sharing a category, or, where an observation has a single category, by excluding one another, and no feature or category suppresses another *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1015: Groups of objects drawn from beta processes share features only if the measure they are drawn around is discrete; in the hierarchical beta process that measure is itself a beta process draw, and at each shared feature a group's prevalence is Beta(c_j b, c_j(1 − b)) around the shared prevalence b, so a small c_j lets groups differ and a large one pulls them together *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1019: Under the Markov Indian buffet process the expected number of features on at the first time step is α, as in the Indian buffet process, but it rises over time toward α·E[ln((2 − b)/(1 − b))] with b ~ Beta(γ, δ), which is 9.04 at γ = 10 and δ = 1, so after the first step the rows are not distributed as an Indian buffet process *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1024: In GPT-J, for 652 CounterFact facts the model knows, the per-fact causal-tracing effect at an MLP layer adds at most 3.2 points of explained variance in the success of editing that fact at that layer, beyond what the choice of layer alone explains, across ROME, MEMIT and constrained fine-tuning and five editing objectives; ROME rewrites the fact at over 96% at every layer but the last, including layers where tracing does not place it, and the only reliable link appears when the edit is made on the noised input that tracing uses *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1034: In the Markov Indian buffet process each feature's probability of staying on is drawn independently of its probability of switching on, so how long a feature persists once on does not depend on how rare it is; the process is defined for the time steps of one sequence, not for several objects over time *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1037: In the infinite hidden Markov model, drawing at each time step a slice variable uniformly below the probability of the transition taken leaves the posterior unchanged and leaves only finitely many state trajectories with positive probability, so a whole trajectory can be resampled exactly by forward filtering and backward sampling, with no truncation of the state space *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1041: In the Indian buffet process the feature probabilities in decreasing order are products of independent Beta(α, 1) draws, so the k-th has mean (α/(α + 1))^k, and keeping only the first K of them gives an expected number of occupied features among N objects that approaches αH_N from below: 8.97 at K = 16, N = 12 and α = 3, against 9.31 in the limit and 6.83 for the finite model with sixteen independent prevalences *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1043: The finite feature model in which each of K features has prevalence Beta(α/K, 1) has, as K grows, a limit on equivalence classes of binary matrices that ignore the order of columns, and the Indian buffet process, in which the i-th object takes each earlier feature with probability m/i and Poisson(α/i) new ones, produces the same distribution, so its objects are exchangeable and the number of features they hold is Poisson(αH_N) *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1046: In infinite sparse factor analysis, where a binary mask says whether a source is active at a data point and an independent Gaussian value says how strongly, the evidence of that data point for the source being active, with its value integrated out, is σ̂·exp(μ̂²/(2σ̂²)) for the posterior mean μ̂ and standard deviation σ̂ of the value; when the residual has no component along the source's loading the ratio is σ̂, below one, so the data favour an inactive source over an active one at zero by a factor that the prior on the value sets *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1048: On the Black Queen Hypothesis of Morris, Lenski and Zinser, losing a costly function whose product leaks to neighbours is favoured by ordinary individual selection in large free-living microbial populations, and the loss proceeds until the remaining producers just supply the community, so that most cells come to depend on a rare few with no relatedness, cooperation or collective required *(used by 3; also transient-support)*
- THEORY-1049: On McCutcheon and colleagues' survey, bacterial endosymbionts lose their own cell-envelope and envelope-transport genes together below about 400 kb, and begin to lose translation genes (ribosomal proteins, tRNAs, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases) below about 200 kb, so that the smallest-genome symbionts cannot be self-sufficient and their membranes, transport and protein synthesis are presumably supplied by the host, as for organelles *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1050: In Athreya, Czuppon and Gokhale's adaptive-dynamics model of an incipient endosymbiosis, mutual dependence (the product of the partners' obligacies) evolves ahead of reproductive cohesion (the product of their adhesions) early on, but only under the mapping in which each partner's free-living growth depends on its own obligacy alone while dissociation depends on both partners' adhesions; the authors' own appendix shows the bias vanishing under matched mappings and reversing under the opposite one, and their survey of real symbioses cannot test it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1051: In Athreya, Czuppon and Gokhale's model of an incipient endosymbiosis, the partner with the larger and faster-growing population evolves faster and becomes fully obligate first, which the authors read as a Red King effect in which the collective's shared fate aligns interests; with equal within-collective rates for both partners, the other partner's dependence then stays where it was, rises to full dependence, or falls to none, according to whether partners are born or die inside the collective; and in its simulations dependence rose from zero at the higher collective carrying capacities tried and not at the lowest, under a condition the authors show sufficient and not necessary, so a full transition to a mutually dependent, co-reproducing pair is a parameter-dependent outcome and not the default *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1053: Under unitary evolution, two states of a quantum system can each leave a record in another system while themselves staying undisturbed only if they are orthogonal or the record does not distinguish them; so the outcomes that can be recorded repeatably form an orthogonal set, a result that uses only unitarity and repeatability and not the Born rule *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1054: One arrangement of harmonic particles on a finite graph, with the same wiring, potential and inverse-mass response, gives the discrete wave equation when the integrator stores position and momentum and the discrete heat equation when it stores position alone; both are governed by the symmetrized graph Laplacian, and the coupling data do not decide between them *(used by 2; also realizability)*
- THEORY-1059: The dynamics a coupled cell network admits, restricted to a robustly synchronous pattern, are dynamics admitted by a smaller quotient network whose cells are the synchronized classes, so behaviour of the quotient, including symmetric behaviour the original network has no symmetry to force, appears in the original as synchronous behaviour; the quotient admits more dynamics than restriction produces, and is unique only up to refinement of its arrow types *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1061: Flack makes downward causation operational as components tuning their behaviour to their own estimates of aggregate variables they collectively compute: weak (apparent) when at least one component tunes to a variable slower than the behaviour producing it, strong (effective) when the variable is predictive, robust, used nearly universally, agreed on and gaining mutual information with the microscopic behaviour; she speaks of a new level only at the strong form, and regeneration of the variable by its use is not among her criteria *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1062: On a discourse sheaf, where each agent expresses a private opinion through a linear map into each edge's space of topics, sheaf-Laplacian opinion diffusion converges to the orthogonal projection of the initial opinions onto the global sections, which are agreement in what each pair expresses and not in what they hold; stable polarized or incomparable private opinions are therefore possible, and when the sheaf has no nonzero global section the only limit is all opinions zero *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1065: In a coupled cell network, a pattern of synchrony is invariant under every dynamics the network's architecture admits if and only if its partition of the cells is balanced, each cell of a class receiving, through each kind of arrow, the same number of inputs from each class; symmetry is one way to get balance and not the only one, so robust synchrony occurs in networks with no symmetry and among cells with no coupling between them, and the invariance says nothing about whether the pattern attracts *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1066: In constructor theory, a set of attributes is an information variable when every permutation of it and its cloning are possible tasks, and distinguishability is defined afterwards, as the possibility of mapping a variable onto an information variable; so information is fixed by counterfactual properties of a substrate without presupposing distinguishability, and instantiating it is stated as an intrinsic property of the substrate in the sense of referring to no other specific substrate *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1067: In angular synchronization from m pairwise offsets, each exact with probability p and otherwise uniform over L values, no estimator of any computational cost can recover all n angles with small error when p is below about √((n/m)·2 log₂ L/(L − 1)), nor an angle of average degree below about √((n/m)·log₂ L/(L − 1)), because each offset carries at most I(L, p) ≈ ½(L − 1)p² bits; below these thresholds a global configuration that exists is not determined by the pairwise evidence, whatever the resources spent on finding it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1068: In the founding statement of relational quantum mechanics the states and values of systems are relative to other systems, but the systems are not: the world is assumed decomposed, possibly in several ways, into systems each characterized by the questions that can be asked of it and a finite information capacity, so the relata precede the relations, as an assumption and without an ontology of events *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1069: In a von Neumann measurement the measuring variable's information about the measured variable grows continuously under the unitary coupling, in Di Biagio and Rovelli's model as I_{A:B}(t) = sin²(ωt)H_A, so the discontinuity of a quantum measurement lies only in a threshold on when information counts as a fact; with an idealized pure ready state a fact conditional on a pointer value appears at once, which they attribute to the idealization *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1070: For a weighted cellular sheaf of finite-dimensional vector spaces on a finite cell complex, the kernel of the degree-k Hodge Laplacian is the k-th sheaf cohomology, in degree 0 the space of global sections, and the linear flow ẋ = −Δ^k x converges exponentially to the orthogonal projection of its initial state onto that kernel, each eigencomponent decaying at its own eigenvalue; the inner products on the stalks are part of the data, so the same sections can come with different rates, and the Laplacian does not determine the sheaf *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1071: Quantum mechanics does not entail agential realism: Bohmian mechanics reproduces its predictions with an ontology of individual particles on determinate trajectories, and relational quantum mechanics, the interpretation Barad names as closest, makes values relational while keeping the systems prior to their interactions *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1075: In relational quantum mechanics as Di Biagio and Rovelli define it, a fact relative to one system is stable for another, so that the other may sum over it classically, only approximately and only relative to that other system: decoherence of the first system by an environment the second cannot reach gives the classical rule to order of the environment states' overlap, a differently coupled system may still see interference, and a fact can be stable for a system for which it is not yet a fact *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1076: For Bohr a phenomenon is the observation obtained under a specified experimental arrangement, epistemic and derivative, with atomic object and instrument presupposed real; his relational holism is epistemic, and the subject–object, knower–known and word–world dualisms are presupposed by his account, so Bohr's authority does not support agential realism *(used by 2; also record-as-apparatus)*
- THEORY-1078: Constructor theory puts constraint in two places: a principle is a law that constrains other laws and is tested through its rivals, and a constructor is a physical thing that keeps its ability to cause a transformation; a task is possible when the laws set no limit, short of perfection, on how well it could be performed and that ability retained, so possibility needs no actual constructor, and constructor-theoretic statements mention none *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1079: An open system can tip away from an attractor that exists, keeps its stability and keeps its basin at every frozen value of its parameter, when the attractor moves faster than the system can track it; with steady drift what bifurcates is the ability to track, in a co-moving frame, not the attractor, and the critical rate depends on the relaxation rate, the distance to the tipping threshold and the starting state *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1081: Di Biagio and Rovelli locate the Frauchiger–Renner contradiction and the violation of the Local Friendliness inequalities in one step, a superobserver using facts relative to a friend he holds in full quantum control as if they were his own, which is the classical sum rule applied where those facts are not stable for him; they base quantum ontology on facts relative to systems rather than on stable facts, arguing that stability is itself relational and only approximate and counting the Local Friendliness violation as evidence, with an absolute macroreality emerging only approximately and only relative to systems for which decoherence is strong *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1082: On a connected graph whose edges carry phase shifts αᵢⱼ = −αⱼᵢ, the edge relations zⱼ = e^{iαᵢⱼ}zᵢ have a common nonzero solution, equivalently the twisted Laplacian Lα = δα*δα has a zero mode, exactly when the phase accumulated around every cycle is 0 mod 2π; otherwise each relation can be met alone but not all together, and the smallest eigenvalue of Lα, positive, measures the residual incompatibility, which on an isolated ℓ-cycle is largest at holonomy π *(used by 7; also formal-apparatus)*
- THEORY-1085: In Toner and Tu's hydrodynamic theory, a flock's ordered state is a broken continuous symmetry of a coarse-grained velocity field: speed fluctuations relax in a finite time of order 1/α and are dropped, leaving as slow degrees of freedom the transverse velocity and the conserved density, which propagate as sound at ω = ±cq⊥; no individual member appears in the description, which is offered for a universality class of microscopic rules *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1087: In the symmetric Sakaguchi–Kuramoto model on a triangle and a pentagon sharing one vertex, the lag α gives each ℓ-cycle a phase-independent path mismatch (ℓ − 2)α, and the remote-synchronized locked branch passes through an exact two-group state at α = π/3, where the pentagon's mismatch reaches π; but that branch has already lost transverse stability, in the pentagonal symmetry sector, at αc ≃ 1.0164, so the point of maximal cycle frustration marks the geometry of the phase relations, not the end of the synchronized pattern *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1088: When the expression maps of a discourse sheaf diffuse to reduce disagreement, with opinions held fixed they converge to the nearest sheaf, in Frobenius distance, of which the opinions are a global section, so apparent consensus is reached by changing what is said ("learning to lie"); with opinions diffusing too the joint flow is gradient descent on ½‖δx‖², and conserved diagonal blocks of αδᵀδ − βxxᵀ keep the opinions from collapsing to zero; nothing in either flow checks an expression against the opinion it expresses *(used by 6; also formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- THEORY-1089: In a passive linear network, eliminating interior nodes by the principle of minimum power, which over a general field with positive elements is stationarity, takes a Dirichlet form to a Dirichlet form on the remaining nodes, linearly in their values; eliminating one node s adds c_is·c_js/Σ_k c_ks to each coupling c_ij, so two resistors in series act at their ends as one of resistance r_AB + r_BC; composing Dirichlet forms by this elimination is associative but lacks identities, because an ideal wire of zero impedance has no power functional *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1090: Eliminating an interior vertex of a cellular sheaf on a graph can leave its boundary a space of consistent assignments that no sheaf on the boundary vertices has: the interior can impose a constraint among boundary vertices that no set of pairwise compatibility conditions expresses, so Kron reduction, which turns the Laplacian of a connected graph into a graph Laplacian on any set of boundary vertices, fails for sheaves in general and holds when every vertex stalk has dimension at most one *(used by 6; also record-as-apparatus, realizability)*
- THEORY-1093: In Di Biagio and Rovelli's reformulation of relational quantum mechanics a relative fact is a conditional probability concentrated on one value: A is a fact relative to B when the relative information I_{A|B} = I_A + I_{A:B} is maximal; since only commuting variables have a joint distribution, perspectives belong to commutative subalgebras of observables, not to quantum systems, so a qubit has none, and the joint distribution is itself relative to a further system, so the relativity iterates *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1098: On Karnkowska and colleagues' genome analysis, the oxymonad Monocercomonoides exilis lost its mitochondrion only after the organelle's essential functions had been removed one by one, Fe–S cluster assembly to a bacterial-type SUF system shared with mitochondriate relatives and then the glycine cleavage system by loss, and the loss left the rest of the cell canonical, with no compensating changes found *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1099: On Kay and colleagues' relaxed-clock dating of pre-LECA gene duplications, most duplications in eukaryotic gene families of archaeal origin, including actin, tubulin, vesicle-trafficking and nuclear-targeted families, predate the onset of duplications in genes of alphaproteobacterial origin at about 2.2 billion years ago, which the authors take as the start of mitochondrial endosymbiosis, so the host was elaborating its cytoskeleton, endomembranes and nuclear machinery before the mitochondrion; each date is a maximum age for its paralogues' functions, many intervals reach below 2.2 billion years, and the order of phagocytosis and the mitochondrion is left open *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1100: On Sørensen and colleagues' review, a bacterial endosymbiont becomes genetically integrated, the authors' mark of an organelle, when nuclear genes whose products are imported into it functionally replace essential genes it has lost, and this does not require gene transfer from the endosymbiont: in the Paulinella chromatophore and the nitroplast, the two systems with hundreds of imported proteins, many of which fill gaps left by lost genes, the imported proteins come mostly from the host's own genes or from other bacteria, and in the nitroplast no gene transfer from the endosymbiont has been found *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1101: Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf and Koonin find, on 5,850 eukaryotic gene stems, that normalized stem length does not behave as a clock of acquisition time: alphaproteobacterial stems are longer than Asgard ones for the 70% of stems below 0.3 and shorter only above 0.35, oxidative-phosphorylation genes presumed acquired together vary by more than two orders of magnitude, and information-processing genes have short stems; they conclude that even normalized stem lengths are set primarily by factors other than acquisition time, at least over the long timescales analysed, and suggest that adaptation after acquisition lengthens stems *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1102: On Pittis and Gabaldón's stem-length analysis of the LECA proteome, families of alphaproteobacterial origin and mitochondrial location sit closer to their prokaryotic relatives, after correction for each family's rate, than families of other bacterial origin (P = 0.044), which sit closer than archaeal families, and the authors read this as late acquisition of the mitochondrion by a host whose proteome was already chimaeric, under their stated assumption that rates before and after LECA are correlated *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1103: On Shigenobu and colleagues' genome of Buchnera sp. APS, the aphid symbiont keeps the genes for the amino acids its host cannot make and has lost almost all of those its host can, uses host-made glutamate and aspartate as precursors, and lacks phospholipid synthesis and nearly all its own transcriptional regulators, so that its metabolism interlocks with the host's and it presumably lives only inside the bacteriocyte, a state reached by gene loss from an E. coli-like ancestor *(used by 2; also transient-support)*
- THEORY-1104: In Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf and Koonin's constrained-tree survey of widespread eukaryotic protein families, Asgard archaea are the largest single prokaryotic source, with about half the likelihood weight in the best-resolved families and the lead in nearly every functional system, while Alphaproteobacteria contribute a small, coherent set centred on the mitochondrion and other bacteria about a third of families, scattered across functions with no pathway led by one donor except a narrow Myxococcota signal in nucleotide-sugar and nicotinate metabolism; the authors read this as one Asgard host lineage, one endosymbiont and piecemeal gene transfer rather than further symbioses *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1105: In Bernabeu, Manzano-Morales, Marcet-Houben and Gabaldón's reconstruction of the last eukaryotic common ancestor's proteome, two bacterial phyla besides the mitochondrial ancestor, Myxococcota and Planctomycetota, each account for a share of the proteome comparable to that of Alphaproteobacteria and Asgard archaea under thresholds calibrated on those accepted partners, and stem-length distributions order the acquisitions as waves, Asgard first, then Planctomycetota, then the mitochondrial ancestor and Myxococcota together; the authors read this as serial associations with several partners, while conceding that their data cannot say whether any donor was a symbiont *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1106: Campbell and colleagues report, from four cicada species with five or six eggs each, that Hodgkinia cells per egg range from about 4,900 in a species with one Hodgkinia lineage to about 30,000, some six times as many, in Magicicada septendecim, whose Hodgkinia has split into many interdependent lineages and the only species that differs significantly, while Sulcia numbers are not raised, the transmission route is the same, and every egg sampled carries every lineage tracked by marker genes; the authors take the raised titre as a host adaptation that compensates for the symbiont's fragmentation, and a cost of it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1107: On Sørensen and colleagues' scenario, an endosymbiont becomes an organelle in steps: the host first targets effector proteins into it; an imported host protein redundant with one of its functions then lets the endosymbiont's own gene decay, making it dependent; and a general import pathway, once evolved, brings in hundreds of proteins; this genetic integration arises only in permanent, vertically transmitted associations, and host effector control without vertical transmission, as in rhizobia, does not lead to it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1108: On Imachi and colleagues' cultivation of Candidatus Prometheoarchaeum syntrophicum MK-D1, the first Asgard archaeon grown in the laboratory is a small, internally simple coccus with long branching protrusions that degrades amino acids only in syntrophy, handing hydrogen and formate to partners that can be exchanged, and from its genome and other Asgard genomes the authors infer that the Asgard ancestor was likewise dependent on metabolic partners; the isolate is a modern relative separated from the host lineage by about two billion years, grown only in co-culture, and the entangle–engulf–endogenize model built on it is a hypothesis the authors call not definitive *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1109: Santana-Molina, Williams, Snel and Spang find that the last eukaryotic common ancestor's central carbon metabolism was chimeric: a few Asgard-archaeal enzymes in cytosolic glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway, four placed with Asgard archaea at bootstrap 39–97% and two ambiguously, most alphaproteobacterial ones in the mitochondrial TCA cycle and pyruvate conversion, and others from various bacteria with no third dominant donor, since remodelled by loss, horizontal replacement and retargeting so that compartment no longer follows origin; the authors take the cytosol–mitochondrion split as support for syntrophy *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1119: Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde propose that minimal agency requires individuality, interactional asymmetry and normativity set by the system's own organisation, each necessary and together, they say, sufficient; that individuality without the other two is not agency; and that a system optimizing an externally fixed function is not a model of agency *(used by 6; also organizational-normativity)*
- THEORY-1141: In the time limit, sheaf diffusion on a graph projects node features onto the harmonic space of its sheaf Laplacian, and which labellings that space can linearly separate depends on the class of restriction maps: a weighted graph Laplacian cannot separate the sides of a balanced bipartite graph, signed one-dimensional maps separate any two classes and no one-dimensional sheaf separates three, while diagonal maps with d ≥ C and orthogonal bundles with C ≤ 2d (d = 2, 4 and, against the paper, 8) separate any labelling; every separating sheaf is built from the labels *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1158: On synchronization of S4 relations with outliers, an untrained mechanism that composes relations through third vertices gains 26–45 points over the single direct path, and weighting the candidate paths by the Wilson loops of squares that avoid the missing edge adds 0.6–7.8 points, most where clean two-hop paths become a minority; it stays below spectral synchronization with one reweighting pass on every setting and within 2.2 points of plain spectral synchronization either way; its 0.99 AUC for corrupted triangles is the ceiling that exactly flat clean data set, not a measure of detection power *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- THEORY-1161: In Friedkin's simulations of reflected appraisal with Friedkin–Johnsen anchoring on initial positions, 99.0–100% of 100,000 random strongly connected networks of 5 to 25 members, complete or with random zero weights, evolve to a single leader and the rest to two *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1162: In a consumer-resource model whose species-resource benefits and impacts have correlation rho, the replica-symmetric cavity fixed point loses stability where rho squared equals surviving species over non-depleted resources *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- THEORY-1163: Krakauer et al.'s organismal and colonial individuality, A* = I(S_{n+1}; S_n) and A = I(S_{n+1}; S_n | E_n), cannot decrease when variables are moved from the environment into the candidate system, so maximizing either over candidate boundaries selects the largest candidate, and a boundary found this way needs a size cost the measures do not contain *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1165: Kahl proposes that agency in the sense that bears on responsibility needs a standpoint that settles and carries forward revised evaluative standards when its inherited ones break down, which is absent where revision is imposed from outside, escaped by rollback or chosen by a fixed higher-order rule; that allocating authority among a system's own components coordinates execution without authoring its governing frame; and that planning, autonomy, memory and coordination do not supply that standpoint *(used by 3; also organizational-normativity)*
- THEORY-1166: Di Paolo argues that autopoiesis as originally defined entails conservation and not active homeostasis, so it gives a system only an all-or-nothing norm, to go on or to die, which an observer and not the system can use; that a graded norm the system itself has needs adaptivity, a capacity to detect tendencies toward the boundary of its viability and to act so as to reverse them; and that sense-making and agency need adaptivity *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1167: When one intervention distribution over micro states is used at both levels, the effective information of a coarse-graining of a discrete mechanism, with each macro intervention realized by that distribution within its block, cannot exceed the micro effective information; so a positive causal emergence of effective information, scored with a uniform distribution at each level, equals the micro gain from changing the distribution minus a non-negative loss, and is a gain from the change of distribution *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- THEORY-1168: In a Lotka–Volterra community with a symmetric interaction matrix, the growth-weighted biomass rᵀx strictly increases along every edge of the invasion graph, so the invasion graph has no cycles *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1169: For a discrete mechanism scored with one full-support intervention distribution over micro causes at both levels, a coarse-graining of cause and effect keeps all of the micro effective information if and only if it merges only causes with identical rows P(Y | do(x)) and only effects with proportional columns, whatever the distribution; so the coarsest coarse-graining that ties the micro is the causal partition of causal feature learning, with effects grouped by normalized likelihood, and any merge of causes with different effects loses information under every such distribution *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- THEORY-1194: Clark and Chalmers argue that if belief is individuated by functional role, an external store that is constantly consulted, directly available and automatically endorsed can carry a standing belief, so that the material vehicles of some mental states extend beyond the skin; the step from coupling to parthood rests on that premise and on a parity principle they state rather than argue *(used by 2; also nucleating-argument)*
- THEORY-1227: Haken, Kelso and Bunz model the switch of rhythmic bimanual coordination from anti-phase to in-phase at a critical frequency as the loss of one stable state of an order parameter, relative phase, derived from two coupled oscillators; Kelso, Scholz and Schöner report the variability of relative phase rising before the switch in the anti-phase pattern only, in a few subjects and with no statistical test *(used by 4)*
- THEORY-1247: Griesemer and Shavit propose, as a first and rough sketch, that a collective becomes a new level of individuality only when collaboration toward a shared goal, rather than coordination or cooperation, organizes it, some core interactions have become generatively entrenched, and it has organizational closure, and that such a community can be reproduced only by exporting an organized sample of its roles and interactions, not of its members alone *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1248: Catalysts cancel out of the stoichiometric matrix, so a cycle of mutual catalytic production among species is not a stoichiometric cycle: the cycles that carry a reaction network's steady currents and affinities are fuel-to-waste pathways through it, and who catalyses whom enters only the rates, never the thermodynamic driving *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1249: In a fully observed, finite, communicating, stationary controlled Markov process, a deterministic goal-conditioned policy that achieves every composite goal of depth up to n with probability at least 1 − δ times the optimum determines every transition probability to within √(2P(1−P)/((n−1)(1−δ))), read from its first action on either-or goals; for a policy competent only at one-step goals no bound follows *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1250: A chemostat is an emergent structure of a closed reaction network: when exchange reactions are fast and the reservoir species are abundant by a factor of order Omega, the closed network behaves to leading order as the open one, with its local detailed balance and dissipation, over a window that opens once exchange equilibrates and closes on a time of order Omega, after which a driven network relaxes to equilibrium; neither separation alone suffices *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1252: In ℓ2-regularized regression held to a fixed training-error tolerance, refitting to one's own predictions on the same inputs shrinks each eigencomponent of the labels by a factor that falls with its Gram eigenvalue, while the regularization weight needed to meet the tolerance rises as the labels shrink, so repeated rounds amplify regularization and reach the zero function after finitely many; the loss comes from the regularizer acting again, not from information the student lacks *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1259: When a teacher's next-token distribution depends on a context the student cannot observe, the forward-KL-optimal student is the teacher averaged over the contexts compatible with the student's observation, the loss it cannot remove is the conditional mutual information between the teacher's output and the hidden context, and the optimal student is at least as uncertain as the teacher is on average; the self-distillation objectives actually trained may not be forward KL at all *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1260: Richens et al.'s sense of "an agent contains a world model" is that the transition function can be computed from the agent's goal-conditioned input-output map, uniquely to within the theorem's error, so the attribution is not a stance an observer may withhold, unlike a representation-theorem fit; but it holds of every implementation of the same map, a lookup table included, and so cannot show that a predictive component is realized inside the agent *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1261: At stationarity a driven reaction network is confined to a thermodynamic space: each reaction's affinity lies between zero and the largest cycle affinity per use of that reaction among the elementary flux modes containing it, and each product of concentrations lies between the effective equilibrium constants of the extremal pathways; with no driving the space collapses to the equilibrium point, so multistability, symmetry breaking and amplification above equilibrium need driving and are bounded by it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1264: Far from equilibrium, the weak-noise escape rate from an attractor goes as the exponential of minus system size times a barrier in the quasi-potential, not in any free energy, and that barrier is bracketed by thermodynamics: it is at most the entropy produced in relaxing from the saddle into the attractor and at least minus the entropy produced along the most likely escape path; the two bounds coincide at detailed balance and separate by twice the dissipation of the probability circulation, so far from equilibrium they can be very loose *(used by 2; also will-organization)*
- THEORY-1266: In an open reaction network of reversible elementary mass-action reactions, sustained currents need an emergent cycle with nonzero affinity: each chemostatted species either breaks a conservation law or opens an emergent cycle, so one chemostat never suffices; with every emergent affinity zero the network relaxes to a unique equilibrium fixed by its unbroken conserved quantities; and a nonequilibrium steady state dissipates exactly the sum over emergent cycles of current times affinity *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1267: A safe set that a nominal barrier-function controller keeps invariant can be left under an arbitrarily small input disturbance, but if the barrier inequality holds with a disturbance penalty, ḣ ≥ −α(h) − ι(‖d‖), the state stays in a larger set {h + γ(‖d‖∞) ≥ 0} with γ class-K, and adding a damping term along the barrier's input direction to any barrier controller gives this with an enlargement of ‖d‖²/(4ε) in units of h *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1268: In a nonequilibrium steady state of a thermodynamically consistent Markov jump network, the entropy produced while a current is counted, times the squared relative uncertainty of that count, is at least 2k_B, independent of the counting time, so a current precise to ε costs at least 2k_BT/ε² of dissipation; the 2015 letter proves this within linear response and for single-cycle networks at any affinity, and for many-cycle networks far from equilibrium shows it numerically and states it as a conjecture *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1269: In overparameterized linear regression, iterated self-training with fresh covariates, noiseless pseudo-labels and minimum-norm students applies a fresh random orthogonal projection to the estimate each round, so noise from the first fit decays geometrically while signal along a direction of variance s decays at the slower rate s/(s + τ); risk is U-shaped under anisotropy and monotone under isotropy, tends to the risk of predicting zero, and every student fits its teacher exactly on its own sample *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1273: In a driven chemical system with two stable states and a finite number of molecules, each maintained state is metastable: it is left by fluctuation after a time exponential in system size, set by a barrier in a nonequilibrium quasi-potential that closes at the saddle-node, and the long-run share of time in each state is fixed by the parameters and system size, not by the initial condition; the deterministic rate equation, where the initial condition decides, holds only on times short of that escape time *(used by 3; also transient-support)*
- THEORY-1274: Under a shared linear output head, the cross-entropy gradient of a multi-token-prediction head at its hidden state is exactly the gradient of a forward KL toward the model's own position-aligned next-token prediction, held fixed, plus the next-token cross-entropy gradient at the aligned state, which alone carries the sampled target; the identity is about gradients and computations, not information, and in heads fed the intervening tokens the student and its teacher condition on the same evidence *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1276: In Simondon's ontology, as Iliadis and Bencherki read it, information is not a signal transmitted between finished entities but a disparity between two differently ordered domains of a metastable system, and its meaning is the new structure that transduction produces in resolving it *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport)*
- THEORY-1287: The experiments mechanists use to find a mechanism's components (correlation, lesion, stimulation, and intervening on the whole while recording the parts) run in both directions between part and whole and, by Craver and Bechtel's own account, show only prima facie that an item is a component, because an item not interactively integrated into the system could be a background condition; they give no test of integration, so the experiments do not by themselves fix where a mechanism ends *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1288: If a mechanism's behaviour supervenes on its constituents' behaviours and constitution is not causal, every cause of that behaviour is also a cause of some constituent along another path, so no intervention can change the whole without separately changing a part; mutual manipulability by ideal interventions is then unsatisfiable, and once interventions are relaxed to admit these common causes, every model with constitutive dependence has a model without it that implies the same correlations under every manipulation, even in ideal experimental conditions *(used by 4)*
- THEORY-1289: In a dynamical model anchored to an identified mechanism, holding one part's variable fixed and finding that the phenomenon persists indicates that the part is not a component of the mechanism responsible for that phenomenon, as when Smolen et al. fixed CLOCK and circadian oscillation continued; the verdict is relative to the phenomenon and only as good as the model, and it decides which pathways the phenomenon needs, not which lie inside the system *(used by 2; also evidence-for-experience)*
- THEORY-1290: A dynamical model whose variables are properties of parts and operations already identified by experiment explores the dynamics of that mechanism, while one that posits its parts de novo and is checked only by fit to behaviour shows at most how a mechanism of that kind could produce the behaviour; fit can rule such models out but usually cannot decide between competing architectures that each fit, and what decides is independent evidence about the parts *(used by 4)*
- THEORY-1293: Given that every change in a phenomenon is simultaneously realized by some constituent on every lower level, that simultaneous changes are not causally related, that co-occurrence is transitive, and that the parts and their levels are already known, a single intervention that changes a part and the phenomenon simultaneously while directly changing at most one behaviour on each lower level shows that the part is a constituent; the condition presupposes the boundary and the level hierarchy it is applied to and cannot supply them *(used by 3)*
- THEORY-1304: In latent Dirichlet allocation each document draws its own topic mixture from a Dirichlet shared across the corpus and draws a topic afresh for every word, a three-level model of conditionally independent assignments; the mixture of unigrams, which draws one topic per document, is its two-level comparison, and the Dirichlet is a distribution over mixtures, not over topics *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- THEORY-1307: In Slemp et al.'s meta-analysis of 881 mostly cross-sectional samples, perceived support for autonomy, competence and relatedness each correlated strongly with satisfaction of all three needs (ρ = .44–.62) and negatively with their frustration, but the three supports intercorrelated .67–.71, and their need-specificity appears only in joint models: with all three entered, relatedness support carried relatedness satisfaction (β = .56) and autonomy support added nothing to it (β = .007) *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1310: In Sheldon, Elliot, Kim and Kasser's three studies of most satisfying events, self-esteem was as salient as autonomy, competence and relatedness in every sample and the largest unique predictor of event affect balance among ten candidate needs in two of the three US samples (β = .28, .38); the authors, SDT researchers, concluded that there may be four fundamental needs and judged it imprudent to treat self-esteem as an outcome *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1315: As a stochastically forced system approaches a fold bifurcation its dominant eigenvalue goes to zero, so it recovers ever more slowly from small perturbations, and under ongoing perturbation this critical slowing down shows as rising lag-1 autocorrelation and rising variance; skewness and flickering are further warnings not caused by slowing; but the same signals, less pronounced, also precede thresholds that are not bifurcations, so they mark proximity to a broad class of thresholds and not which kind, nor when the shift will come *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1316: In eight samples pooled to 3,692 respondents, the covariance of the BPNSFS items is organized more by item keying than by need: factors sharing a keying direction correlate .64 to .75 while satisfaction and frustration of the same need correlate .17 to .38, a higher-order model grouping the six scales by keying fits better than one grouping them by need, and the frustration items carry almost no thwarting content *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1318: Among 31 original self-report scales of psychological need fulfillment found by a 2023 systematic search, 21 measure satisfaction only, one measures frustration only and one thwarting only; all are self-reports of experience or of the perceived environment, the field uses satisfaction, frustration, support and thwarting interchangeably in places, and several frustration scales are negatively worded satisfaction items *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1320: In Ntoumanis et al.'s meta-analysis of 73 SDT-informed health interventions, mostly randomized, the interventions raised perceived need support (g = 0.64), autonomy and competence satisfaction (0.37, 0.31), autonomous motivation (0.30) and health behaviour (0.45) by the end of the intervention, but not relatedness, controlled motivation or amotivation, and their small effect on psychological health (0.29) was gone at follow-up (0.14, ns); need frustration was not an outcome and mediation was not tested *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1322: In Belgian adolescents, need frustration measured by the twelve BPNSFS frustration items statistically absorbs most of the association between depressive and eating disorder symptoms: cross-sectionally their latent correlation falls from .50 to a non-significant .18, and in a two-wave latent change model their correlated change falls from .43 to .24; its mediating role is shown in correlated change over the same six months, not in temporal order *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1323: Under weak local noise a many-body operator decays at a rate proportional to its size, so a Hamiltonian's small-sized integrals of motion, which chaotic dynamics does not spread, decay slowly while generic operators, which it spreads, decay fast; in exact diagonalization of Ising and Heisenberg chains of up to nine sites at weak depolarizing noise, the slowest Lindbladian eigenoperators are linear combinations of the known exact and approximate small integrals of motion, and which approximate ones rank among the slowest moves with the noise strength *(used by 3; also will-organization)*
- THEORY-1327: As Ryan and colleagues' 2022 meta-review maps it, the meta-analytic evidence for self-determination theory is concentrated in cognitive evaluation, organismic integration and basic needs theory, is mostly cross-sectional and heterogeneous, and has gaps: no meta-analysis of relationships motivation theory or of need frustration, one or two of causality orientations and goal contents, and none that separates integrated from identified regulation *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1338: In the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale as Chen et al. built it, the distinction between satisfaction and frustration coincides with item direction: every satisfaction item states a positive experience and every frustration item an aversive one, so the better fit of six factors over three, which is the scale's evidence that frustration is a separate dimension, is also what a keying or valence factor would produce *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1345: In three cross-sectional studies of undergraduates, most of the variance in adult attachment security lay within persons, across relational partners (56–79%, error included), and relationship-specific satisfaction of the needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness predicted relationship-specific security in every relationship tested, also with the relatedness items removed; relatedness was the strongest unique predictor, then autonomy, then competence *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1346: In rat cortical slices with synapses blocked, extracellular fields of the local field potential's size, applied by an electrode, shift the membrane potential of layer 5 pyramidal neurons by less than 0.5 mV at frequencies up to 100 Hz and, with spiking driven by current, phase-lock spike times without changing spike counts, most effectively for slow fields, and synchronize nearby neurons; the authors explain the effect by Kirchhoff's circuit laws and a fixed firing threshold *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1347: In Patrick, Knee, Canevello and Lonsbary's three correlational studies, perceiving that a romantic partner fulfils one's needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness goes with better relationship quality, with relatedness the strongest unique predictor and the partner's fulfilment adding to one's own; but the measure does not separate the needs, its autonomy and competence subscales correlating .96 once corrected for unreliability *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1349: In two cross-lagged panel studies of university students, a negatively worded self-report of need frustration predicted later depressive symptoms (standardized β .13 to .18 over three lags) and later negative affect, net of earlier depression and negative affect, while negative affect did not predict later depression; depression also predicted later need frustration at one lag of two *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1350: The Persona Selection Model holds that pre-training gives a language model a distribution over personas, that post-training updates it into a posterior over Assistant personas which runtime context keeps conditioning, and that the Assistant's traits are a key determiner of behaviour; it disowns a single coherent persona and exhaustiveness, and names as open a router that selects personas and could carry goals no persona has *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- THEORY-1352: In Van Lange and Bergmann's model, human cooperation is readily sustained between individuals, above all in dyads, through precise reciprocity, empathy and a partner who cannot be excluded at no cost, and is fragile between groups: categorization alone yields mistrust and in-group favouritism by bounded reciprocity, observed out-group favouritism hardens it into distrust, and chiefly negative interdependence, real or perceived, turns that into costly competition, aggression and hate, so that the processes that build in-group cooperation can fuel intergroup conflict *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1388: De Oliveira, de Sá and Martins give multi-period forms of the FLEET and local-reliability expected covering models, letting ambulances move among bases between periods, and trade the number of bases against coverage as a bi-objective problem, for Belo Horizonte's emergency medical service *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1392: Chou, Chua, Teo and Zheng report that Jordan and Graves found by simulation that limited flexibility configured as a chain gives most of the expected sales of full flexibility, and prove that for balanced plants with independent, identically distributed symmetric demand the long chain keeps about 89.6% (uniform) and 96% (normal, coefficient of variation 0.33) of full flexibility's expected sales as the system grows, a smaller share of its gain over dedicated plants, and less for more variable demand *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1394: Larson and Odoni's hypercube model represents an urban emergency service's N distinguishable units, each busy or free, as a Markov chain on the vertices of an N-cube under fixed-preference dispatch from point sources of Poisson calls, and from its steady state computes each unit's workload, the inter-district dispatch fractions and the mean travel times *(used by 3; also readiness)*
- THEORY-1395: Kaelbling, Littman and Cassandra restate, citing Smallwood and Sondik among others, that for a finite-state Markov process controlled through noisy observations the probability distribution over states is a sufficient statistic for control, show that the optimal value with finitely many steps left is the upper surface of finitely many linear functions of that distribution, hence piecewise-linear and convex, and credit Sondik with the first exact finite-horizon algorithm, whose worst case is exponential *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1396: Mukhopadhyay and colleagues present static coverage models for emergency response as moving from deterministic models that treat a facility as always available, through multiple coverage as a partial hedge against busy stations, to probabilistic models that represent station availability explicitly, beginning with the maximum expected covering and maximum availability models *(used by 3; also readiness)*
- THEORY-1416: van Leeuwaarden, Mathijsen and Zwart report that Halfin and Whitt showed that in a many-server queue with Poisson arrivals and exponential service the probability that an arrival waits tends to a value strictly between zero and one exactly when the number of servers exceeds the offered load by a multiple of its square root, and that the scaled number in system then tends to a diffusion that is a negative-drift Brownian motion above full occupancy and an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process below it; they prove the limit of the waiting probability under that scaling *(used by 2; also readiness)*
- THEORY-1474: Heins, Unrau and Avram, following Mauss, hold that a gift carries no legal guarantee of return yet obliges one, and that an unreturned gift leaves the recipient inferior and poisons the relation; they report Dillon's reading of the Marshall Plan in France, whose recipients, unable to repay, responded with resentment, and his proposal that circular (kula-like) reciprocity that lets the recipient give back is the better design for aid between nations *(used by 2; also transient-support)*
- THEORY-1531: Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy propose that communication be treated as transduction, the continuity of an action through processes that it transforms, rather than as exchange between parties, with meaning the contribution an action makes, in retrospect, to a joint individuation and coexisting meanings the mark of concurrent individuations, and they assert that the problem of scaling agency from individual to collective then vanishes *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- THEORY-1535: Bencherki and Iliadis propose that persons and organizations are not successive stages of individuation, with the collective built up from individuals, but coexisting informational levels that one action can reorder at once, each preserving the characteristics of its organized components, so that scaling up from individual to organizational action is neither a sequence of steps nor a synthesis *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1562: Cottingham reports that the third lecture of Scheffler's Death and the Afterlife holds that a life must be temporally bounded for its goods to have the status of values, so that personal immortality is no remedy, and that among the commentators Frankfurt doubts the concern for humanity's continuation is altruistic and Wolf denies that impending extinction would or should undercut our projects *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1563: Thorstad argues that on simple models of existential risk higher risk does not raise, and in most variants lowers, the value of reducing it, so that high risk this century is compatible with astronomical value for mitigation only if risk falls soon and stays very low, and that three arguments offered for such a time of perils, from wisdom, an existential risk Kuznets curve and space settlement, are weak, leaving aside the argument from advanced AI *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1565: Luper argues that Epicurus's case that death is nothing to us needs intrinsic hedonism and a narrow view of extrinsic harm, that without them death can harm by depriving one of goods, and reports Pitcher's preferentialist view that posthumous events harm the living person by thwarting desires held while alive, a view the entry shows contested *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1566: Tarsney argues that the chance an intervention's effect is nullified acts as an exponential discount, so that under expectational utilitarianism and deliberately pessimistic inputs existential-risk reduction beats a strong global-health benchmark only if nullifying events are rare, and its robust win rests, on some views, on probabilities of order 10^-18 or less *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1567: MacAskill, Thomas and Vallinder factor the change in value an event makes through a feature of the world as significance times persistence times contingency, give its marginal, ex ante and alternative forms, and place it as an estimate of the importance factor of the importance, tractability and neglectedness framework *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1568: Meyer argues that a threshold notion of harm lets a weakly person-affecting view state harms to future people despite the non-identity problem, best specified as weakly sufficientarian, and that such a view gives no reason to prefer a flourishing future to none, a gap he fills with concerns that rest on what present and past people value and an obligation owed to them *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1569: Gardiner argues that climate change joins a global commons problem to an intergenerational one that institutions and reciprocity cannot solve, because the generations do not coexist, and that these, with our theories' weakness, leave each generation open to moral corruption that hides its exploitation of its temporal position, even from itself *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1570: Miyazono and Inarimori argue that self–other merging is best read as group identification, so that in empathic helping the other's welfare becomes a constituent of one's first-person plural welfare, and the helping is altruistic at the individual level and egoistic at the group level *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1571: Ramsey argues that a community that lives for ever and does not discount later enjoyments should save at the rate at which saving times the marginal utility of consumption equals the shortfall of present net enjoyment from Bliss, a rule independent of the interest rate, and he calls discounting later enjoyments ethically indefensible, a product of the weakness of the imagination *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1572: Johnston withdraws the account of his Surviving Death, on which our deepest future-directed attitudes fix which future embodiments are ours, arguing that every reductionist account of personal identity breeds fellow travelers with moral status, and holds instead that we are essentially embodied wills whose present embodiments are not essential *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1573: Klein and colleagues report that in seventeen labs and 1,550 participants writing about one's own death did not raise preference for a pro-US over an anti-US essay author (g = 0.07, 95% CI −0.03 to 0.17), whether or not the protocol was designed with the original authors *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1574: Bostrom argues that on aggregative, time-neutral views of value reducing existential risk is a global priority, and that it is undersupplied for lack of motivation as well as understanding, since its benefit is a pan-generational public good whose future beneficiaries cannot pay and moral sentiment is insensitive to scope *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1575: Narveson argues that creating a person neither benefits nor harms them, that the existence of people with good lives is normally good and a reason to create them though no one is owed it, and that only harm to actual persons can justify coercion over procreation *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1576: Heard and Martienssen argue that an effect is transgenerational only in a generation never exposed to the trigger, and that two rounds of epigenetic reprogramming in mammals leave little chance for such inheritance, which is well documented in plants and nematodes and rare in mammals *(used by 1)*
