- THEORY-1577: Scheffler argues that the survival of other people after one's death is a condition of much of what matters to us mattering, and matters to us in its own right, and reads this as our dependence on future people rather than altruism toward them *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1578: Stich argues that Sober and Wilson's evolutionary arguments from parental care give no evidence for psychological altruism, the strongest of them failing if hedonism rests on sticky sub-doxastic beliefs, which would make it as reliable as an ultimate desire for the child's welfare, and holds that evolutionary and psychological altruism are logically independent *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1579: Syropoulos et al. report that felt responsibility to future generations is endorsed by most people in Europe and the US, is nearly unrelated to ideology and demographics and half as tied to conservatism as responsibility for climate, predicts self-reported proenvironmentalism, and was raised a little by each of five brief interventions, most by a letter to a person born today and least by a longtermist text *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1580: Spears and Postmes state the SIDE model: anonymity and immersion in a group do not remove the self but make the salient identity more salient, so behaviour follows the group's norms more closely under a salient group identity and moves away from them under a salient personal one, and anonymity to a powerful out-group frees in-group-normative behaviour it would punish *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1581: Swann, Gómez, Seyle, Morales and Huici report that a single pictorial item picks out a distinct, group-specific class of Spanish participants fused with Spain, and that challenging or activating a fused person's personal self raised their stated willingness to fight and die for the group while leaving the nonfused unchanged, which they read as personal and social identity being functionally equivalent in the fused *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1582: Kilduff, Elfenbein and Staw report that rivalry among NCAA men's basketball teams, rated by student sportswriters, varied mostly with the particular pair of teams, grew with proximity, similarity, repeated play and above all a history of even contests, and was largely reciprocated, one-sided rivalry running from lower-status to higher-status teams *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1583: Leach and colleagues report that in-group identification among Dutch students has five components on two correlated higher-order dimensions, group-level self-definition and self-investment, and that faced with their group's misdeeds, self-definition predicted group-based guilt while self-investment predicted legitimizing the misdeed *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1585: Kruse and Schmitt, following McAdams, hold that generativity springs from cultural demand and an inner desire that includes a need for symbolic immortality, that its motives can be selfish or altruistic so that it is not altruism, and report, without statistics, that it predicted life satisfaction in older adults and rose in intergenerational projects *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1587: Jawaid and Mansuy argue that in rodents parental trauma, stress and drugs pass behavioural phenotypes to offspring through the germline, with non-coding RNA in sperm the best-described candidate carrier, while granting that how effects pass beyond the first generation is unclear and that germline dependence is not established in humans *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1589: Pinter and Greenwald report that four minimal-group inductions produced comparable explicit in-group liking and identification, and the three compared on it comparable allocation favouritism, that only memorizing one group's names produced large implicit self-association with and preference for that group, and that implicit self-association and liking were related but separable *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1590: Markus and Kitayama propose that cultures construe the self as independent or interdependent, that for the interdependent self others are included within the self's boundaries without a merging of self and other, and that the construal shapes cognition, emotion and motivation *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1591: Wade-Benzoni, Sondak and Galinsky report that framing an intergenerational decision as leaving burdens rather than using up benefits raised legacy concern, felt responsibility and affinity toward future generations, and that people kept more of a benefit than of a burden for themselves when the other party would receive it in the future, though no study measured legacy concern and allocation together *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1592: Smith and Mackie hold that identifying with a group makes it an aspect of the self through self-categorization, so that events are appraised for what they mean to the group and emotions are felt on its behalf, with the emotion shifting with the salient membership and identification moderating it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1593: Heijmans and colleagues report that people conceived during the Dutch Hunger Winter had, about six decades later, slightly lower methylation of the imprinted IGF2 gene in blood than their same-sex siblings, while people exposed only late in gestation showed no difference *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1594: Costa, Yetter and DeSomer report that sons born after the Civil War to Union soldiers held as prisoners when exchanges had stopped had about 1.11 times the older-age mortality hazard of non-prisoners' sons, with no effect on daughters, and favour an epigenetic route by elimination without measuring one *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1595: Rubin and Hewstone report, from a count of experiments on social identity theory's self-esteem hypothesis, that intergroup discrimination tends to raise self-esteem but is not in general motivated by low self-esteem, so the hypothesis is not supported in its full and unqualified form, and that most tests measured global personal self-esteem where the theory implies specific social state self-esteem *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1596: Pembrey, Saffery and Bygren report that in the Överkalix cohorts a paternal grandparent's mid-childhood food supply was associated, sex-specifically, with grandchildren's mortality, and argue from the exposure's sensitive period that cultural or genetic inheritance alone is unlikely to explain it, while granting that replication is needed *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1597: Volkan argues, from clinical work and facilitated dialogues, that a large group's shared image of an ancestral injury at the hands of an enemy, real or mythologized, changes function across generations into a marker of the group's identity, a chosen trauma, which a threat to that identity brings up, and that a recent trauma still mourned, like the Holocaust, is not one *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1598: Reimer, Schmid, Hewstone and Al Ramiah present self-categorization as placing oneself in a social category, hierarchical in level and salient by accessibility and fit, and social identification as a separate, multidimensional relation to the group whose components need not covary, and conclude that these identity processes alone do not explain negative intergroup attitudes *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1599: Wickersham et al. report that writing about one's legacy, or about a loved place under climate change, raised pro-environmental intentions and hypothetical donations by small amounts that did not differ by age, and that each task raised both legacy motivation and love of nature, which in a model with both mediators carried at least as much of the legacy task's donation effect *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1600: Sandoval-Obando and colleagues report that in 430 Chilean teachers a 14-item Spanish Loyola Generativity Scale has three factors, a three-item Generative Legacy factor on symbolic continuity standing apart from Generative Action (r = .45), from an analysis they call confirmatory that chooses the number of factors from the data *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1601: Levin and Shomrat report, in an announcement without data, that planarians trained to recognise a laser-etched chamber recognised it after head removal and regeneration given a brief refresher, and infer that memory can be stored outside the brain and imprinted on the regenerated one *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1602: Dias and Ressler report that male mice fear-conditioned to an odour before mating had sons and grandsons more sensitive to that odour, and not to another, with more olfactory neurons for its receptor, a change that held in offspring conceived by IVF, and they read what passes as sensitivity to the cue, not fear *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1603: Scheepers and Ellemers present social identity theory: social identity is the part of the self-concept that derives from group membership together with its value and emotional significance, people strive for a positive social identity through favourable comparison with out-groups, and members of low-status groups choose mobility, collective action or social creativity by permeability, legitimacy and stability *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1604: Greaves and MacAskill argue that in the most important decisions facing agents today every near-best option is near-best for the far future and delivers much larger benefits there than in the near future, on expected-value reasoning that they concede needs a zero pure rate of time preference and may fail through fanaticism *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1605: Salice and Miyazono argue that group identification, as philosophers of shared agency use it, runs together two separable processes, adopting the group's perspective and self-transformation into a member, and that self-transformation is a Pushmi-Pullyu representation that describes and motivates at once *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1606: Eyerman argues, in his book's first chapter, that cultural trauma is a loss of identity and meaning in a group rather than an individual wound, and that slavery became the cultural trauma of African Americans in retrospect, for a generation after emancipation, by shared fate rather than by experience or descent *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1607: Blackiston, Shomrat and Levin argue, from learned behaviour reported to survive brain remodelling in metamorphosing insects, regenerating planaria and hibernating mammals, that synaptic plasticity alone does not explain lasting memory, and propose, untested, that a planarian's memory may be stored outside the brain and imprinted on the regenerated one *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1608: Spears argues, reviewing the self-categorization account of social influence, that when a group is internalized as a level of self, influence from in-group members is private acceptance and partly self-influence, bounded by shared identity and stronger from more prototypical members, and that crowd members switch to a group identity rather than lose the self *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1609: Hershfield reviews evidence, mostly from his own studies, that people who feel less similar to their future selves treat them more like strangers and choose less patiently, while directly reported liking and caring for the future self, answered near ceiling, did not predict choice *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1610: Parfit argues that narrow person-affecting principles fail in non-identity and different-number cases, and that a wide person-affecting principle, on which being caused to exist with a life worth living is an intrinsic benefit and an outcome is in one way worse if it benefits people less, solves the non-identity problem and keeps the relation of being better transitive *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1611: Dovidio, Gaertner, Shnabel, Saguy and Johnson report that recategorizing two groups as one removed in-group bias in helping, that White students helped a Black student more when he expressed a common university identity, partly through empathic concern, and that they helped him no more when he expressed a dual identity than when he expressed only his subgroup identity *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1612: Youssef and colleagues review two small parent–child studies and three of stress in pregnancy, report that Holocaust survivors had higher FKBP5 methylation and their offspring lower, and read the studies as accumulating evidence that trauma-related methylation changes pass from parent to child, while naming small samples, cross-sectional designs and unmeasured confounds as weaknesses *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1613: Hirst, Cyr and Merck argue that flashbulb memories make members of a community who learned of an event at a distance into witnesses who can carry its trauma process, and report a study in which most children knew a parent's flashbulb memory of 9/11 and knew it better the more strongly they identified as American *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1614: Bird argues that mammals actively erase epigenetic marks between generations, that no validated mechanism lets the environment instruct a heritable epigenome, and that the human cases most cited, the Swedish famine studies and the Holocaust FKBP5 study, are weak *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1615: Castano, Yzerbyt, Paladino and Sacchi report that in 48 Italian students a reminder of their own death raised identification with Italians, the perceived entitativity of Italians and in-group bias, and propose, without separating it from worldview defence, that a group seen as a real entity lets the self project beyond death *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1616: Hurlstone et al. report that in a threshold climate game 9 of 10 groups reached the target when the saved endowment paid the players the next day, 2 of 10 when it paid for trees for future generations, and 7 of 10 when messages meant to activate the legacy motive were added, with no control message and no manipulation check *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1617: Caviola et al. report that laypeople judge adding a very happy person to a world as good as adding a very unhappy one is bad, prefer larger happy populations with averages fixed but less so as numbers grow, reversing at one billion against ten billion, and tend to favour the higher average when average and total conflict *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1618: Horsthemke argues that human studies of germline epigenetic inheritance can exclude genetic inheritance but not ecological or cultural inheritance, proposes a three-step standard of proof that he grants can hardly be met in humans, and classifies the Dutch Hunger Winter effects as fetal programming *(used by 2)*
- THEORY-1619: Otten reports that minimal-group categorization, with no personal stake in the allocations, reliably produces in-group favouritism alongside a strong pull towards fairness, that projecting the positive personal self onto the new group is a crucial route to it, and that people allowed to pay themselves take the most for themselves and favour the in-group with the rest *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1620: Schubert et al. report that most laypeople judge human extinction bad but not uniquely worse than a catastrophe killing 80%, that the share who judge it uniquely bad rises when the victims are animals or the lost future is pointed out, and in one of two general samples when the catastrophe sterilizes, and that it passes a majority only when the surviving future is described as long and utopian *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1621: Fridman reports that, in a registry sample, women who survived the Holocaust as young children and lost both parents showed more dissociation, less life satisfaction and higher cortisol than matched women six decades later, while their daughters did not differ on any psychological, health or cortisol measure *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1622: Siegel's oral history of the Juggernaut redub dates its making to November 2005 and its posting to 14 February 2006, and relays the film's cowriter's remark that the line was a reshoot addition by the director, but gives no production testimony on why the line was added *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1623: Ord reports that since The Precipice existential risk from climate change has fallen, risk from nuclear war has risen, and risk from pandemics and from AI has moved in no clear direction, so that none of the book's rounded per-century estimates has moved far *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1624: Doris, Stich, Walmsley and Schulz report that Batson's experiments tell against the social-punishment and aversive-arousal versions of egoism, argue that self–other merging would make helping egoistic only as perceived numerical identity, which none of the four merging measures in the 1997 exchange tests, and hold that psychological altruism is not yet established *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1625: Branand, Mashek and Aron report that in close relationships partners experience each other's resources, perspectives and identities as partly their own, that the inclusion-of-other-in-self circle scale is validated as a measure of subjective closeness, and that inclusion shows in cognitive signs such as slower self-judgements on traits where the partner differs and self–partner confusions in memory *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1626: Ord argues that, with value summed over time and no pure time preference, advancing progress is worth an amount that does not grow with the future's duration, while reducing near-term existential risk multiplies the whole future's value like an enhancement, so pure advancements rarely rival existential risk reduction *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1627: Danieli, Norris and Engdahl report that, among 422 adult children of Holocaust survivors, parents' wartime internment was linked to the children's reported impacts only through the parents' post-war victim style, that the post-war family milieu weighed more than wartime history, and that broken generational linkages, among them rarely counting the murdered grandparents as one's own, had the largest total effect *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1629: Chen and colleagues report that the mortality-salience literature, which uncorrected reproduces Burke and colleagues' average effect, shrinks under corrections for publication bias to about r = .18, or to no effect on one method, with true effects so heterogeneous and studies so underpowered that many published effects are likely spurious *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1630: Sugden argues that theories of social preference either fit any choice trivially or cannot represent trust, and that cooperative team reasoning, which intends the common interests of members rather than the collective interest of the team, represents trust and market exchange as joint action for mutual benefit *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1632: Brewer argues that close relationships and group memberships are two distinct forms of social identification by which the individual self is extended to include others, the relational self taking in particular others and the collective self a symbolic group, and that they meet distinct needs rather than one need for belonging *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1633: Bostrom argues that delay in settling the local supercluster loses potential lives at a vast rate, but that on a total, undiscounted view even a small cut in existential risk outweighs any feasible acceleration, while on a person-affecting view, given some chance that people now alive share the cosmic future, safety must be balanced against speed *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1634: Blackiston, Silva Casey and Weiss report that tobacco hornworm caterpillars conditioned in the last larval instar to avoid an odour still avoided it as moths, that residue on the pupal case does not explain the aversion, and that an aversion learned two instars earlier survived larval molts but not metamorphosis *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-1635: Zahavi argues, reconstructing Husserl, that seeing oneself as one of us requires second-person address and taking over the other's perspective on oneself, which keeps the self–other difference while downplaying it, and that a we is not an enlarged I *(used by 1)*

## Will-organization

- THEORY-027: Two individually decisive people, weak Pareto and an unrestricted domain cannot all hold, even when choice need only yield a best element; unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, organizational-affect, formal-apparatus, authenticity)*
- THEORY-046: Expected tangible rewards for merely engaging in an interesting task lower later free-choice engagement with it *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-053: A treatment's efficacy is not evidence for its theory of change: only change in the theorised process that is specific and comes before the outcome bears on it, and moving the process without moving the outcome counts against the theory *(used by 1)*
- THEORY-068: In a two-alternative choice made by two competing leaky accumulators, the decision is optimal only when leak and mutual inhibition balance, so that the network integrates the difference of the evidence without loss; imbalance bounds accuracy at any fixed time and weights early or late evidence *(used by 7; also distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-121: Moral responsibility requires guidance control, moderate reasons-responsiveness of the agent's own actual-sequence mechanism, and not regulative control over alternative possibilities, so responsibility is compatible with causal determinism *(used by 4; also authenticity)*
- THEORY-127: On the court agenda, and on any agenda in which every proposition reaches every other by conditional entailment and some minimally inconsistent triple stays consistent with two of its members negated, a group whose judgments are robustly rational under universal domain and respect unanimity cannot form its judgment on each proposition from its members' judgments on that proposition alone unless one member dictates; its judgments must supervene on the members' whole sets of judgments, and so can depart from what the members judge on the same proposition while being wholly fixed by them *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-132: Stability, a system's speed of return to equilibrium after disturbance, and resilience, its capacity to absorb change and persist within its domain of attraction, are distinct properties that can trade off, so a system can be highly unstable and highly resilient, and managing it for constancy can erode its resilience *(used by 4; also nucleating-argument, distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-134: Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time *(used by 12; also nucleating-argument, distributed-agency, realizability, readiness)*
- THEORY-138: X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport, distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-140: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board found that the institutional causes of the Challenger accident had not been fixed and recurred in Columbia's: in both, evidence that the design was not performing as expected was repeatedly reinterpreted as acceptable, each decision seeming correct in itself and each survived anomaly justifying the next flight, while budget and schedule pressure, consensus sign-off, a hierarchy that kept dissent from rising and a safety organization dependent on the program it oversaw sustained the pattern for twenty years and undid post-Challenger reforms *(used by 6; also organizational-normativity, distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-149: Users can govern a shared resource durably without either privatisation or central control, and the institutions that last are marked not by particular rules but by structural regularities: user-made and user-monitored rules, graduated sanctions, cheap local conflict resolution, recognised rights to self-organise, and nested layers of governance *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-285: In an illustrative active-inference simulation of post-traumatic context inference, run once per phenotype, a prior that one is in a harmful context, made overly precise by a run of harmful trials under the "vulnerable" learning and forgetting weights, makes exploratory sampling look uninformative, so the agent attenuates the periphery, never receives the evidence that would correct the prior, and the belief sustains itself; lowering precision makes the attenuation policy less vigorous without correcting the prior, and the policy returns when precision is restored *(used by 5; also distributed-agency)*
- THEORY-654: For full-state linear-quadratic regulation of a single-input plant, the return-difference identity keeps the sensitivity at or below 1 at every frequency, so the loop tolerates any gain increase, a gain cut to one half and at least 60° of phase error for any Q ≥ 0 and r > 0; the guarantee does not carry over when the state is replaced by an observer's estimate *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-688](../record/theory.d/THEORY-688.md): In an actor-critic learner that can choose temporally extended options as well as primitive actions, options that fit the task speed learning, while options with ill-placed subgoals slow it, and options that fit an earlier layout keep the agent from finding a newly opened shortcut, so hierarchy helps only with the right subroutines *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-820](../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md): For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement *(used by 8; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-843](../record/theory.d/THEORY-843.md): Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern's approximate abstraction error, the least over surjective context maps of the worst case over allowed interventions and contexts of the high-level distance between the coarse-grained low-level outcome and the high-level outcome, is zero exactly for τ-abstraction; an abstraction followed by an α-approximation of the high-level model is within α, an α-approximation of the low-level model followed by an abstraction only within kα, k the worst-case ratio of high- to low-level distances, and an approximate abstraction need not factor into an exact abstraction and an approximation *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-848](../record/theory.d/THEORY-848.md): In an acyclic structural equation model, marginalising a variable that no declared intervention sets is an exact transformation, provided the coarse model's exogenous noises may be dependent; so exactness does not require the dropped variable to be causally idle, and it can drop a variable that decides how its children respond to an intervention that is declared *(used by 5; also formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-849](../record/theory.d/THEORY-849.md): For deterministic causal models with a countable set of allowed interventions, a high-level model reproduces the coarse-grained interventional law of a low-level one for every distribution on contexts exactly when some map τ_U on contexts commutes with every allowed intervention, τ(M_L(u, i)) = M_H(τ_U(u), ω(i)); exactness for one distribution is strictly weaker, since a well-chosen distribution lets unrelated models match, and τ-abstraction and strong abstraction are strictly stronger; the context map is only required to exist, so high-level exogenous variables may carry what the coarse state drops *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-897](../record/theory.d/THEORY-897.md): In Brown, Price and Dombrovski's reading of seven computational learning studies they selected without a systematic search, with mixed directions, anxiety goes with altered adjustment of learning rate to uncertainty, mostly for aversive outcomes, while overall learning rate, choice consistency and outcome valuation show little relation to it *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-900](../record/theory.d/THEORY-900.md): A systematic review of 116 studies of avoidance learning in healthy humans finds the evidence contradicting two-factor and other associative theories and favouring expectancy and inference-based accounts, but also finding residual avoidance after the outcome is visibly removed, which a purely inferential account does not predict *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-901](../record/theory.d/THEORY-901.md): As Mancinelli and Bach's systematic review of avoidance learning in healthy humans reports it, rating both A, an avoidance response left available during extinction persists, in some participants for hundreds of unpunished trials, and keeps expectancy of the aversive outcome higher than in people denied it (nine studies); and less effective or costlier responses extinguish faster (six studies, one exception) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-903](../record/theory.d/THEORY-903.md): In a 2026 meta-analysis of standalone safety-behaviour manipulations outside exposure, mostly with young non-clinical or subclinical adults and mostly on appearance concerns and social anxiety, reducing safety behaviours lowered symptoms relative to control (d = 0.43, about 0.31 after adjustment for publication bias), and instructed increases raised them (d = 0.65, five studies) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-904](../record/theory.d/THEORY-904.md): Gollwitzer and Sheeran (2006) conclude, narratively from a handful of studies that measured or manipulated the goal intention, that implementation intentions affect performance only when the goal intention they serve is strong and activated, so the planned response is not elicited mechanically by its cue; in 2024, across eight tests, plan effects were larger with strong, activated or self-concordant goal intentions than with weak, unactivated or self-discordant ones (d = .79 for the difference), and in 31 physical-activity tests split at the median of intention, planning helped with strong intentions (d = .31) and had no effect with weak ones (d ≈ 0) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-907](../record/theory.d/THEORY-907.md): As Chou, Wilson and Smith review them, in about six foraging studies, mostly sub-clinical, higher stress or anxiety went with less exploration, and in one task with a predator to check for (Trier et al. 2023), people higher in trait somatic anxiety checked less and did worse, a reduction the study's further analyses associated with greater aversion to detecting the predator *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-908](../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md): Between tests, uncorrected for publication bias, implementation intentions in the contingent if-then format had larger effects than plans that schedule when, where and what without linking cue to response (d = .43 against .29); tests in which the plan was rehearsed had larger effects (.45 against .33, with no gain beyond one rehearsal), tests in which it was recorded had smaller ones (.31 against .44), and adding how or for how long to a time and place went with about half the effect (.24 against .46) *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-909](../record/theory.d/THEORY-909.md): As reviewed by Gerstner et al. (2018) from five papers, mostly in slices and one laboratory per region, pairing pre- and postsynaptic activity changed the synapse when a neuromodulator or plateau potential followed within about 1 s in striatum, within 5 s (noradrenaline, LTP after pre-before-post pairing) or 2.5 s (serotonin, LTD after post-before-pre pairing) in visual and prefrontal cortex, and within about 2 s in CA1, and not at longer delays; the reviewers read this as a decaying synaptic eligibility trace and as experimental support for three-factor learning rules on behavioural time scales *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-910](../record/theory.d/THEORY-910.md): Brown, Price and Dombrovski propose, without a model run or data, that in aversive environments avoiding uncertain states keeps their uncertainty high and so perpetuates avoidance, that anxiety strengthens this loop by misreading noise as change, and that exposure works by reducing the uncertainty rather than an excess of learned threat *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-912](../record/theory.d/THEORY-912.md): In a picture-based avoidance task, treatment-seeking patients with OCD or PTSD avoided a safety cue more than healthy controls and, after effective avoidance, still expected the aversive picture more; patients with panic disorder with agoraphobia or PTSD reported more relief when it was omitted; the groups did not differ in avoiding the danger cues *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-913](../record/theory.d/THEORY-913.md): In small fixed-effect meta-analytic pools without correction for publication bias, responses specified in if-then plans ran more immediately (d = .77, k = 7), held up under a concurrent cognitive load (d = .85, k = 7) and ran without conscious intent (d = .72, k = 3) compared with responses under a goal intention alone, and the planned cues were detected, attended to and remembered better (d = .80, k = 6); the authors read this as control of the response handed in advance to the cue *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-915](../record/theory.d/THEORY-915.md): In Zorowitz, Momennejad and Daw's simulations of a Markov decision process, an agent that evaluates actions as if it will fail to avoid danger at later steps, while in fact choosing optimally at each step, spreads threat value to states far from the danger and avoids early and widely, which reproduces qualitatively exaggerated threat appraisal, fear generalization and several laboratory findings associated with anxiety *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-917](../record/theory.d/THEORY-917.md): Chou, Wilson and Smith read about eight computational studies of exploration in reward-based bandit tasks, mostly in sub-clinical samples, with mixed results and none replicated, as suggesting that directed exploration rises with trait or cognitive anxiety and falls with state or somatic anxiety; none they review links random exploration to anxiety *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-918](../record/theory.d/THEORY-918.md): Across 642 experimental tests to September 2019, forming implementation intentions improved outcomes, with uncorrected effects on behaviour (d = .27), cognitive performance (.47), affect regulation (.66) and social judgement (.52), but publication bias was substantial: the pooled d = .36 falls to a model-averaged d = .15 under robust Bayesian meta-analysis, which still found extreme evidence of an effect (BF10 = 319), with large heterogeneity *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-920](../record/theory.d/THEORY-920.md): As Mancinelli and Bach's systematic review reports it, rating it B, in three laboratory studies of healthy humans a signalled, costless avoidance response offered for a stimulus never paired with the aversive outcome was used, and withdrawing it raised expectancy of the outcome for that stimulus, though Xia et al. (2019) found no change in skin conductance or startle; every study signalled the response's availability, which may itself have read as a danger cue *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-921](../record/theory.d/THEORY-921.md): As Craske et al.'s 2014 review reports it, citing six studies and reporting no data of its own, how far fear falls during an extinction or exposure session, or across sessions, does not predict how much fear is expressed at follow-up, in animals, human laboratory samples and fearful, mostly analog, human samples *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-922](../record/theory.d/THEORY-922.md): Among 56 of 88 patients in one DBT intensive outpatient programme, kept because they finished a four-month cycle and gave enough diary data, skills-homework completion in months 1–3 correlated with larger falls in suicide and substance-use urges (r ≈ .35) and phone-coaching frequency with a larger fall in self-harm urges (r = .31); neither correlated with change in how often the behaviours occurred, and only homework separated patients with and without a target behaviour in month 4 *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-923](../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md): In one simulated T-maze task with hand-set parameters, run once per condition, an active inference agent's habit, learned by counting its own state transitions and policy choices, emerged from goal-directed behaviour, and once acquired it persisted, and reinforced itself, after the reward was devalued, while an agent devalued before acquisition switched at once *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-962](../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md): In a finite partial-monitoring game, the signals of a set D of actions determine the expected loss difference of actions i and j under every outcome distribution iff ℓ_i − ℓ_j lies in the sum of the row spaces of their signal matrices; when it does not, two outcome distributions differing along a vector in the common kernel give every action in D the same signal law and reverse the preference between i and j, so no amount of play restricted to D can learn the comparison *(used by 4; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-963](../record/theory.d/THEORY-963.md): The minimax regret of every finite partial-monitoring game against an oblivious adversary, degenerate and duplicate actions included, is 0 when no two actions are neighbours, Θ̃(√n) when every pair of neighbours is locally observable, Θ(n^2/3) when every pair is globally but some pair is not locally observable, and linear otherwise; its lower bounds are proved against stochastic outcomes, so the same four classes hold for them *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-988](../record/theory.d/THEORY-988.md): In an attention-only transformer without layer norm or biases, once every attention pattern is held at its value on the input, the logits are exactly a sum of end-to-end path terms, a direct path from embedding to unembedding, one term per head and one per chain of heads composed through their values, and each head's attention scores are a bilinear form in the tokens through which earlier heads can enter on the query side, the key side or both *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1096](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md): Blackwell's comparison of experiments, its easy direction: an experiment is a family of distributions indexed by a common parameter, and if one experiment is a garbling of another by a Markov kernel, every risk attainable with the garbling in any decision problem with bounded losses is attainable with the original, on any outcome spaces *(used by 12; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-1110](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md): Shenhav, Botvinick and Cohen propose that control is allocated top-down by a dedicated specifying system: dACC computes the expected value of a control signal, its probability-weighted payoff less an intrinsic cost rising with intensity, and specifies the signal that lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1117](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1117.md): Ainslie proposes that self-control over time needs no faculty of will: hyperbolic discounting makes preferences that dominate at different delays, these grow into interests that bargain with no governor above them, and resolve is the recursive staking of expected future choices on the present one *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1118](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1118.md): McKenna and Coates argue, with Dryden and with Buss and Westlund, that a condition on free agency stated only in the agent's present psychological structure is met by an agent whose structure a manipulator installed, so a mesh account must count that agent free or add a historical condition; Frankfurt, read first-hand, takes the first option *(used by 4; also authenticity, organizational-normativity)*
- [THEORY-1264](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1264.md): Far from equilibrium, the weak-noise escape rate from an attractor goes as the exponential of minus system size times a barrier in the quasi-potential, not in any free energy, and that barrier is bracketed by thermodynamics: it is at most the entropy produced in relaxing from the saddle into the attractor and at least minus the entropy produced along the most likely escape path; the two bounds coincide at detailed balance and separate by twice the dissipation of the probability circulation, so far from equilibrium they can be very loose *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1303](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1303.md): For an uncertain linear program, a decision fixed before the data are revealed must satisfy every realization at once (the robust counterpart, ∃ solution ∀ data), while a decision that may adjust after them need only have a feasible adjustment for each (the adjustable robust counterpart, ∀ data ∃ adjustment); the second is never more conservative and can be feasible where the first is not, the two coincide when each constraint's uncertainty is its own, and decisions may be restricted between them by what part of the data they read or by the form of the rule *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1306](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1306.md): Juarrero, restating the hierarchy theory of Salthe, Allen and Starr, and Allen, O'Neill and Hoekstra, holds that boundaries between levels of organization are typically marked by sharp discontinuities in order parameters and average process and relaxation rates, overarching levels being usually slower than their components; that levels relate by constraint, not energy exchange, because the faster level's dynamics complete before the slower level's feedback arrives; and that a lack of asymmetry in cycling rates between levels reflects the absence of control constraint by one on the other, regardless of signal amplitude, and of qualitative difference between them *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1309](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1309.md): For a small-noise diffusion the Freidlin–Wentzell quasi-potential equals 2 inf ∫ |b| sin²(θ/2) ds over curves, θ the angle between curve and drift, and the minimizing curve is the path a noise-driven transition follows with probability tending to one; with gradient drift and identity noise that curve runs against the drift, the time-reversed relaxation path, while a far-from-gradient drift, as in the Maier–Stein model above β = 4, makes it depart from the heteroclinic orbit *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1323](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1323.md): Under weak local noise a many-body operator decays at a rate proportional to its size, so a Hamiltonian's small-sized integrals of motion, which chaotic dynamics does not spread, decay slowly while generic operators, which it spreads, decay fast; in exact diagonalization of Ising and Heisenberg chains of up to nine sites at weak depolarizing noise, the slowest Lindbladian eigenoperators are linear combinations of the known exact and approximate small integrals of motion, and which approximate ones rank among the slowest moves with the noise strength *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1332](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1332.md): In Bishop's account, chaos is a property of deterministic dynamics, so sensitive dependence is not indeterminism; under determinism it may model deliberation but is not sufficient for incompatibilist freedom, and under indeterminism the incompatibilist (Kane) must still show that agents can harness amplified indeterminism; and amplification itself may fail, since damping, the sign of the local Lyapunov exponents when a perturbation arrives, and the brain's parallel redundancy limit it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1341](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md): In Jennings's hybrid account, attention is prioritization of processing by a subject that is the whole collection of an organism's fixed, formed and fluid interests, separated from filtering by whether selection answers to that collection, marked by feedback from dorsolateral prefrontal cortex; when interests are equally weighted, attention breaks the stalemate and updates the chosen option's value, so that a fluid interest becomes a formed one *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1344](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1344.md): Empowerment is the channel capacity from an agent's next n actions to its sensor n steps later, an open-loop, interventional measure of how many perceptibly different futures the agent can bring about, which counts no control the agent cannot perceive; given side information about the channel's state it is never lower, so it is ordered by what the agent can read, from full state through its own sensor history to none *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1348](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1348.md): In Froese's Irruption Theory an agent's motivations make a difference to behaviour only as an increase in its material underdetermination, measurable at best indirectly as neural or behavioural entropy, and such irruptions are by the theory's own terms undirected: scaled up by chaos, 1/f noise or criticality, they loosen the current organization but "cannot force the formation of the behavior that is to come", so the theory places behaviour's direction in the body's attunement and not in the irruption *(used by 1)*

## Normative judgment about organizations

- [THEORY-012](../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md): An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality *(used by 8; also pragmatic-transport, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-140](../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md): The Columbia Accident Investigation Board found that the institutional causes of the Challenger accident had not been fixed and recurred in Columbia's: in both, evidence that the design was not performing as expected was repeatedly reinterpreted as acceptable, each decision seeming correct in itself and each survived anomaly justifying the next flight, while budget and schedule pressure, consensus sign-off, a hierarchy that kept dissent from rising and a safety organization dependent on the program it oversaw sustained the pattern for twenty years and undid post-Challenger reforms *(used by 6; also will-organization, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1118](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1118.md): McKenna and Coates argue, with Dryden and with Buss and Westlund, that a condition on free agency stated only in the agent's present psychological structure is met by an agent whose structure a manipulator installed, so a mesh account must count that agent free or add a historical condition; Frankfurt, read first-hand, takes the first option *(used by 4; also authenticity, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-1119](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1119.md): Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde propose that minimal agency requires individuality, interactional asymmetry and normativity set by the system's own organisation, each necessary and together, they say, sufficient; that individuality without the other two is not agency; and that a system optimizing an externally fixed function is not a model of agency *(used by 6; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1165](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1165.md): Kahl proposes that agency in the sense that bears on responsibility needs a standpoint that settles and carries forward revised evaluative standards when its inherited ones break down, which is absent where revision is imposed from outside, escaped by rollback or chosen by a fixed higher-order rule; that allocating authority among a system's own components coordinates execution without authoring its governing frame; and that planning, autonomy, memory and coordination do not supply that standpoint *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1463](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1463.md): Pritchett, Woolcock and Andrews argue that many low-capability states, at their measured pace of improvement, would take centuries to millennia to reach high state capability, and that the persistence is sustained by two techniques: isomorphic mimicry, keeping legitimacy by imitating the forms of functional organizations without their function, and premature load bearing, loading fledgling organizations with tasks too complex too soon *(used by 1)*

## Organizational affect

- [THEORY-027](../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md): Two individually decisive people, weak Pareto and an unrestricted domain cannot all hold, even when choice need only yield a best element; unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, will-organization, formal-apparatus, authenticity)*
- [THEORY-102](../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md): In Vishne, Gerber, Knight and Deouell's intracranial recordings from ten epilepsy patients viewing clearly visible images for up to 1.5 s, the pattern of high-frequency activity across ventral temporal cortex carried image category, and exemplar identity among 60 images, in a time-invariant code for as long as the image stayed on while amplitude fell about 80%; at the sampled prefrontal and parietal sites, category content was a burst about 150 to 600 ms after onset that did not track duration *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-123](../record/theory.d/THEORY-123.md): In ad hoc groups of students negotiating a bonus, a confederate's randomly assigned pleasant or unpleasant mood spread to the other members, by their self-reports and by blind coders, and the more pleasant mood a group caught, the more cooperative and the less conflicted coders rated it, a correlation with measured contagion rather than a manipulated effect; members' moods also converged without a confederate, and members did not credit their mood for how effective they judged themselves; the numbers are from the 2001 manuscript *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-245](../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md): In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, prefrontal cortex carried a seen image's category but not its identity, and a face's orientation at most weakly, while posterior cortex carried category, face orientation and the identity of objects, letters and false fonts, though not of faces; no prefrontal site showed the preregistered onset-and-offset response, and one, found in an exploratory analysis, responded at offset earlier than predicted *(used by 2; also evidence-for-experience)*
- [THEORY-324](../record/theory.d/THEORY-324.md): A system adapts by trial and error to an environment whose effect on its essential variables it does not know only if a second feedback, through those variables, changes the parameters of its primary feedback; and if that feedback changes them whenever, and for as long as, an essential variable is outside its limits, every equilibrium the whole can reach is an adapted one *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-894](../record/theory.d/THEORY-894.md): A flow of pairwise comparisons on a graph splits orthogonally and uniquely into a gradient part, the l2-best global ranking, and a cyclic part, which splits into curl (local) and harmonic (global) inconsistency; a finite game's flow of unilateral payoff differences has no curl part, so every finite game is uniquely a potential game plus a harmonic game plus a nonstrategic remainder, and potential games are exactly those with no harmonic part; the decomposition is cardinal *(used by 6; also formal-apparatus, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-896](../record/theory.d/THEORY-896.md): A finite game in strategic form has the finite improvement property, every path of strict unilateral improvements being finite, exactly when it has a generalized ordinal potential, a real function on strategy profiles that rises with every strict unilateral improvement; so in a finite game an ordering along which every improving move climbs exists exactly when there is no improvement cycle, and every sequence of improving moves ends at a pure equilibrium *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-902](../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md): In Friedkin, Jia and Bullo's study of 30 four-person student groups discussing 15 choice dilemmas, a member's self-reported closure to influence on the next issue rose with their influence centrality on the previous issue, an effect constant along the sequence, and with their average centrality over all prior issues, an effect that grew along it; influence networks thinned and discussions shortened while the rate of consensus did not change. Closure and centrality both come from the members' own chip allocations, and prior closure is not controlled *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*

## Authenticity and concordance

- [THEORY-027](../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md): Two individually decisive people, weak Pareto and an unrestricted domain cannot all hold, even when choice need only yield a best element; unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, will-organization, organizational-affect, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-121](../record/theory.d/THEORY-121.md): Moral responsibility requires guidance control, moderate reasons-responsiveness of the agent's own actual-sequence mechanism, and not regulative control over alternative possibilities, so responsibility is compatible with causal determinism *(used by 4; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-1118](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1118.md): McKenna and Coates argue, with Dryden and with Buss and Westlund, that a condition on free agency stated only in the agent's present psychological structure is met by an agent whose structure a manipulator installed, so a mesh account must count that agent free or add a historical condition; Frankfurt, read first-hand, takes the first option *(used by 4; also will-organization, organizational-normativity)*

## Contextual pragmatic information transport

- [THEORY-003](../record/theory.d/THEORY-003.md): Maximizing HSIC between representations and image identity maximizes the average squared MMD between the images' view distributions, whose kernel mean embeddings exist by the Riesz representation theorem *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-004](../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md): A representation is determined by its centred kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal transformation, and the rotation-aligned distance between two representations equals the Bures distance between their kernels *(used by 6; also formal-apparatus, distributed-agency, learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-006](../record/theory.d/THEORY-006.md): InfoNCE is a lower bound on mutual information for every critic and can never exceed the log of the batch size *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-007](../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md): Kernel PCA under the positive-pair density ratio recovers the eigenfunctions of the positive-pair Markov chain, and their top span is minimax-optimal for linear prediction of approximately view-invariant targets *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-008](../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md): On a finite set of stimuli, what a regularized linear readout can decode from a representation is a function of its normalized kernel, and CKA, CCA and GULP are averages of readout agreement *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-009](../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md): In the positive-pair spectral self-supervised papers, self-adjointness comes from the symmetry of the positive-pair distribution, not from the Riesz representation theorem; elsewhere in the family it comes from a symmetrized loss, a precondition on the kernel, or composing the conditional-expectation operator with its adjoint *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus, learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-011](../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md): Generalized contextuality is strictly broader than Kochen–Specker contextuality: a qubit already has no preparation-noncontextual model, though no Kochen–Specker argument with sharp measurements exists in dimension two *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-012](../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md): An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality *(used by 8; also formal-apparatus, organizational-normativity)*
- [THEORY-014](../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md): In both formalisms of contextuality, classicality is the existence of a nonnegative version of a linear representation that always exists over the reals, so negativity is universal and only its unavoidability is nonclassical *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-015](../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md): Kochen–Specker noncontextuality is measurement noncontextuality plus outcome determinism for sharp measurements, and preparation noncontextuality implies that determinism, so every Kochen–Specker proof refutes universal generalized noncontextuality while measurement noncontextuality alone is consistent with quantum theory *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-016](../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md): An operational theory admits a generalized-noncontextual model exactly when its GPT admits a positive quasiprobability representation, and for a tomographically local theory any diagram-preserving such model is an exact frame with exactly as many ontic states as the GPT's dimension *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-017](../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md): In a Hilbert-space model only unitarily invariant structure is intrinsic; a basis or tensor factorisation, and so any parts or features, is extra data supplied from outside the space, and the record's Hilbert-space works differ in where they get it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-018](../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md): Softmax training identifies a language model's final-layer representation only up to an invertible linear map, so no inner product on it is intrinsic, and Park, Choe and Veitch's causal inner product is fixed by a stipulation *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-019](../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md): Symmetry forces spectral degeneracy but degeneracy does not identify a symmetry: an operator commuting with a group has eigenspaces built from its real irreducibles, so abelian rotation groups force pairs over ℝ, and the spectrum fixes neither the group nor a basis inside a multiplet *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-020](../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md): Every Boolean algebra is the clopen algebra of its Stone space of prime ideals, and a finite one is the power set of its atoms, so a single Boolean context always has two-valued valuations and the Kochen–Specker obstruction lies in how contexts overlap *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-032](../record/theory.d/THEORY-032.md): The Yoneda lemma determines an object only up to isomorphism, from its whole hom-functor, among objects the category already has; as a formal version of "an object is determined by its relations" it presupposes the relata *(used by 12; also formal-apparatus, realizability)*
- [THEORY-034](../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md): Chakravartty's dilemma reaches only structural realisms that keep relata but deny them every intrinsic identity-fixing feature, and of the seven structural-realist texts read here against it, two are of that kind: Floridi's informational structural realism and Esfeld and Lam's moderate structural realism *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-037](../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md): In the topos programme quantum propositions form a distributive Heyting algebra, not an orthocomplemented lattice, and its negation is a pseudo-complement under which excluded middle can fail *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-041](../record/theory.d/THEORY-041.md): Birkhoff and von Neumann proposed the modular law, not orthomodularity, and proved it fails for closed subspaces in infinite dimension; Husimi used the orthomodular identity only as an unnamed proof step *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-042](../record/theory.d/THEORY-042.md): Under a superselection rule a coherent superposition across sectors is operationally a mixture, because no observable connects the sectors; Wick, Wightman and Wigner proved such a rule for integer versus half-integer spin and only postulated it for charge *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-082](../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md): Steepest descent is defined only relative to a metric, and Amari's proof that natural-gradient learning is Fisher efficient needs the Fisher information at the optimum to be invertible, the condition whose failure WBIC calls singular; in a multilayer perceptron it fails wherever an output weight is zero *(used by 4; also distributed-agency, learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-087](../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md): The Bayesian complexity penalty grows as (d/2) log n in a regular model, where the curvature at the optimum sets the Occam factor, and as λ log n in a singular one, where λ is the real log canonical threshold; with the prior positive on the optimal set, λ falls below d/2 when that set is infinite or has a point of degenerate curvature, and equals d/2 when it is finitely many points of non-degenerate curvature *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-111](../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md): In image classifiers, between two networks linearly connected by spawning from a shared checkpoint or by permutation alignment (MLPs, and VGG-16, ResNet-20 and ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet), nearly every layer's features at three points on the line were proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features, and pairs that were not linearly connected were far from it *(used by 4; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-112](../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md): Aligning independently trained solutions over the architecture's symmetries removed the linear barrier between them for MNIST MLPs and 32×-wide ResNet-20s on CIFAR-10, two-thirds of it for an ImageNet ResNet-50, and not all of it for VGG-16 or ResNet-20 at 1× width, the barrier after weight matching falling with width; for 6- to 8-layer ViTs and GPT-2s, permutations alone removed 63–90% of it, and adding an orthogonal map on the residual stream, learned against the loss at the path's midpoint, took it to zero or near zero except on BookCorpus (0.42) *(used by 5; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-113](../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md): Merging ResNets trained from different initialisations on disjoint halves of a label set by permuting one onto the other and averaging fell far short of the ensemble; their cross-model feature correlation fell with depth, merging only the early layers recovered most of the ensemble's accuracy, and merging features within each model as well as across both helped at 4× width and above; Stoica et al. attribute the failure to features with no counterpart in the other model *(used by 3; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-117](../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md): In Uselis, Dittadi and Oh's two-concept grids, ResNet-50s trained from scratch, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, reach unseen combinations as the share of combinations seen grows and not as up to four times more data of the same combinations is added; and when embeddings are exactly linearly factored, seen pairs that connect every value of both concepts, as two per value arranged in one cycle do, determine the embedding of every unseen pair *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-138](../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md): X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent *(used by 3; also will-organization, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-155](../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md): Iterated learning by Bayesian agents who sample from the posterior converges, in an ergodic chain, to the shared prior *(used by 5; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-156](../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md): For experiments on a finite parameter set whose outcome spaces are standard Borel, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation *(used by 8)*
- [THEORY-158](../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md): For a Markov process on a finite state space, an observable commutes with the generator exactly when its mean and variance are both conserved in every state, which is exactly when it is constant on each connected component of the transition graph, so a conserved mean alone does not give a symmetry *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-160](../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md): In the algebraic Hamiltonian setting, symmetry and conservation correspond because the bracket is antisymmetric, which for a bilinear bracket is each observable conserving itself; the theorem's content lies in identifying observables with generators *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-161](../record/theory.d/THEORY-161.md): In Zhao et al.'s (2025) and Chai et al.'s (2023) semantic rate–distortion frameworks, meaning is a latent variable with a known joint law with the observation, so their limits are indirect source-coding limits; Zhao et al.'s posterior-matching semantic distortion is, with KL divergence, exactly the information bottleneck, and with total variation a bound on the expected lost value of every bounded-loss decision *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-163](../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md): In Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier and Tishby's analysis, the colour-naming systems of the World Color Survey languages and English lie near the information-bottleneck bound for compressing perceptual meanings into words, at a trade-off parameter just above 1 and nearer than hue-rotated variants of themselves, with the need distribution over meanings estimated from the naming data *(used by 3; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-164](../record/theory.d/THEORY-164.md): As Raviv, Meyer and Lev-Ari report it, in a laboratory game where 12 fully connected groups of eight and 12 of four built a new communication system with total interaction held fixed, the larger groups' languages grew more systematic faster, ended more systematic and differed less from one another, while communicative success and convergence did not differ by size; input variability, higher in the larger groups, predicted the next round's gain in structure, an association measured and not manipulated *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-165](../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md): Within a fixed measurement scenario, the non-contextual fraction is the value of a linear programme whose constraint vector is the empirical model's probability table, and the contextual fraction is convex under mixing *(used by 5)*
- [THEORY-166](../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md): In the 66 Pew surveys of 2001–2011 that varied the order of two back-to-back binary questions, question order changed the answers but not the probability of giving the same answer to both, the equality a Lüders projection model predicts for any projectors; a classical model with order events can meet the same equality, so the regularity does not by itself favour quantum over classical probability *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-168](../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md): In Contextuality-by-Default, whether a fixed set of measurements is contextual depends on how the system is represented: which couplings are imposed, and which dichotomizations of the variables are included *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-171](../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md): When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-172](../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md): In Frank and Goodman's one-shot reference games, listeners' mean bets matched a parameter-free listener inverting a speaker who chooses among true utterances by informativeness, with a separately measured salience prior, and not salience alone; and in Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling games with novel symbols, listeners read a signal as excluding what the available alternative would have conveyed *(used by 6)*
- [THEORY-174](../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md): Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a convex map between two scenarios' model sets is induced by a classical non-adaptive procedure exactly when some non-contextual model of the hom scenario that satisfies its predicate induces it *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-175](../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md): Cosine similarities to matched anchor points are unchanged by exactly the maps that preserve each sample's cosines to the anchors, among them every orthogonal map times a positive scalar and every per-sample positive rescaling but not translations; in Moschella et al.'s experiments independently trained encoders agreed in them only approximately, enough for a decoder reading them to transfer untrained between seeds, architectures and languages with loss, while their nearest neighbours mostly differed *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-176](../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md): A task-loss stitching penalty compares representations in one decision problem, through a fixed top network and a restricted map class, so it is not Blackwell's order: representations that are functions of each other can stitch differently, and a negative penalty shows the fitted map did not reproduce the layers it replaced *(used by 6; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-177](../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md): In a binary cyclic system, the Contextuality-by-Default measure of signalling is twice the sum, over contents, of the least direct influence of context that a canonical causal model of the data must place on each content, and each content's least influence is the total-variation distance between its two marginals *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-185](../record/theory.d/THEORY-185.md): When each binary attribute of a word affects its co-occurrence independently and multiplicatively, the PMI is affine in the attributes with rank at most d + 1, so a spectral PMI embedding is a linear image of the attribute hypercube and parallelogram analogies hold exactly; over the full hypercube of words, each attribute's two values equally frequent, the raw co-occurrence ratio mixes in products of attributes, and keeps exact analogies only when the strengths are alike enough that every attribute mode outranks every product mode *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-189](../record/theory.d/THEORY-189.md): Nested angular cones in the Poincaré ball, symmetric about the outward ray with an aperture depending only on the apex's radius, are transitive only if the aperture is at most π/2 and r sin ψ(r)/(1 − r²) does not increase outward; so no such cone can be defined near the origin, the widest admissible family is sin ψ = K(1 − r²)/r, and every point a cone contains lies farther from the origin than its apex *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-193](../record/theory.d/THEORY-193.md): A simplicial complex grown by gluing each new d-simplex to one (d − 1)-face, by a rule that uses no geometry, has a 1-skeleton whose geodesic triangles are 2-thin at every size, so hyperbolic network geometry in Gromov's sense is an outcome of the combinatorial growth; the equal-link drawing as ideal simplices is a convention, a tiling of the hyperbolic plane for d = 2 in the manifold flavor but not a tiling of hyperbolic d-space for d ≥ 3 *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-211](../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md): In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise *(used by 5; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-228](../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md): On a finite augmentation space, at the population optimum of the spectral contrastive loss with k ≥ 2r, linear-probe error is bounded, up to constant and logarithmic factors, by the error of recovering the label from an augmentation divided by the squared sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-230](../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md): The Fisher–Rao geometry of a language model's next-token laws over a set of contexts is a function of those laws alone, so models with identical laws share it, while activation geometry changes under invertible reparameterizations of the hidden layer that leave outputs unchanged; in Picozzi's ten transformer, state-space and recurrent models it agreed at a mean rank correlation of 0.88 against 0.62 for activation geometry, and about 9% of the top eigenvector overlap exceeded a null matched to the shared laws *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-231](../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md): Within classical realism, a generalized-noncontextuality no-go refutes Leibnizian representations, not realist representations as such; it rests on a stronger assumption than a Bell-like no-go and so applies where none exists, as in prepare-measure scenarios, but only Leibnizianity implying noncontextuality is proved *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-239](../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md): For any joint law of an input and a context, symmetric or not, the top-d left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator attain the minimum, over d-dimensional spans, of worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1 − ε, namely (s₁² − (1 − ε)²)/(s₁² − s²_{d+1}) when s_{d+1} < 1 − ε ≤ s₁, though other spans can tie *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-261](../record/theory.d/THEORY-261.md): In sparse distributed memory, recall of uniform random data from exact cues is a signal-to-noise problem whose optimum activates about (2MT)^-1/3 of the hard locations, and capacity then grows in proportion to the number of hard locations, rising toward about a tenth of them at 0.999 bit fidelity, not with the word length *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-270](../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md): In Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise's common-nonsense model, where the source language and the plausibility prior are uniform over sets from which shared random nonsense is removed and translators are one-to-one, maximum likelihood with the prior alone translates without parallel data with error O(log|Θ| / (α·min(m, |T|))) with high probability, falling in the shared nonsense α, in the size of the source language and in the number of samples *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-271](../record/theory.d/THEORY-271.md): In a toy subject–verb–object corpus whose eight subjects carry every combination of three binary aspects, the subjects' raw co-occurrence rows form a parallelepiped if and only if, for each object, its four sentences are equally probable; any other sentence distribution breaks it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-280](../record/theory.d/THEORY-280.md): The bisimulation metric between two finite Markov chains with observed states and a known cost bounded by 1 can be estimated without a transition model from independent samples of each chain's discounted state-pair occupancy, to accuracy ε with probability 1 − δ from a number of samples polynomial in the state-space sizes, 1/(1−γ), log(1/δ) and 1/ε² *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-281](../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md): Perfect concept erasure caps what a representation can keep at the information not about the concept: for X of finite support, if Z is independent of A then I(Z;X) is at most H(X|A), and a deterministic erasure reaches that cap only when the concept groups' distributions are permutations of one another *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-282](../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md): A subspace intervention can reproduce the output effect of changing a variable without localizing it, by pairing a direction that varies with the variable but cannot reach the output with one that can reach the output but does not vary on the data *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-289](../record/theory.d/THEORY-289.md): For ordinary least squares on T ≥ d + 2 isotropic Gaussian covariates reused every round, with each round's labels generated by the previous fit, keeping every earlier round's data keeps the expected excess test error below π²/6 times the first fit's, though it rises every round, where replacing the data makes it grow linearly in the number of rounds *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-315](../record/theory.d/THEORY-315.md): For a state whose four-state reflection orbit is realizable, generalized noncontextuality bounds two binary predictabilities by |⟨X⟩| + |⟨Z⟩| ≤ 1, so the form of a predictability trade-off, not its existence, can witness contextuality *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-319](../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md): When two views are redundant for a label, the predictor that infers one view from the other is within εX + 2√(εXεZ) + εZ of the Bayes predictor in mean squared error, and it is linear in the contrastive density ratio, so for a bounded label and a square-integrable ratio a linear readout of m random evaluations of the exact ratio approaches it at rate 1/m, with no symmetry between the views required *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-335](../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md): Selective accessibility, the account that comparing a target with a plausible anchor makes anchor-consistent knowledge more accessible and that this knowledge carries anchoring, fits the moderations of the effect by applicability, representativeness and plausibility that Strack and Mussweiler found, but its accessibility step is inferred, not measured: Harris et al.'s repetition of the recognition test of it, four times by lexical decision and once by continuous identification, found nothing in five preregistered experiments, with tasks that also missed direct picture priming *(used by 4; also nucleating-argument)*
- [THEORY-337](../record/theory.d/THEORY-337.md): In the comparative-question paradigm, judging whether a quantity is higher or lower than a high or low anchor pulls the later estimate of it toward the anchor, with large effects in five preregistered experiments of 128 people each, lasting through dozens of intervening word-recognition trials *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-405](../record/theory.d/THEORY-405.md): Adding one classifier-free guidance term per concept to a diffusion model's unconditional noise prediction samples images that satisfy several concepts at once without retraining, and on synthetic scenes it composes object positions far better than compositional energy-based models but relations no better; the reading of the summed score as the score of a product of experts holds only for concepts conditionally independent given the image, unit weights, a conservative field and the noise-free distribution *(used by 2)*
