- [THEORY-419](../record/theory.d/THEORY-419.md): In a structural causal model of autonomous equations, with intervention do(X = x) defined, as Pearl defines it, as a surgery that deletes X's own equation, sets X to x and solves the rest, and with observing X = x violating no equation and amounting to ordinary conditioning, models that agree on every observational distribution can disagree on the effect of an intervention, and in a structural equation y = βx + ε the coefficient β is the rate of change of E[Y | do(x)], which equals the regression slope of Y on X only when X is uncorrelated with ε *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-421](../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md): In HGCN embeddings of two synthetic 3-ary trees trained for link prediction or node classification, distance from the origin is only a partial reading of hierarchical level: the root is not innermost (distance 1.8–3.3 against a minimum of 1.2–2.4) and level order is recovered for 69–75% of node pairs; a loss built only on pairwise distances leaves the origin arbitrary *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-439](../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md): Given the same few demonstrations, temporarily updating a language model's weights on them and then conditioning beats conditioning alone, most on tasks with structural rules or distribution shift and most when the update is trained in the in-context format: for models of 1–8B parameters, examples used as context and the same examples used as a training signal are not interchangeable *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-472](../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md): A speaker who chooses words to minimise the information lost about a single intended referent, with words' literal meanings uniform over their extensions, picks each true word with probability inversely proportional to a power of its extension, so the size principle follows from informative communication; in one betting experiment, learners who knew the referent bet on a novel word's meaning in line with the inversion of that speaker (r = .93 on condition means), and in one free-description study speakers' word use followed it only weakly (r = .19) *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-478](../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md): If the diffusion densities' Hellinger distances obey a Hölder bound with exponent θ in d_T / t^(1/β) and are bounded below once d_T exceeds a multiple of t^(1/β), then for 0 < α < θ/β summing scale-weighted hyperbolic distances between diffusion densities over dyadic times gives a distance two-sided equivalent, up to constants, to min{1, d_T^(αβ)} for pairs above the finest scale: it keeps the tree's neighbourhoods and not its global distances; whether a tree's heat kernel, or sampled data, meets the bounds, and with which θ, is not shown *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-481](../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md): Under gradient flow averaged over tasks and data, a linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression learns as a two-layer linear network from an aligned start does: when tasks share the input covariance's eigenbasis and the weights start and stay aligned with it, then in the long-context limit each input mode is learned on its own logistic curve whose timescale falls with the square of its variance, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the layer converges to the estimator preconditioned by the inverse input covariance; at finite context length the modes decouple exactly only when inputs are isotropic and the modes start equal, and otherwise couple at order 1/N *(used by 3; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-489](../record/theory.d/THEORY-489.md): Chains of human function learners, each trained on the previous learner's responses, forget their starting function and in 28 of 32 families converge within a few generations to a positive linear function, the bias earlier studies report, whatever function trained the first learner; this is convergence to the learners' favoured function, not shown to be convergence to their prior *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-496](../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md): In few-shot classification and multiple choice by language models up to 175B parameters, whether each demonstration's label is correct contributes little to the gain over zero-shot, while the distribution of the inputs, the label space and the paired format carry most of it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-516](../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md): For any presheaf of propositions over a small category of contexts, a sieve-valued valuation satisfies the generalized functional-composition condition exactly when it is a subobject of that presheaf, and the construction runs unchanged in classical physics, where every microstate gives a global section yet truth values are still non-Boolean sieves; so the logic of the truth values is fixed by the base category, not by whether a presheaf has global sections *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-522](../record/theory.d/THEORY-522.md): Open text-to-image diffusion models of 2022–2023 render a single named object almost always but fail most on relative position and next on attribute binding, by human rating and by detector checks alike; scaling the image model or continuing pretraining does not fix position, and interactions are rated near ceiling only by rubrics that ask whether an action is depicted *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-545](../record/theory.d/THEORY-545.md): Aerts and Gabora's founding quantum model of concepts is a classical probability model written in a Hilbert space: every context it uses is a projector diagonal in one basis, so the contexts commute and generate a Boolean algebra, its entangled 'pet fish' state gives the same statistics as a classically correlated mixture for every context in the model, and its guppy weights are copied from single-concept ratings rather than predicted for the conjunction *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-559](../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md): In Kolmogorovian probability, joint distributedness is transitive, so representing a measurement by one random variable in every context it occurs in already puts all measurements of a connected system on one probability space; within that representation a Kochen–Specker or Bell contradiction refutes the context-independent identification of measurements, not the existence of a joint distribution *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-602](../record/theory.d/THEORY-602.md): An ergodic source's entropy is the least average rate at which it can be encoded, a noisy channel has a capacity below which any rate can be sent with arbitrarily small error and above which the equivocation cannot fall below the excess, and a source can be reproduced at a given fidelity over a channel exactly when its rate for that fidelity does not exceed the capacity; Shannon rests the justification of entropy on these theorems, not on the axioms that single out −Σ p log p *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-611](../record/theory.d/THEORY-611.md): Classifier-free guidance extrapolates between a conditional and an unconditional score learned by one network; with exact scores this equals classifier guidance by the classifier the generative model defines through Bayes' rule, but learned scores need not be conservative, so the guided field is in general the gradient of no density and the tilted distribution that motivates guidance is not shown to be what is sampled *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-623](../record/theory.d/THEORY-623.md): In the two tests of contextuality in language data that the record has read, the contextuality is put there by the experimenter or not secured: meaning-selection models of ambiguous phrases estimated from corpora are all signalling and their two Contextuality-by-Default verdicts are plausibly noncontextual by their own bootstrap, while BERT's 52 million anaphora models have a support fixed by the sentence schema, so whether each counts as contextual depends only on how uncertain the model's three referent choices are *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-652](../record/theory.d/THEORY-652.md): Over any field, a finite-dimensional associative algebra with no nilpotent two-sided ideal is uniquely a direct sum of simple algebras, and each simple algebra is a full matrix algebra over a division algebra, which over the reals can be the complex numbers or the quaternions *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-668](../record/theory.d/THEORY-668.md): When the encoder is restricted to prunings of one fixed hierarchy of nested partitions, any non-negatively weighted sum of relevant information, irrelevant information and compression decomposes into per-node terms, so a bottom-up recursion finds the unique optimal tree with fewest leaves exactly in linear time, while greedy top-down splitting can miss information lying below a level that carries none; penalising irrelevant information only prunes the information-bottleneck tree *(used by 2; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-683](../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md): Permuting a fixed set of few-shot examples moves a GPT-family model's classification accuracy between near chance and near the supervised state of the art, at every model size tested; the good orders are specific to the model, the spread survives more examples and calibration, and bad orders mostly fail by predicting one label *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-697](../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md): Sparse distributed memory's read weights each stored pattern by the number of hard locations within the read radius of both query and pattern, a ball-intersection count that falls roughly exponentially in Hamming distance over a local window, so softmax attention over cosine similarity of unit-norm queries and keys, with a fitted inverse temperature, approximates the SDM read there; the approximation cannot hold globally, since the binary count vanishes beyond twice the radius, and its inverse temperature comes from a regression, not from the paper's analytic bound *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-698](../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md): Thresholding linear attribute probes on a language model's embeddings yields a complete concept lattice for any incidence whatever, so the lattice is guaranteed by construction; what the Lattice Representation Hypothesis measured is per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o annotations at F1 70–83, and no lattice law *(used by 2; also realizability)*
- [THEORY-717](../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md): For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix *(used by 7; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-719](../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md): On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-720](../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md): Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned *(used by 5)*
- [THEORY-721](../record/theory.d/THEORY-721.md): On a complex Hilbert space no orthonormal basis or tensor factorisation of given dimensions is distinguished by the space alone, and orthonormal bases correspond exactly to commutative special †-Frobenius algebras; over the reals that correspondence fails *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-722](../record/theory.d/THEORY-722.md): In Contextuality-by-Default 2.0, whether a system of non-binary variables is contextual depends on which variables represent the measurements: coarse-graining can turn a noncontextual system into a contextual one, while for connections of two variables, and for consistently connected systems, CbD 1.0 and 2.0 agree *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-723](../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md): For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-726](../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md): Weight decay on factors is a nuclear-norm penalty on their product: with tied weights λ‖W‖²_F = λ‖WWᵀ‖_*, and for untied factors the least (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over UVᵀ = M is ‖M‖_*, so for any loss that sees the weights only through the product, square-penalized training is nuclear-norm-penalized training of a product of bounded rank *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-739](../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md): For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-778](../record/theory.d/THEORY-778.md): In the Random Hierarchy Model with v symbols per level, m rules per symbol and s-tuples, the covariance between two tokens whose lowest common ancestor is ℓ levels up has zero mean over grammars and root-mean-square size about ((1 − m/v^(s−1))/(v³ m^(2ℓ−1)))^(1/2), falling by a factor m per level, while its estimate from P sequences carries noise of about (v²P)^(−1/2), so the two meet at P_ℓ ≈ v m^(2ℓ−1)/(1 − m/v^(s−1)); all to leading order in large v and m *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-839](../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md): A model optimal for the distribution its own deployment induces, a performatively stable point, need not minimize the risk it actually incurs, and the gap is bounded: for a loss that is L_z-Lipschitz in the data and γ-strongly convex in the parameters, and a distribution map that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1 distance, every stable point lies within 2L_zε/γ of every performative optimum; in a biased-coin example the stable point is µ/(1 − ε) and the optimum µ/(1 − 2ε), equal only when the prediction has no effect *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-843](../record/theory.d/THEORY-843.md): Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern's approximate abstraction error, the least over surjective context maps of the worst case over allowed interventions and contexts of the high-level distance between the coarse-grained low-level outcome and the high-level outcome, is zero exactly for τ-abstraction; an abstraction followed by an α-approximation of the high-level model is within α, an α-approximation of the low-level model followed by an abstraction only within kα, k the worst-case ratio of high- to low-level distances, and an approximate abstraction need not factor into an exact abstraction and an approximation *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-846](../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md): Information usable by a predictor restricted to a family V can be created by computing on the data, so the data-processing inequality fails for V-information: with Z the exclusive-or of two fair independent bits, linear and one-coordinate families extract nothing about Z from the pair and all of it from their exclusive-or; V-information computed from any function of the source is bounded by the source's Shannon information when the family's input-free predictions can match the marginal of the target, and can exceed it otherwise *(used by 4; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-848](../record/theory.d/THEORY-848.md): In an acyclic structural equation model, marginalising a variable that no declared intervention sets is an exact transformation, provided the coarse model's exogenous noises may be dependent; so exactness does not require the dropped variable to be causally idle, and it can drop a variable that decides how its children respond to an intervention that is declared *(used by 5; also formal-apparatus, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-861](../record/theory.d/THEORY-861.md): When a deployed model changes the distribution it is scored on, retraining on the distribution the last model induced contracts at rate εβ/γ, for a β-jointly smooth, γ-strongly convex loss and a distribution map that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1 distance, and so converges to a unique performatively stable point when ε < γ/β; each condition is needed, since dropping strong convexity, joint smoothness or the bound on ε each admits a case where retraining never converges *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-862](../record/theory.d/THEORY-862.md): In US law schools under the U.S. News ranking, administrators and faculty reported, and public sources corroborated, that schools changed what they did in order to move their rank: they moved money toward the ranking's inputs, redefined admissions and career-services work around its indicators, and gamed its figures, so the ranking altered the things it measured *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-961](../record/theory.d/THEORY-961.md): In a finite partial-monitoring game, an action optimal wherever two neighbouring actions tie has a loss vector on the segment between theirs, so a degenerate or duplicate action never creates a neighbouring pair or decides the trivial class, yet its signals count toward the pair's local observability; and the T^2/3 lower bound for a pair that is not locally observable needs the separating direction in the kernel of the signal matrices of all such actions, not only of the two neighbours *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-962](../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md): In a finite partial-monitoring game, the signals of a set D of actions determine the expected loss difference of actions i and j under every outcome distribution iff ℓ_i − ℓ_j lies in the sum of the row spaces of their signal matrices; when it does not, two outcome distributions differing along a vector in the common kernel give every action in D the same signal law and reverse the preference between i and j, so no amount of play restricted to D can learn the comparison *(used by 4; also distributed-agency, will-organization, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-972](../record/theory.d/THEORY-972.md): In the author–topic model the likelihood of a corpus depends on the topics Φ and the authors' topic distributions Θ only through the document–word matrix ΦΘA, A being fixed by the observed authorship, so LDA (each document its own author) and the topic-free author model (each author one topic) are special cases; and the likelihood leaves Φ and Θ unidentified not only up to the permutations of topics the paper names but along a continuum of changes of topic basis whenever every topic gives every word positive probability *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-993](../record/theory.d/THEORY-993.md): In the mixed membership stochastic blockmodel the probability of an edge from p to q, given the memberships, is (1 − ρ)π_pᵀBπ_q, so the graph's likelihood given the memberships is unchanged by π ↦ Rπ, B ↦ R⁻ᵀBR⁻¹ for any invertible R that keeps the memberships on the simplex and B in [0, 1], a continuum around any solution with B's rates strictly between 0 and 1; and the sparsity parameter ρ enters only through (1 − ρ)B, so it is fixed by nothing but the bound B ≤ 1, and the paper's printed estimator of it is the fraction of absent edges whatever the fit *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1010](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1010.md): On ten corpora simulated from three-level hierarchical LDA itself (100 documents of 250 words, a vocabulary of 100, sparse topics with η = 0.005, γ = 1), the highest-probability state of the collapsed Gibbs sampler recovered the generating tree exactly in eight; in one of the other two a wrong tree had higher posterior probability than the true one *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1088](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1088.md): When the expression maps of a discourse sheaf diffuse to reduce disagreement, with opinions held fixed they converge to the nearest sheaf, in Frobenius distance, of which the opinions are a global section, so apparent consensus is reached by changing what is said ("learning to lie"); with opinions diffusing too the joint flow is gradient descent on ½‖δx‖², and conserved diagonal blocks of αδᵀδ − βxxᵀ keep the opinions from collapsing to zero; nothing in either flow checks an expression against the opinion it expresses *(used by 6; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-1096](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md): Blackwell's comparison of experiments, its easy direction: an experiment is a family of distributions indexed by a common parameter, and if one experiment is a garbling of another by a Markov kernel, every risk attainable with the garbling in any decision problem with bounded losses is attainable with the original, on any outcome spaces *(used by 12; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-1120](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1120.md): On 416 translations into English by four LLMs of 104 culturally loaded utterances in Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil and Malayalam, each scored for pragmatic adequacy by one native rater per language, the reference-based COMET metric correlates with the ratings at Pearson r = 0.813 and Spearman ρ = 0.860, against r 0.80 and ρ 0.79 for XCOMET and r 0.73 and ρ 0.79 for MetricX, with no test of the differences; four outputs picked after the fact that invert or misplace the source's meaning get COMET scores of 0.65–0.86 against the rater's 1 or 2 *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1129](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1129.md): Anchors entered as node features in fused Gromov–Wasserstein break a structural tie only when they move under it: with α strictly between 0 and 1, the zero-cost matchings of a structure with itself are exactly its automorphisms that fix every anchor, so a 6-cycle has 12 with no anchor, 2 with one anchor, 1 with two adjacent anchors and still 2 with two antipodal ones, and whether a set of anchors identifies the correspondence can be decided from the structure before any fit *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1132](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1132.md): For K networks compared under square loss, the multi-marginal fused Gromov–Wasserstein objective of a joint coupling tensor is exactly the sum of the pairwise fused GW objectives of its two-way marginals, so the joint optimum is at least the sum of the pairwise optima, with equality exactly when some choice of pairwise optimal couplings is jointly realizable as the marginals of one tensor; a joint alignment is consistent in that sense by construction, which for deterministic couplings means the pairwise maps compose and for soft ones does not *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1133](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1133.md): The Gromov–Wasserstein objective between two spaces depends on each only through its within-space similarity matrix and weights, so every transformation of a space that preserves them, a single orthogonal map or per-vector rescaling under cosine similarity, leaves every coupling's cost unchanged, and any coupling composed with a symmetry of either structure costs exactly what it did; GW can therefore identify a correspondence only up to the automorphisms of the two similarity structures, and on symmetric data it cannot choose between branches or categories that the symmetry exchanges *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1134](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1134.md): A translation metric that predicts a sentence score and token-level error spans from one shared encoder reaches segment-level agreement with expert MQM annotation of Kendall τ about 0.4 and span F1 under 0.33, the best among open metrics and GPT-4 prompting at the time, while the score computed from its own spans correlates with its regression scores at Pearson 0.73 to 0.82, and at 0.90 to 0.92 with its final score, which includes the span score by construction *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1140](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1140.md): If every entity's O(d) frame may change independently and relation transports change as Tᵢⱼ ↦ gᵢTᵢⱼgⱼ⁻¹, then functions of the transports alone carry no invariant information except around cycles, a triangle's invariants are exactly the class functions of its holonomy H = TᵢⱼTⱼₖTₖᵢ, and an equivariant update of an edge from one cycle through it is Ψ(H)Tᵢⱼ with Ψ conjugation-equivariant; the symmetry fixes a family of updates, not one mechanism, and says nothing about whether a task has the symmetry *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-1142](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1142.md): A translation between two logics presented as institutions is correct, in the Satisfaction Condition's sense, when a translated sentence holds in a model exactly when the original holds in the model's translation; given the model translation this fixes the sentence translation up to semantic equivalence, and when every model of the target is reached it preserves and reflects entailment, so one logic's prover can decide the other's; but the condition alone admits collapsing translations and is relative to a model translation it does not supply *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1151](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1151.md): A learned translation metric trained with synthetic hallucinations and diagnostic perturbations alongside human MQM flags most injected localized critical errors (all but 0 to 17 percent, by type and model size) and ranks fully detached hallucinations below other translations with AUROC up to 0.96, and without a reference it ranks hallucinations better than with one; how far this reflects the synthetic training data has not been separated from how far it generalises *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1153](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1153.md): In the PETra corpus of English-source TED and Europarl translations, the additions for the target audience that a named-entity and null-alignment filter, and a classifier trained on its finds, turned up, as labelled by one annotator with no agreement reported, are mostly system transfers, chiefly unit conversions, and entity changes, and their mix differs by target language *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1155](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1155.md): Co-optimal transport between two data matrices of equal shape with uniform weights vanishes exactly when one is the other with its rows and its columns separately permuted, and its objective is unchanged when a pair of optimal plans is composed with any joint relabelling of rows and columns that leaves a matrix unchanged; its sample and feature couplings are therefore identified at best up to that joint symmetry group, which can exchange a block of samples together with its block of features though neither exchange alone is a symmetry, and the paper proves no uniqueness beyond it *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1158](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1158.md): On synchronization of S4 relations with outliers, an untrained mechanism that composes relations through third vertices gains 26–45 points over the single direct path, and weighting the candidate paths by the Wilson loops of squares that avoid the missing edge adds 0.6–7.8 points, most where clean two-hop paths become a minority; it stays below spectral synchronization with one reweighting pass on every setting and within 2.2 points of plain spectral synchronization either way; its 0.99 AUC for corrupted triangles is the ceiling that exactly flat clean data set, not a measure of detection power *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1164](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1164.md): Propp proposes, from his analysis of Afanasyev's tales 50–151, that the Russian wondertale is built from 31 character functions, each defined by its consequence for the action, occurring in one order and falling to seven roles, so that wondertales share one composition and differ in who performs the functions and how *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1276](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1276.md): In Simondon's ontology, as Iliadis and Bencherki read it, information is not a signal transmitted between finished entities but a disparity between two differently ordered domains of a metastable system, and its meaning is the new structure that transduction produces in resolving it *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1531](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1531.md): Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy propose that communication be treated as transduction, the continuity of an action through processes that it transforms, rather than as exchange between parties, with meaning the contribution an action makes, in retrospect, to a joint individuation and coexisting meanings the mark of concurrent individuations, and they assert that the problem of scaling agency from individual to collective then vanishes *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1586](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1586.md): Abramsky and Sadrzadeh model a basic discourse representation structure as a section of a presheaf of consistent literals, a choice of anaphoric resolution as a cover and a discourse's meaning as the gluing, unique when it exists; in their linguistic examples the only obstruction to gluing is inconsistency of literals, which is not contextuality in Abramsky and Brandenburger's sense *(used by 3)*

## Nucleating an argument

- [THEORY-132](../record/theory.d/THEORY-132.md): Stability, a system's speed of return to equilibrium after disturbance, and resilience, its capacity to absorb change and persist within its domain of attraction, are distinct properties that can trade off, so a system can be highly unstable and highly resilient, and managing it for constancy can erode its resilience *(used by 4; also will-organization, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-134](../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md): Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time *(used by 12; also will-organization, distributed-agency, realizability, readiness)*
- [THEORY-136](../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md): A persistent or abrupt change is not evidence that a system has alternative stable states: field patterns such as jumps, multimodality and dual relationships also arise from a stepwise driver or a simple threshold, and only hysteresis, initial-state dependence or a lasting shift after a temporary disturbance, with slow return excluded, comes close to showing one *(used by 7; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-155](../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md): Iterated learning by Bayesian agents who sample from the posterior converges, in an ergodic chain, to the shared prior *(used by 5; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-178](../record/theory.d/THEORY-178.md): In an ensemble of sign-consistent Boolean rules on the 87-gene core of E. coli's regulatory network, a transient knockout or overexpression of one gene can leave the network in a different attractor after release, and every gene that does so reaches a strongly connected component containing a positive circuit *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-272](../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md): In Hopfield's 1982 simulations at N = 30 and 100, a network of threshold units with symmetric Hebbian couplings acts as a content-addressable memory whose stored random patterns are attractors: recall degrades severely near 0.15N patterns, a pattern placed 10 bits from another at N = 100 often fuses with it, and at 25-fold overload no stored pattern stays stable *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-335](../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md): Selective accessibility, the account that comparing a target with a plausible anchor makes anchor-consistent knowledge more accessible and that this knowledge carries anchoring, fits the moderations of the effect by applicability, representativeness and plausibility that Strack and Mussweiler found, but its accessibility step is inferred, not measured: Harris et al.'s repetition of the recognition test of it, four times by lexical decision and once by continuous identification, found nothing in five preregistered experiments, with tasks that also missed direct picture priming *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-348](../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md): When staying in one state costs a fixed amount per request and leaving it costs a fixed one-time price, switching once the extra cost paid for staying equals that price is within 2 of the offline optimum on every request sequence, and no deterministic online rule does better; with a third option the best guaranteed ratio rises to 3 *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-371](../record/theory.d/THEORY-371.md): For conjunctive queries without equality or comparisons, two queries are equivalent exactly when homomorphisms run both ways between the queries read as small databases, every such query has a minimal equivalent query unique up to isomorphism obtained by deleting atoms, and evaluating one against a database is NP-complete when the query is part of the input *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-374](../record/theory.d/THEORY-374.md): Given views with conjunctive definitions, deciding that they answer a conjunctive query exactly is NP-complete in the size of the query and definitions, while a maximally-contained rewriting can be built in time polynomial in that size without saying whether it is exact; and finding all certain answers from the stored contents is polynomial in their size under the open-world assumption when the views are conjunctive and the query conjunctive or datalog, but co-NP-hard in that size under the closed-world assumption even for conjunctive views and queries *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-376](../record/theory.d/THEORY-376.md): In a simulated single-client, read-only database answering selection queries on one relation, describing cached data by the predicates of past queries let each query be answered partly from cache, with only the remainder Q ∧ ¬V sent to the server; this matched page caching on a clustered index, beat it on an unclustered one, and, on an unindexed attribute with a disk cache, answered over 60% of 1% queries without contacting the server; the cost of computing probe and remainder queries was not charged *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-386](../record/theory.d/THEORY-386.md): When a cached interval of width W is kept valid by its source, which pushes a refresh at cost C_vr whenever the value leaves it, and queries fetch the exact value at cost C_qr whenever it is too wide, and the chances of the two per step go as 1/W² and as W, the expected refresh cost is least at W* = (ρK₁/K₂)^(1/3) with ρ = 2C_vr/C_qr, where ρ times the chance of a pushed refresh equals the chance of a fetch *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-389](../record/theory.d/THEORY-389.md): For conjunctive queries and views without comparison predicates, a stored view can be used in an equivalent rewriting of a query exactly when the view's body maps homomorphically into the query's, a minimal rewriting needs no more literals than the query, and deciding whether a rewriting shorter than the query or one using only the views exists is NP-complete in the size of the query and view definitions; with comparisons in both, deciding whether any rewriting uses the views is Π2p-complete *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-725](../record/theory.d/THEORY-725.md): On the court agenda {P, Q, R, R iff (P and Q)} under universal domain, proposition-wise majority voting is not robustly rational, while the premise-based procedure is, and it makes the group's judgments a function of the members' whole judgment sets that the members' judgments on the conclusion neither fix nor need to enter *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1194](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1194.md): Clark and Chalmers argue that if belief is individuated by functional role, an external store that is constantly consulted, directly available and automatically endorsed can carry a standing belief, so that the material vehicles of some mental states extend beyond the skin; the step from coupling to parthood rests on that premise and on a parity principle they state rather than argue *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*

## What a record of inquiry keeps

- [THEORY-347](../record/theory.d/THEORY-347.md): Belief bases with the same logical closure can revise to opposite conclusions on the same input, so a closed belief set does not fix its own revision; partial meet contraction of a base need not satisfy Recovery, and bases keep distinct inconsistent states apart, while a belief-set model reproduces the base difference only by attaching a different selection mechanism to the same set *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-353](../record/theory.d/THEORY-353.md): For a logically closed theory, the contractions satisfying the six basic AGM postulates are exactly the partial meet contractions, and those satisfying the two supplementary postulates as well are exactly the ones whose selection of remainders is generated by a transitive relation; the theory alone does not fix the contraction, and the results concern one change of one fixed theory *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-362](../record/theory.d/THEORY-362.md): For nonrecursive Datalog or SQL views with safe stratified negation and stratified aggregation, under set or duplicate semantics, storing with each derived tuple only the number of its derivations suffices to maintain the view under insertions and deletions of base tuples: signed counts propagated through delta rules stratum by stratum give each tuple's change as its new count minus its old, a tuple leaves when its count reaches zero, and a MIN or MAX group whose extreme is deleted is recomputed from the stored lower stratum *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-367](../record/theory.d/THEORY-367.md): For SPJU relational queries, which Buneman, Khanna and Tan's tree model encodes, the minimal witnesses of an output tuple, the inclusion-minimal sets of source facts from which the query still derives it, are the minimal sets matched by single derivations and so are the same for every equivalent query, while where-provenance, the source location a value was copied from, can differ between equivalent queries *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-373](../record/theory.d/THEORY-373.md): For positive relational algebra on relations whose tuples are annotated from a commutative semiring, every query's annotated answer equals its answer over provenance polynomials N[X] in the input tuple ids, evaluated at the input annotations, so set, bag, c-table and event-table semantics all factor through the polynomials; revaluing inputs can remove output tuples but never add them, and nothing is shown for negation, difference or aggregation *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-380](../record/theory.d/THEORY-380.md): For datalog over a finite input instance annotated from a commutative ω-continuous semiring, with an answer's tag defined as the sum over its derivation trees of the product of its leaves' tags, the tags are the least fixed point of a finite polynomial system and factor through formal power series N∞⟦X⟧ in the input tuple ids; an answer tuple's series has an infinite coefficient exactly when one of its derivation trees contains a tuple lying on a cycle of unit rules *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-387](../record/theory.d/THEORY-387.md): For positive recursive Datalog views under set semantics, deleting every derived tuple that has any derivation through a deleted base fact, then restoring each deleted tuple that still has a derivation from what remains, then adding what insertions derive, leaves exactly the tuples derivable from the new base (E − Δ⁻) ∪ Δ⁺, with no derivation counts stored; the extension to stratified negation and aggregation is asserted, not shown, and the size of the overestimate is not measured *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-548](../record/theory.d/THEORY-548.md): In generalised Lotka–Volterra dynamics with every interaction delayed by τ, a feasible equilibrium that is stable without delay loses stability at τ_c = min over the community eigenvalues j of arctan(|Re j|/|Im j|)/|j|, where a pair of roots crosses the imaginary axis transversally (a Hopf point), so the critical delay is set by the community spectrum; in Saeedian et al.'s strongly self-regulated setting the oscillating regime's community-level variability falls with diversity (S = 10–70) while species-level variability rises, and the fall matches what summing independently oscillating species gives *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-884](../record/theory.d/THEORY-884.md): A retained state supports exact answers to a declared family of questions after every finite sequence of a declared family of total deterministic revisions exactly when each of its fibres lies within one class of the coarsest revision-invariant refinement of agreement on current answers; that refinement can be strictly finer than what present answers require, and at most K* − K revision sequences, beyond the current answers, are needed to tell its K* classes apart *(used by 2; also formal-apparatus)*

## The record as its own apparatus

- [THEORY-327](../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md): Fricker, in her 2003 paper and her 2017 retrospective, holds that testimonial injustice is an ingenuous misjudgement of a speaker's credibility caused by prejudice, and that deliberate manipulation of credibility is a related but distinct wrong; and she accepts Anderson's structural form, which is pre-emptive: a speaker's word is never sought because of a structural prejudice, such as an un-refreshed list, that is no one's fault *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1064](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1064.md): In counterexample-guided abstraction refinement, a spurious counterexample locates the distinction its abstraction lacked: walking it forward through the concrete system, the first abstract state where no concrete continuation exists merges the states the trace can reach with the states that have the transition onward, and splitting them removes the counterexample; for finite-state programs and ACTL* properties whose counterexamples are paths or loops, repeating check and split ends in a real counterexample or a proof *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1072](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1072.md): In Simon's analysis, whether a problem is well structured is a relation between the problem and a bounded solver, judged by practicable rather than in-principle computability, so it comes in degrees and has no sharp boundary; on that standard even theorem proving and chess fail some of the conditions, chess is well structured in the small and ill structured in the large, and problems presented by the world become well structured only in being prepared for a solver *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1076](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1076.md): For Bohr a phenomenon is the observation obtained under a specified experimental arrangement, epistemic and derivative, with atomic object and instrument presupposed real; his relational holism is epistemic, and the subject–object, knower–known and word–world dualisms are presupposed by his account, so Bohr's authority does not support agential realism *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1084](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1084.md): Simon proposes that ill structured problems can be handled by an alternation between a solver working on a problem that is well structured at each moment and a recognition and retrieval system that keeps modifying the problem space from memory or the environment, that a serial solver gains nothing by assembling the problem space at the outset, and that nothing but the size of the knowledge base may separate ill from well structured problems, so that no qualitatively new mechanisms are needed *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1090](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md): Eliminating an interior vertex of a cellular sheaf on a graph can leave its boundary a space of consistent assignments that no sheaf on the boundary vertices has: the interior can impose a constraint among boundary vertices that no set of pairwise compatibility conditions expresses, so Kron reduction, which turns the Laplacian of a connected graph into a graph Laplacian on any set of boundary vertices, fails for sheaves in general and holds when every vertex stalk has dimension at most one *(used by 6; also distributed-agency, realizability)*
- [THEORY-1094](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1094.md): In counterexample-guided abstraction refinement the property and the concrete system are fixed inputs: the property's atomic formulas help build the first abstraction and no abstraction may merge states that disagree on them, every refinement only splits classes toward the concrete state space, and a real counterexample ends the procedure; so the loop revises which of the concrete system's distinctions the model draws, never the property or the space of possible answers *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1564](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1564.md): Bencherki and Iliadis propose that knowledge of an entity should focus on its individuation process and reflect on the way that knowledge itself has individuated, and the first author, the ethnographer of their illustrating case, describes his own individuation through the fieldwork *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1628](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1628.md): Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy hold, quoting Simondon, that research into individuation consists in following the being in its genesis and accomplishing the genesis of thought with the genesis of the object, so that researchers individuate into what they study, and they leave open what methods would do this *(used by 1)*

## Evidence for experience

- [THEORY-245](../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md): In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, prefrontal cortex carried a seen image's category but not its identity, and a face's orientation at most weakly, while posterior cortex carried category, face orientation and the identity of objects, letters and false fonts, though not of faces; no prefrontal site showed the preregistered onset-and-offset response, and one, found in an exploratory analysis, responded at offset earlier than predicted *(used by 2; also organizational-affect)*
- [THEORY-296](../record/theory.d/THEORY-296.md): In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, category-selective posterior cortex showed no sustained content-specific synchronization with early visual cortex, which iEEG sampled with 12 electrodes: the preregistered phase coupling was brief, low-frequency and mostly stimulus-evoked, and exploratory amplitude coupling, gamma included, was also brief *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-766](../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md): Brushing a seen rubber hand in synchrony with the hidden real hand, against asynchronous brushing, raises reports that touch is felt at the rubber hand and, more weakly and less reliably, that the rubber hand is one's own; the proprioceptive drift toward the rubber hand that accompanies these reports is not a measure of them; the standard comparison conditions do not equalise participants' expectations, so whether the stimulation or the expectation produces the report difference is open *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-865](../record/theory.d/THEORY-865.md): In Gurnee, Sofroniew et al.'s experiments on Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6, the residual-stream directions a corpus-averaged Jacobian lens marks as verbalizable (the J-space) carried most of the causal effect on verbal report and on unspoken two-hop intermediates while holding a small share of their variance (swaps along them succeeding on 59% and 61% of trials, against 5% and 28% for the remainder, which fell to 0% and 6% with the J-space clamped), held instructed concepts, and passed one swapped argument to several functions (76 of 192 swaps); in two small task sets (n = 8 and 11), report and flexible inference followed a swap while continuation, anomaly detection and line wrapping did not, a split the authors partly define by this result; and by the lens's own statistics the J-space works in a middle band of layers, holds about 25 active directions and under 10% of activation variance, and is amplified and relayed by the weights more than other directions *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-866](../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md): Expert texts of Shamatha, Transcendental and Stillness Meditation describe their so-called contentless goal-states as lacking thoughts, perceptions, images and memories but keeping many forms of content, and as differing across the practices in attentional stability and vividness *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-869](../record/theory.d/THEORY-869.md): In Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6, Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. found that projecting out the ten most active J-space directions in layers 38 to 54 of 100 lowered an experiential-language score, graded by Opus 4.6-based model graders on five or six prompts per condition, both in the models' narrations of their own processing and in their descriptions of another person's experience, while norm-matched perturbations along other directions left it near baseline and the text stayed fluent; on Haiku 4.5 coherence failed first *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-870](../record/theory.d/THEORY-870.md): In one study of 33 experienced Transcendental Meditation practitioners and 33 matched controls who counted instead, the practitioners rated their session higher on a retrospective pure-awareness scale whose top was defined for them as free from content (d = 0.77), and a classifier on EEG separated meditation from counting at 65% balanced accuracy on held-out subjects and, within practitioners, meditation from rest with 88% sensitivity; the authors found no robust association between the ratings and the EEG features *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-871](../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md): In two midlife community samples (n = 182 and 176), instructed reappraisal of aversive pictures, mostly by reinterpretation, lowered reported negative affect, while the BOLD responses of the amygdala, periaqueductal gray, hypothalamus and the other subcortical regions that responded to the pictures showed evidence of no change (Bayes factors below 1/10); the emotion-responsive regions it reduced were all cortical, mainly higher visual and parietal *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-953](../record/theory.d/THEORY-953.md): On Isaac's structuralist account, the strongest evidence that a quality-space model targets phenomenal experience, and not only behaviour or neural activity, is convergence between models of the same space derived through different behavioural procedures, since experience is what those procedures share; he concedes that the convergence observed is coarse, with discrepancies that in many cases exceed each method's own uncertainty, and that because the models average over subjects what they converge on is a standard observer *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1289](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1289.md): In a dynamical model anchored to an identified mechanism, holding one part's variable fixed and finding that the phenomenon persists indicates that the part is not a component of the mechanism responsible for that phenomenon, as when Smolen et al. fixed CLOCK and circadian oscillation continued; the verdict is relative to the phenomenon and only as good as the model, and it decides which pathways the phenomenon needs, not which lie inside the system *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1295](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1295.md): Metzinger 2024 calls consciousness without an egoic self or first-person perspective "empirically established" on the strength of retrospective, self-selected reports from meditators, while its own methods chapter grants that a remembered report of a selfless state is "highly dubious" evidence that the state was selfless when it occurred, and leaves that problem open *(used by 2)*

## How training finds structure

- [THEORY-004](../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md): A representation is determined by its centred kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal transformation, and the rotation-aligned distance between two representations equals the Bures distance between their kernels *(used by 6; also pragmatic-transport, formal-apparatus, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-009](../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md): In the positive-pair spectral self-supervised papers, self-adjointness comes from the symmetry of the positive-pair distribution, not from the Riesz representation theorem; elsewhere in the family it comes from a symmetrized loss, a precondition on the kernel, or composing the conditional-expectation operator with its adjoint *(used by 4; also formal-apparatus, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-021](../record/theory.d/THEORY-021.md): In the exact configurations of uniform superposition (regular polygons, the tetrahedron, antipodal pairs, and tegum products of these that span the hidden space, with equal norms within each factor) the features form a rank-one POVM compressed from the n-feature basis: their dimensionality-weighted projectors sum to the identity *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-082](../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md): Steepest descent is defined only relative to a metric, and Amari's proof that natural-gradient learning is Fisher efficient needs the Fisher information at the optimum to be invertible, the condition whose failure WBIC calls singular; in a multilayer perceptron it fails wherever an output weight is zero *(used by 4; also distributed-agency, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-083](../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md): In Papyan, Han and Donoho's runs of VGG, ResNet and DenseNet trained with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation, training past zero error shrinks last-layer within-class variability against between-class variability, and moves the centred class means and the classifier toward a common simplex equiangular tight frame and the decision toward nearest class mean, nearly to completion on the four easier datasets and only partly on ImageNet *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-086](../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md): In the kernel regime gradient descent fits the target eigenspace by eigenspace of the neural tangent kernel, at rates set by their eigenvalues; on uniform spherical data the eigenspaces are the harmonic degrees, and for fully connected ReLU networks the non-zero eigenvalues decay as k^(−d) at every depth *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-105](../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md): For RoBERTa-base fine-tuned on English classification data, with loss measured by a linear probe refitted on the frozen encoder, points sampled from the convex hull of models fine-tuned on one dataset, one task family or twelve GLUE and SuperGLUE datasets lost no more than any model fine-tuned elsewhere and beat the group's own members in 88% to 96.7% of comparisons, and the centroid of the general-level models was a better starting point for BitFit than the pretrained model *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-111](../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md): In image classifiers, between two networks linearly connected by spawning from a shared checkpoint or by permutation alignment (MLPs, and VGG-16, ResNet-20 and ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet), nearly every layer's features at three points on the line were proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features, and pairs that were not linearly connected were far from it *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-112](../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md): Aligning independently trained solutions over the architecture's symmetries removed the linear barrier between them for MNIST MLPs and 32×-wide ResNet-20s on CIFAR-10, two-thirds of it for an ImageNet ResNet-50, and not all of it for VGG-16 or ResNet-20 at 1× width, the barrier after weight matching falling with width; for 6- to 8-layer ViTs and GPT-2s, permutations alone removed 63–90% of it, and adding an orthogonal map on the residual stream, learned against the loss at the path's midpoint, took it to zero or near zero except on BookCorpus (0.42) *(used by 5; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-113](../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md): Merging ResNets trained from different initialisations on disjoint halves of a label set by permuting one onto the other and averaging fell far short of the ensemble; their cross-model feature correlation fell with depth, merging only the early layers recovered most of the ensemble's accuracy, and merging features within each model as well as across both helped at 4× width and above; Stoica et al. attribute the failure to features with no counterpart in the other model *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-114](../record/theory.d/THEORY-114.md): In image classification, linear mode connectivity appeared during training and not at initialization: copies of ResNet-20 and VGG-16 on CIFAR-10 and of ResNet-50 and Inception-v3 on ImageNet, trained from a shared state, became stable to SGD noise in test error only after 1.5–20% of training (LeNet on MNIST was stable from the start), and between independently initialized MLPs on MNIST and CIFAR-10 the barrier after weight-matching alignment was high at initialization and fell gradually through training *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-117](../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md): In Uselis, Dittadi and Oh's two-concept grids, ResNet-50s trained from scratch, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, reach unseen combinations as the share of combinations seen grows and not as up to four times more data of the same combinations is added; and when embeddings are exactly linearly factored, seen pairs that connect every value of both concepts, as two per value arranged in one cycle do, determine the embedding of every unseen pair *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-163](../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md): In Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier and Tishby's analysis, the colour-naming systems of the World Color Survey languages and English lie near the information-bottleneck bound for compressing perceptual meanings into words, at a trade-off parameter just above 1 and nearer than hue-rotated variants of themselves, with the need distribution over meanings estimated from the naming data *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-169](../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md): For unnormalized causal linear attention and for softmax attention, conditioning on a context is exactly training a learner on it and predicting: the first is one batch gradient step of a linear inner model from zero, the second kernel regression that stores the context, and one linear self-attention layer with constructed weights carries one gradient step of in-context linear regression; for these layers conditioning and per-sequence weight updates differ in what state is kept, not in kind *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-176](../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md): A task-loss stitching penalty compares representations in one decision problem, through a fixed top network and a restricted map class, so it is not Blackwell's order: representations that are functions of each other can stitch differently, and a negative penalty shows the fitted map did not reproduce the layers it replaced *(used by 6; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-181](../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md): In a model that decodes the sum of two learned embeddings, at zero training loss with an injective decoder, a training set fixes the generalising representation of addition when its same-answer pairs leave only translation and scale free; for non-modular addition with p = 10 and one-dimensional embeddings, generalisation sets in near the training fraction, about 0.4, at which that becomes likely *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-184](../record/theory.d/THEORY-184.md): Under a permutation-equivariant update whose map is K-Lipschitz, coincident neurons stay coincident at every step size, and at step size below 1/K distinct neurons cannot merge in finitely many steps *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-187](../record/theory.d/THEORY-187.md): In a deep linear network trained by gradient descent on whitened inputs from decoupled, balanced initial weights, depth slows learning through the initial end-to-end strength of each mode: counting iterations as learning time over the stable step size, from strength of order one the number of iterations stays bounded as depth grows, once the step size falls with depth as stability requires, while from small strength ε the plateau lengthens from ln(1/ε) with one hidden layer towards 1/ε at great depth *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-191](../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md): In four natural odour sources (strawberry, tomato, blueberry and mouse-urine volatiles), the rank order of correlations between compound concentrations has the Betti-curve signature of points near the boundary of a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of any uniform Euclidean cube tried, and human odour-descriptor profiles for 127 odorants have that of a full three-dimensional hyperbolic ball *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-192](../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md): In twelve sessions of rat dorsal CA1 from three data sets, pairwise correlations among place cells have the Betti-curve signature of points sampled uniformly from a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of a low-dimensional Euclidean cube, and the fitted radius rose with the logarithm of exploration time *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-195](../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md): On the Random Hierarchy Model, in the experiments reported (s = 2, L ≤ 4, small v), deep CNNs matched to the tree and trained in a feature-learning regime reach a tenth of chance error from about n_c m^L examples, polynomial in the input dimension, at the training-set size at which their hidden layers become invariant to swapping synonymous tuples; two-layer networks and the same CNNs as fixed kernels need a number proportional to the whole input space, exponential in the input dimension, and deep CNNs stay near chance when every tuple is made equally likely in every class *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-197](../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md): Mehta and Schwab's correspondence between Kadanoff's variational renormalization group and restricted Boltzmann machines is an identity of parametrizations, under which an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution; away from that point it does not make training by distribution fitting a renormalization *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-204](../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md): On TinyStories and WikiText-103, the data-limited exponent of transformer test loss, fitted to the lower envelope of learning curves across context lengths at up to about 10^8 training tokens, overlaps γ/(2β), where β is the decay with lag of the top singular value of the token–token covariance and γ the decay of next-token conditional entropy with context length; under assumed per-lag scaling forms, a horizon n*(P) ~ P^(1/(2β)) gives the exponent min(δ, γ/(2β)), δ being the decay rate of the within-horizon excess losses *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-206](../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md): For networks of smooth units without biases, one hidden layer needs exactly ∏(rᵢ+1) neurons to match the monomial x₁^r₁⋯xₙ^rₙ's Taylor polynomial at the origin, and a deep network O(Σ log rᵢ), with the upper bounds holding for uniform approximation too, so the cost of flattening a polynomial grows exponentially with its degree in distinct variables and not with the number of inputs: products of many inputs separate depths, bounded-degree polynomials do not *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-211](../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md): In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise *(used by 5; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-213](../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md): Every mirror symmetry of a network's per-sample loss makes its symmetric subspace invariant under gradient descent and SGD, and when the loss's Hessian is bounded below by −c, weight decay γ‖θ‖² with γ > c/2 puts every minimum in that subspace; rescaling symmetries that hold at λ = −1, rotation symmetries and permutation symmetries contain such mirrors, whose subspaces are zeroed weights, reduced rank and identical neurons *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-227](../record/theory.d/THEORY-227.md): Mutual information between an input and its representation does not fix the representation's quality: invertible encoders all preserve it exactly, yet under a linear probe some do better than the raw input and some worse *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-229](../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md): For a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss on a linear or fixed-kernel model, gradient flow from a small initialization of common scale aligned with the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation learns them one at a time, in order of eigenvalue, and ends at a top spectral solution, which is exactly a minimum-norm zero-loss solution: kernel PCA on K_Γ *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-234](../record/theory.d/THEORY-234.md): Two softmax next-token predictors induce the same distribution exactly when their embeddings and unembeddings are related by an invertible linear map on the subspaces that enter the logits, with arbitrary distortion off them, so a linear relational property is shared by all such models or none when it lies in those subspaces, and can fail to be shared otherwise *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-238](../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md): The expected generalization error of an encoder–decoder learner is bounded by the encoder alone, through the KL divergence of its train-and-ghost latents to a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations, for any decoder; and under lossy compression the bound can stay finite for deterministic continuous encoders, whose lossless bound is infinite *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-243](../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md): In the three-unit identity network x ↦ x(1, 0, 1) ↦ (0, 2, 1)·h, aligning the input with the third unit and aligning it with the direction (h₁ + h₂)/√2, two alignments related by an orthogonal change of basis, pass every interchange intervention on the input equally, so interchange interventions on that variable alone do not fix which internal direction mediates it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-246](../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md): Among ResNet-50s trained on ImageNet with nine objectives and stopped early, seven of which beat softmax cross-entropy's top-1 by up to 0.9 points, fixed penultimate features with more class separation transfer worse by linear probe to datasets whose classes are mostly not ImageNet's (Spearman ρ = −0.93 across the nine; mean accuracy 75.9% for softmax to 48.3% for squared error), and within cosine softmax a higher temperature raises separation and lowers that accuracy; the objectives' representations differ mainly in the last third of the network, and full fine-tuning brings mean transfer to within 1.3 points across them *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-248](../record/theory.d/THEORY-248.md): The expected generalisation error of a learning algorithm is at most √(2σ²R/n) + ε, where R is the least information about the sample carried by any surrogate output whose expected generalisation error is within ε; I(S;W) is the lossless case, and for an L-Lipschitz loss R is at most the rate-distortion function of the output's law at distortion ε/(2L), so the bound is finite wherever that function is, including where I(S;W) is infinite *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-253](../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md): In Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark's Geometry model of independent skills with orthogonal task vectors, simulation shows skills progressing together under gradient descent, the weaker taking about 1/p of the time, and in sequence under sign descent, a weaker skill progressing fast only once a stronger is done and the ratio of their times approaching 2; on a rotated quadratic the sequence appears under sign descent only when the loss's eigendirections are misaligned with the coordinates *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-256](../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md): When a sequence generator's latent dynamics factor as a tensor product, its predictive state embeds losslessly and linearly in orthogonal per-factor subspaces of total dimension Σ(d_n − 1); 4-layer GPT-2-style transformers trained by next-token prediction on five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors settle near that dimension, in per-factor subspaces that are linearly independent and approximately orthogonal in their leading components, and under the token noise tested reach it first even when noise makes it lossy *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-263](../record/theory.d/THEORY-263.md): A coding rate that varies with the realised sample and output makes rate-distortion generalisation bounds data-dependent, and with the rate set to the pointwise information density log dP_{W|S}/dP(W) against a fixed prior the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-266](../record/theory.d/THEORY-266.md): For a loss in [0, 1] that is L-Lipschitz in a distortion, with probability at least 1 − δ the average generalisation error along an optimisation trajectory is bounded, under a square root, by the rate-distortion function of the trajectory's law given the sample, a coupling term that carries the trajectory's dependence on the sample, and a distortion term 4Lε *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-269](../record/theory.d/THEORY-269.md): In OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B and GPT-J, how well an affine map from subject to object representation reproduces a factual relation (its LRE causality) tracks how often the relation's subjects and objects co-occur in pretraining, with mean causality above 0.9 beyond about 4.4k, 2.0k and 1.1k co-occurrences respectively, and, across OLMo-7B's eight checkpoints, at whatever step that count is reached *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-278](../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md): Under MSE loss, in Han, Papyan and Donoho's VGG, ResNet and DenseNet runs on five balanced ten-class datasets, the trained classifier stays near the least-squares classifier for its own features from an early epoch; and on that central path, for unconstrained features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance and without weight decay, gradient flow drives the class-separation singular values to infinity at equal rates, which in that model is neural collapse *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-283](../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md): For a hierarchical multi-index target with isotropic Gaussian inputs and even, separable links, direction k becomes weakly recoverable by the Bayes-optimal estimator at a sample count proportional to its squared weight to the power minus one, so features emerge one at a time through sharp spectral transitions in the number of samples; a target-agnostic spectral estimator attains the thresholds and the optimal weighted error, and a two-layer network whose first layer is that estimator, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-284](../record/theory.d/THEORY-284.md): If a feature's values form a compact metric space carried continuously and injectively onto the unit sphere, and cosine similarity is locally a C² decreasing function of squared feature distance, then every path on the representation manifold is √(−2g′(0)) times as long as the feature path it images, so on-manifold shortest paths recover the feature's intrinsic length metric up to one scale; a homeomorphism alone does not fix it *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-293](../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md): For an optimal capacity-bounded learner on an orthogonal mixture of equally frequent random facts and a second domain, the facts are learned not at all below a capacity threshold set by the mixing ratio and in full once capacity exceeds it by the facts' total entropy, and Pythia models trained on synthetic biographies mixed into web text show a threshold in model size and in mixing ratio *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-294](../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md): For a wide two-layer ReLU network with zero bias on one-dimensional data whose two classes lie on opposite sides of the origin, the tangent kernel is a constant multiple of the initialization kernel, so lazy training leaves the within-class variability of its features, NC1, where initialization put it *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-306](../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md): MSN's objective penalizes unequal cluster sizes explicitly and SwAV's enforces equal sizes, and in one study with mini-batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, SimCLR, MSN and VICReg lost 11 to 18 points of ImageNet linear accuracy while MAE and data2vec lost under one *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-445](../record/theory.d/THEORY-445.md): A network built from group correlations over a discrete split group of plane symmetries, pointwise nonlinearities and coset pooling is equivariant to that group by construction, through the regular representation alone: the group is fixed before training and built into the weight sharing, not found in the data *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-478](../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md): If the diffusion densities' Hellinger distances obey a Hölder bound with exponent θ in d_T / t^(1/β) and are bounded below once d_T exceeds a multiple of t^(1/β), then for 0 < α < θ/β summing scale-weighted hyperbolic distances between diffusion densities over dyadic times gives a distance two-sided equivalent, up to constants, to min{1, d_T^(αβ)} for pairs above the finest scale: it keeps the tree's neighbourhoods and not its global distances; whether a tree's heat kernel, or sampled data, meets the bounds, and with which θ, is not shown *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-481](../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md): Under gradient flow averaged over tasks and data, a linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression learns as a two-layer linear network from an aligned start does: when tasks share the input covariance's eigenbasis and the weights start and stay aligned with it, then in the long-context limit each input mode is learned on its own logistic curve whose timescale falls with the square of its variance, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the layer converges to the estimator preconditioned by the inverse input covariance; at finite context length the modes decouple exactly only when inputs are isotropic and the modes start equal, and otherwise couple at order 1/N *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-504](../record/theory.d/THEORY-504.md): In the Gemma Scope sparse autoencoders on Gemma 2, the two fidelity measures disagree by site: residual-stream autoencoders cost more next-token loss than MLP or attention ones at comparable fraction of variance unexplained, and base-model autoencoders transfer to the instruction-tuned model by loss more than by variance explained *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-509](../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md): Under genericity conditions, two dense or top-k (k ≥ 2) mixture-of-experts layers compute the same function only if they differ by a permutation of the experts with their gates and a common translation of the gate weights, and the translation leaves every interpolation barrier unchanged, so expert order is the only gate symmetry alignment must undo *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-566](../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md): In Ganea et al.'s hyperbolic neural networks, linear maps and nonlinearities are Euclidean ones read through the chart at the origin, so a stack of them without biases is a Euclidean network conjugated by that chart, and the curvature acts only through the bias translations and the distance-based output layer *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-668](../record/theory.d/THEORY-668.md): When the encoder is restricted to prunings of one fixed hierarchy of nested partitions, any non-negatively weighted sum of relevant information, irrelevant information and compression decomposes into per-node terms, so a bottom-up recursion finds the unique optimal tree with fewest leaves exactly in linear time, while greedy top-down splitting can miss information lying below a level that carries none; penalising irrelevant information only prunes the information-bottleneck tree *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-732](../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md): For ReLU networks interpolated linearly between two endpoints, weak additivity and commutativity at every layer make each layer's features exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features, output-layer linearity bounds the path's error by twice the endpoints', and for one hidden layer with interpolating minima linear mode connectivity alone gives the exact case *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-734](../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md): In the hyperbolic plane, a root carrying deg_max ≥ 15 chains of length m, embedded with worst-case distortion 1 + ε for ε ≤ 1, forces some node to hyperbolic distance at least (ℓ/(4ε))·ln(deg_max/(π√2)) from the origin, so fixed-point Poincaré coordinates need Ω((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-736](../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md): Two ε-dropout-stable solutions of a multilayer ReLU net, under a loss convex in the output, are joined by a piecewise-linear path whose loss never exceeds the worse endpoint's by more than ε, and joined pairwise paths compose with no higher barrier than their worst *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-738](../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md): In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-740](../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md): A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-741](../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md): A two-layer ReLU student of width at least kM, fitting an orthonormal teacher of M neurons on the sphere, has for any k global minima a global minimum joined to each by a two-piece linear path of minima; and in a deep linear network of depth L and width above 1 + r(L − 1), any r global minima in general position share a global minimum linearly connected to each *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-742](../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md): For a Boltzmann distribution linear in its couplings, observed through any coarse-graining map, the Fisher information the coarse data lose about the bare couplings is the expected conditional covariance of the energy operators given the coarse state; when the renormalized Hamiltonian stays in the family, the parameter map is linear and the additive constant of the step is analytic, that loss is the constant's Hessian, so the singular part of the metric passes unchanged to the coarse data.
