In the hopping model of diffusion at its Gaussian fixed point, keeping every n-th position of a trajectory of fixed duration multiplies the metric by n^(1−μ) in the μ-th Hermite coordinate: the drift's information is kept exactly, the variance's falls as 1/n, and higher shape parameters' faster *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-743](../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md): For finite X and Y, every information-bottleneck optimum at every β gives one encoder to all inputs sharing p(y|x), so it is a stochastic coarsening of the minimal sufficient partition (the causal states of memoryless transduction); as β → ∞ the optima converge to that partition, but in general no finite β attains it, except when Y is a function of X *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-745](../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md): For the reversible walk p = k/d built from a symmetric non-negative kernel on a finite connected set, the t-step diffusion distance is exactly the Euclidean distance between the coordinates λ_l^t ψ_l, and keeping only the coordinates with |λ_l|^t > δ|λ₁|^t errs in D_t² by at most δ²|λ₁|^{2t}(1/π(x) + 1/π(y)), an absolute bound and not the relative accuracy δ that Coifman and Lafon state; the truncated maps are nested as t grows, so with δ fixed the steps t order a refinement chain by eigenvalue modulus, while untruncated they are all invertible images of one another *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-746](../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md): Over a fixed finite set of basis functions, slow feature analysis is a generalized eigenproblem: the outputs that minimize ⟨ẏ²⟩ under zero mean, unit variance and decorrelation are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the derivative covariance against the covariance, in order of slowness, and a stack of such stages, each of whose function spaces contains its inputs, can only keep or lower each of its first m slowness values on the training signal, and may keep them *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-751](../record/theory.d/THEORY-751.md): For a memoryless source with finite alphabets and a per-letter distortion, a description at rate R(D₁) can be refined to distortion D₂ < D₁ at total rate R(D₂) iff some pair of rate–distortion-optimal test channels forms a Markov chain X → X̂₂ → X̂₁; the condition holds for every discrete source under Hamming distortion and fails for some three-letter sources under absolute error *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-753](../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md): For finite X and Y, the information bottleneck is successively refinable from budget λ₁ to λ₂ > λ₁ iff some pair of optimal encoders forms a Markov chain X → T₂ → T₁, that is, iff the coarse optimal encoder is a garbling of a fine one; when the fine optimum's decoder points q(X|t₂) are affinely independent, this holds for that pair iff every decoder point q(X|t₁) of the coarse optimum lies in their convex hull, so a failed hull test on optima that are unique up to merging and relabelling proves that refinement fails *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-757](../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md): The information bottleneck is successively refinable between every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X, by nested erasures of Y, and when X and Y are both binary, where the optimum at each nonzero budget is unique up to merging and relabelling and its two decoder points are the ends of an interval of the source simplex that only widens as the budget grows *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-758](../record/theory.d/THEORY-758.md): For a self-adjoint diffusion operator T with spectrum in [0, 1], the diffusion-wavelet levels are spectral subspaces spanned by the eigenvectors with λ^s ≥ ε for an increasing sequence of powers s, so they form an exactly nested chain of T-invariant subspaces whose differences are bands of the spectrum, about one octave each, not spatial blocks; Coifman and Maggioni's compressed algorithm, which squares the operator on each orthonormal basis, thresholds T^{2^{j−1}} at level j and not T^{2^j−1} as the paper states; and since each level is T-invariant, each is an exactly closed linear coarse-graining whose localized basis is a choice the level does not fix *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-774](../record/theory.d/THEORY-774.md): In a one-dimensional lattice hopping model with 2N+1 free hopping probabilities, all particles starting at the origin and the density after t steps observed with fixed Gaussian error, the Fisher metric is exactly t² times the distribution of the difference of two independent (t−1)-step walks, evaluated at the lag between the two hops, so it does not depend on the drift; when the walk is aperiodic with nonzero variance, its k-th largest eigenvalue is of order t^(3/2−k) for k = 0, …, 2N, so successive eigenvalues separate by a factor of order t *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-775](../record/theory.d/THEORY-775.md): With a Gaussian random-walk prior and an instantaneous unit-variance Gaussian encoder, the KL half of the evidence lower bound is the unordered slowness loss plus a constant; with a linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the bound is maximized on the span of the slowest SFA directions whose lag-one autocorrelation exceeds one half, with the basis inside that span unidentified, and on unwhitened input the maximizer is neither SFA's subspace nor invariant to rescaling the input *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-779](../record/theory.d/THEORY-779.md): In Kunin et al.'s underdamped Langevin model of SGD with momentum on linear regression, with gradient-noise covariance σ²H independent of the parameters, the stationary state is Gaussian with parameter covariance ησ²H(H + λI)⁻¹/(2S(1 − β)) and velocity covariance σ²H/(S(1 − β²)): for small weight decay it spreads equally along every nonzero Hessian direction and not along the null space, each Hessian eigenmode is a damped oscillator with damping ratio (1 − β)/√(2η(1 + β)(ρ + λ)), and the expected squared step is η²σ² tr(H)/(S(1 − β²)) *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-966](../record/theory.d/THEORY-966.md): Greedy edge pruning of the ACDC kind, which removes each edge whose removal changes the output metric by less than a threshold given the edges already removed, keeps only one input of a redundant OR gate, and which input it keeps depends on the order in which edges are visited, so when a model has redundant sufficient paths the circuit it returns is one of several sufficient subgraphs *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-968](../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md): In the Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark's causal-variable localization baselines on Gemma-2 2B and Llama-3.1 8B, features of the public Gemma Scope and Llama Scope sparse autoencoders, selected by a learned binary mask, never gave a higher mean interchange-intervention accuracy than the same mask over the model's own hidden dimensions, in all sixteen task–variable cells and by 1 to 14 points, while distributed alignment search, trained against the causal model it is scored on, gave the highest mean in fifteen of them *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-970](../record/theory.d/THEORY-970.md): On three language-model tasks whose circuits earlier manual work reported, indirect object identification and Greater-Than in GPT-2 Small and Python docstrings in a four-layer attention-only model, ACDC run with resampled corrupted activations against KL divergence ranked the reported edges with areas under the ROC curve of 0.85 to 0.98, above head-importance pruning and subnetwork probing on all three; on two compiled tracr programs it ranked them poorly with corrupted activations, 0.68 and 0.20, and exactly with zero activations *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-973](../record/theory.d/THEORY-973.md): In small attention-only transformer language models of two to six layers, in-context learning, measured as the loss at token 500 minus the loss at token 50, appears abruptly in one early window of training in which induction heads form, and ablating those heads at test time removes nearly all of it; one-layer models show neither, and letting a single layer attend by the previous token brings the jump to one-layer models and moves it earlier in two-layer ones *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-974](../record/theory.d/THEORY-974.md): When a transformer's MLP sublayers are replaced by transcoders and the attention patterns and LayerNorm scales on a prompt are held fixed, the contribution of an earlier transcoder feature at the same token to a later one's pre-activation is the earlier feature's activation times the dot product of its decoder with the later feature's encoder, scaled by one LayerNorm constant per token, so the weight factor is fixed by the trained weights and holds on every input *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-975](../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md): In a two-layer attention-only transformer trained on the Pile, the weight-refined local learning coefficients of individual attention heads start alike and diverge over training, and clustering the curves groups the heads by the functional types that ablation assigns them at the end of training, previous-token, current-token, induction and n-gram-memorizing; among layer-1 heads, those running simple algorithms end with the lowest values and those memorizing the most n-grams with the highest *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-977](../record/theory.d/THEORY-977.md): In the two-layer attention-only transformer that Elhage et al. reverse-engineer, the second-layer heads that compose substantially with first-layer heads do so through their keys, mainly with a head that attends to the previous token and, after the published correction, also with one that attends over the last several tokens; these heads are induction heads, attending from a token to the one after its earlier occurrence, including on repeated random tokens, with positive-eigenvalue copying OV and same-matching QK circuits, and the second-order virtual-head terms add little to the loss reduction *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-978](../record/theory.d/THEORY-978.md): Causal scrubbing scores a hypothesis through the partitions of the dataset that its interpretation nodes induce, so two hypotheses that assign different features to a node but induce the same partition on the dataset, such as two features perfectly correlated on it, receive the same score *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-979](../record/theory.d/THEORY-979.md): On one prompt, a transformer whose MLPs are replaced by a cross-layer transcoder, with its attention patterns and normalization denominators frozen and each MLP's reconstruction error added back as a constant, reproduces the model's activations and outputs exactly and is linear between features, so each active feature's pre-activation is the sum of its attribution-graph edges and constants; a perturbation that clamps MLP outputs up to the target feature's encoder layer then confirms a direct edge by construction, and tests only knock-on effects and the output *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-980](../record/theory.d/THEORY-980.md): In GPT-2 small on fifteen templates of indirect object identification, a circuit of 26 attention heads in seven classes, found by path patching, keeps 87% of the model's mean logit difference when every other head is mean-ablated; knocking out its three main name mover heads costs only 5%, because other heads take over, and knockout sets found by greedy search make the circuit and the full model differ by up to 87% of the logit difference, so the circuit is faithful on average and incomplete under knockouts *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-981](../record/theory.d/THEORY-981.md): When a data distribution is unchanged by a group of orthogonal transformations under which a network is equivariant, the weights fixed by that group form a subspace that population gradient descent never leaves; for attention-only transformers on block-list inductive tasks, with fixed orthogonal write maps, Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann compute this subspace as the span of a few elementary token and position actions composed through the heads, and an elementwise optimizer such as sign descent keeps it only when those actions are aligned with the parameter coordinates *(used by 5; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-983](../record/theory.d/THEORY-983.md): In Geiger et al.'s three-layer feed-forward network trained on hierarchical equality and in BERT fine-tuned on monotonicity inference, interchange interventions on subspaces found by a learned rotation aligned the hypothesised two-variable causal models with interchange intervention accuracy of 1.00 on the rotation's training data, where the axis-aligned alignment closest to the learned rotation reached 0.73 and 0.51; in BERT, the learned lexical-entailment subspace was in turn aligned, at 0.97 to 0.98, with a model holding only the identities of the two words *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-992](../record/theory.d/THEORY-992.md): In sparse autoencoders of about 1M, 4M and 34M features on Claude 3 Sonnet's middle-layer residual stream, whether a concept among chemical elements, cities, animals and foods had a dedicated feature depended on how often it occurs in the training data: the frequency at which a concept became more than 50% likely to have one was slightly below one over the number of live features, and the three dictionaries' curves roughly coincided when frequency was rescaled by that number *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-994](../record/theory.d/THEORY-994.md): In Ameisen et al.'s evaluations, the local replacement model of their 18-layer language model, built from a 10-million-feature cross-layer transcoder, responded to small perturbations much as the model did one layer after the intervention and increasingly differently over later layers, more in the size of the effect than its direction and slightly more for larger dictionaries, and over 20 prompts the graph's influence of one feature on another ranked the effect of ablating the first on the second with a Spearman correlation of 0.72 *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-996](../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md): On Pythia language models from 410M to 12B parameters, in three single prompt pairs and two small prompt distributions, verifying attention or neuron nodes by activation patching in the order given by attribution patching, a first-order gradient estimate of each node's noising effect, found the nodes with the largest effects at about 2 to 50 times the cost of an oracle ordering, below unordered patching, subsampling and block search in every setting; its misses were concentrated in queries and keys behind saturated attention and in nodes whose direct and indirect effects nearly cancel *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1002](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1002.md): On frozen randomly initialized feed-forward networks at chance on hierarchical equality, with 16 input dimensions, distributed alignment search for the two-equality causal model reached interchange intervention accuracy of 0.50 to 0.51 at hidden sizes up to 256 but 0.55 at 1,028 and 0.64 at 4,096, so in a hidden layer much wider than the input a learned rotation can produce above-chance interchange accuracy for an algorithm the network does not implement *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1006](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1006.md): In the dependent Indian buffet process each item's feature indicator is a Gaussian process thresholded at the quantile of a stick length that does not change with the covariate, so its prevalence is the same at every covariate value and its persistence is set separately by the covariance; the whole feature matrix at a covariate value is an Indian buffet process only when there is no shared feature-level process, and with one the items are correlated and fewer features are occupied *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1007](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1007.md): On four subject–verb agreement tasks in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, circuits of sparse-autoencoder features and autoencoder error nodes, selected by linear estimates of indirect effect, carried half or more of the behaviour on held-out pairs with about 100 and 500 nodes, where circuits of neurons needed about 1,500 and more than 30,000; with the error nodes removed, the same feature circuits carried little of it, under about a quarter in Pythia and almost none in Gemma *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1009](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1009.md): In Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann's two-layer attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, once an in-weights circuit that maps each common token to its memorized partner has saturated, the population gradient on the induction circuit is what it would be without it multiplied by fr + (1 − fr)fv, the share of the data the memorized map does not solve, up to errors that vanish at large vocabulary and large in-weights margin when no distractor block carries the query's partner; the two circuits occupy orthogonal coordinates and still interact, because they solve overlapping parts of the data *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1020](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1020.md): In a two-layer attention-only language model, on tokens where induction helps, the standard induction circuit (queries and values from the token embedding, keys from the previous-token head) accounts for 35% of the loss its two induction heads contribute, and a hypothesis that adds three-token matching, layer 0's average effect and three layer-0 heads acting as if they attended to the current token accounts for 86% *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1023](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md): Attribution patching estimates the effect of patching an activation from a clean run into a corrupted run as the difference between the two activations dotted with the gradient of the metric on the corrupted run, so the estimates for every activation come from two forward passes and one backward pass and add over sub-components; the estimate is exact when the metric is affine in the activation, gives no effect for a nonlinearity in saturation whatever the true change, and through LayerNorm ignores the component of a patch along the vector being normalized *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1029](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1029.md): On a three-layer parenthesis-balance classifier, causal-scrubbing hypotheses that resample the terms of one head's input separately scored 81% and 84% of the loss recovered against 77% for the less specific hypothesis they refine, and the authors attribute the rise to resampling washing out a signal, not to a better explanation *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1255](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1255.md): Near a non-degenerate minimum, constant-rate SGD's stationary distribution is a Gaussian set by learning rate, batch size and preconditioner, which can be tuned to match the posterior at a given sample size; training time enters only as the wait for stationarity *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1257](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1257.md): Averaging constant-rate SGD iterates at stationarity gives a covariance that shrinks with the number of examples processed, and equals the Gaussian posterior's for that many observations when the noise covariance equals the Hessian *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1258](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1258.md): The steady state of Hennick and De Baerdemacker's fractional Fokker–Planck model of SGD is a tempered posterior only within a region of constant effective diffusion; the weights between regions, where accessibility would act, are not derived *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1275](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md): In the toy model of superposition, at the paper's one SGD setting, the Bayesian counterparts of the observed training chain 4⁺⁺⁻ → 4⁺ → 5 → 5⁺ have critical sample sizes that rise in the order training meets it at the point estimates of the learning coefficients, though not across their spread; SGD was not seen to take the posterior's main transition, 5 → 6, and trained on 1,000 samples it ends in a phase that the posterior at n = 1,000, dominated by the 6-gon, does not favour *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1304](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1304.md): In latent Dirichlet allocation each document draws its own topic mixture from a Dirichlet shared across the corpus and draws a topic afresh for every word, a three-level model of conditionally independent assignments; the mixture of unigrams, which draws one topic per document, is its two-level comparison, and the Dirichlet is a distribution over mixtures, not over topics *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1330](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1330.md): In Gemma 2 27B, Qwen 3 32B and Llama 3.3 70B, activation vectors for 275 prompted character roles span a low-dimensional space whose first principal component runs from fantastical to Assistant-like roles, with role loadings correlated above 0.92 between models and the default Assistant at its extreme; the contrast vector from the default Assistant to the role mean aligns with it and is largely present before post-training *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1339](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1339.md): In Lu et al.'s synthetic multi-turn conversations, with frontier models playing the user (100 conversations of up to 15 turns per domain, three target and three user models), the mean position of a chat model's responses along the Assistant Axis stays in the Assistant range in coding conversations and, apart from some drift in Gemma, in writing ones, and drifts to the non-Assistant end in therapy-like and AI-philosophy ones; ridge regression on embeddings of the latest user message predicts the next response's position (R² 0.53–0.77) but not its change from the previous response (R² 0.10), from which the authors infer that position depends most strongly on the most recent user message rather than on where it was before, the message itself depending on the conversation *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1350](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1350.md): The Persona Selection Model holds that pre-training gives a language model a distribution over personas, that post-training updates it into a posterior over Assistant personas which runtime context keeps conditioning, and that the Assistant's traits are a key determiner of behaviour; it disowns a single coherent persona and exhaustiveness, and names as open a router that selects personas and could carry goals no persona has *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1357](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1357.md): Lake, Salakhutdinov and Tenenbaum report that a model representing handwritten characters as probabilistic programs, composing strokes from primitives fit to 30 background alphabets into types whose executions give tokens, erred 3.3% against people's 4.5% on 20-way one-shot classification within 10 held-out Omniglot alphabets, and that judges identified its exemplars and new characters at 49–59%, near chance; removing compositionality raised its error to 14.0% and made its productions easier to detect, inflating its learned token-level variability raised error to 11.0% and made exemplars easier to detect, and replacing its learned type-level priors with uniform ones left classification unchanged (3.5%) and exemplars not reliably easier to detect, but made its new characters easier to detect (64–69%) *(used by 1)*

## Formal apparatus

- [THEORY-004](../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md): A representation is determined by its centred kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal transformation, and the rotation-aligned distance between two representations equals the Bures distance between their kernels *(used by 6; also pragmatic-transport, distributed-agency, learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-008](../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md): On a finite set of stimuli, what a regularized linear readout can decode from a representation is a function of its normalized kernel, and CKA, CCA and GULP are averages of readout agreement *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-009](../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md): In the positive-pair spectral self-supervised papers, self-adjointness comes from the symmetry of the positive-pair distribution, not from the Riesz representation theorem; elsewhere in the family it comes from a symmetrized loss, a precondition on the kernel, or composing the conditional-expectation operator with its adjoint *(used by 4; also learned-structure, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-012](../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md): An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality *(used by 8; also pragmatic-transport, organizational-normativity)*
- [THEORY-014](../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md): In both formalisms of contextuality, classicality is the existence of a nonnegative version of a linear representation that always exists over the reals, so negativity is universal and only its unavoidability is nonclassical *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-018](../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md): Softmax training identifies a language model's final-layer representation only up to an invertible linear map, so no inner product on it is intrinsic, and Park, Choe and Veitch's causal inner product is fixed by a stipulation *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-019](../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md): Symmetry forces spectral degeneracy but degeneracy does not identify a symmetry: an operator commuting with a group has eigenspaces built from its real irreducibles, so abelian rotation groups force pairs over ℝ, and the spectrum fixes neither the group nor a basis inside a multiplet *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-026](../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md): For a system driven without feedback through fixed kernels, the average work dissipated at each switch of the drive equals the memory that fails to predict the next input; that is nonnegative when the drive is Markov and, summed, bounds the protocol's dissipation from below when each kernel keeps its equilibrium stationary, so there only nonpredictive memory is wasteful; with feedback, in one binary channel no predictive agent is efficient *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-027](../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md): Two individually decisive people, weak Pareto and an unrestricted domain cannot all hold, even when choice need only yield a best element; unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, will-organization, organizational-affect, authenticity)*
- [THEORY-030](../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md): For a memory evolving reversibly with its environment, Landauer's bound prices only steps that lose logical distinguishability, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit lost, exported to the environment and not necessarily as heat, so copying onto a blank register, measuring or evaluating a bit has no minimum cost; learning a label has a floor only in total entropy production, at least the information learnt, which in Goldt and Seifert's perceptron can be paid in the weights' own entropy with vanishing heat *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-031](../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md): The likelihood-ratio detector is optimal under the payoff, Neyman–Pearson and posterior criteria, which differ only in its threshold, so performance is an ROC and the criterion a point on it; d′ is criterion-free only for equal-variance normal signal and noise *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-032](../record/theory.d/THEORY-032.md): The Yoneda lemma determines an object only up to isomorphism, from its whole hom-functor, among objects the category already has; as a formal version of "an object is determined by its relations" it presupposes the relata *(used by 12; also pragmatic-transport, realizability)*
- [THEORY-087](../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md): The Bayesian complexity penalty grows as (d/2) log n in a regular model, where the curvature at the optimum sets the Occam factor, and as λ log n in a singular one, where λ is the real log canonical threshold; with the prior positive on the optimal set, λ falls below d/2 when that set is infinite or has a point of degenerate curvature, and equals d/2 when it is finitely many points of non-degenerate curvature *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-158](../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md): For a Markov process on a finite state space, an observable commutes with the generator exactly when its mean and variance are both conserved in every state, which is exactly when it is constant on each connected component of the transition graph, so a conserved mean alone does not give a symmetry *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-160](../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md): In the algebraic Hamiltonian setting, symmetry and conservation correspond because the bracket is antisymmetric, which for a bilinear bracket is each observable conserving itself; the theorem's content lies in identifying observables with generators *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-171](../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md): When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-190](../record/theory.d/THEORY-190.md): Under geometric coarse-graining of the S¹ hidden-metric network model, which merges blocks of r angular neighbours into supernodes linked if any of their members were, the supernodes' link probability approaches the S¹ form with β kept, κ′ = (Σκ^β)^{1/β}, μ′ = μ/r and R′ = R/r, its ratio to that form tending to 1 as their separation grows large against the block width and the coupling μκ′κ″; between nearby supernodes it exceeds that form *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-194](../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md): On Monte Carlo samples of the 2D Ising model and of the 2D dimer model with added noise spins, a block coarse-graining trained to maximize mutual information with the system beyond a buffer recovered the variables renormalization already uses (Kadanoff block spins; the dimers' low-momentum electric fields, with no weight on the noise), and iterated on 128 × 128 Ising samples gave the flow away from the critical point, locating it to about 1% and giving ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a restricted Boltzmann machine trained by contrastive divergence on the noisy dimer data coupled to the noise and to columnar patterns instead *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-198](../record/theory.d/THEORY-198.md): For a finite-range lattice Hamiltonian, a block coarse-graining that keeps all the mutual information the block shares with the system beyond a buffer makes the coarse measure factorize across the block, in 1D and, in D dimensions, when capture by a hyperplane of blocks amounts to capture by each block; barring exact cancellation of existing couplings, the renormalized Hamiltonian then gains no range, and in 1D product disorder gains no correlations across the block. The coarse-grainings actually optimized fall short of that condition, and for them the link is computed only for two-spin blocks of 1D Ising chains *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-202](../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md): In variational renormalization over general Boltzmann machines, neither a matched partition function nor Kadanoff's exact trace condition makes a coarse-graining a renormalization: the first holds for joint Hamiltonians whose marginal is not the data, the second for hidden variables that do not interact with the system, so the variables a renormalization keeps must be fixed by a further stated condition *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-205](../record/theory.d/THEORY-205.md): For a short-range lattice model on a cylinder with a symmetric transfer matrix whose leading excited eigenvalue is non-degenerate, with block and environment as slabs L_B transfer steps apart, the uninformative information-bottleneck encoder first loses stability at β = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B), in the direction of the boundary weak value of the leading excited eigenvector, which by the cited conformal finite-size relation is the lowest-dimension primary at large circumference; the uninformative encoder can stop being optimal at a smaller β, and nothing is shown for blocks inside a buffer shell or for the fixed-alphabet RSMI optimum *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-206](../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md): For networks of smooth units without biases, one hidden layer needs exactly ∏(rᵢ+1) neurons to match the monomial x₁^r₁⋯xₙ^rₙ's Taylor polynomial at the origin, and a deep network O(Σ log rᵢ), with the upper bounds holding for uniform approximation too, so the cost of flattening a polynomial grows exponentially with its degree in distinct variables and not with the number of inputs: products of many inputs separate depths, bounded-degree polynomials do not *(used by 3; also learned-structure)*
- [THEORY-222](../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md): With uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a coarse-grained macro description of a known discrete mechanism can have more effective information than the micro description it supervenes on, so the level at which effective information is highest can be a macro level *(used by 6; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-233](../record/theory.d/THEORY-233.md): CKA and normalized Bures similarity are the Euclidean and the Bures comparison of normalized kernels, and each bounds the other only within a factor set by the kernels' ranks, so agreement in one does not carry to the other with a dimension-free constant *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-236](../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md): A representational similarity index that is invariant to every invertible linear map takes the same value on all representations whose rank equals the number of examples *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-244](../record/theory.d/THEORY-244.md): For a computable source distribution f, Shannon entropy and mutual information are the expectations of their Kolmogorov counterparts only to within the complexity of f: 0 ≤ E K(x) − H(f) ≤ K(f) + O(1), and I(X;Y) − K(f) − O(1) ≤ E I(x:y) ≤ I(X;Y) + 2K(f) + O(1); Grünwald and Vitányi's matching statement for the distortion-rate function rests on a step the record has not verified *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-255](../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md): In Aerts's subspace model of Hampton's membership data, and in any lattice whose membership weight is order-preserving, whatever its negation, taking concept conjunction and disjunction as meet and join cannot produce overextension or underextension, so a model of the guppy-type deviations must take conjunction as some operation other than the meet or drop the monotone weight, while the Kolmogorov-type deviations can be had from the meet of a non-Boolean subspace lattice *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-260](../record/theory.d/THEORY-260.md): An individual string's information splits non-trivially into structure and noise only in a model class without a universal member: with partial recursive models every string's minimal sufficient statistic is trivial, while with total recursive functions it is not, and the finite-set, computable-distribution and total-function classes agree to within logarithmic terms *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-261](../record/theory.d/THEORY-261.md): In sparse distributed memory, recall of uniform random data from exact cues is a signal-to-noise problem whose optimum activates about (2MT)^-1/3 of the hard locations, and capacity then grows in proportion to the number of hard locations, rising toward about a tenth of them at 0.999 bit fidelity, not with the word length *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-297](../record/theory.d/THEORY-297.md): A bijection between shapes is equivalent, up to null sets, to the linear operator it induces on functions; in orthonormal bases a volume-preserving bijection's matrix is orthogonal, and an isometry's commutes with the Laplace–Beltrami operator, so it maps each eigenspace to the matching eigenspace *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-299](../record/theory.d/THEORY-299.md): Structured and translational knowledge-graph embeddings are 0-cochains of a cellular sheaf of vector spaces pulled back from the schema, each triple scored by a norm of the coboundary on its edge and, in the squared-Euclidean form, the whole graph by the sheaf Laplacian; since the zero cochain is always a global section, what they learn is a contrastive margin, not the existence of a section *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-304](../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md): In plane Couette and Poiseuille flow, measured in the energy norm, the linearized operator is so far from normal that perturbations can grow transiently by O(R) and resonate by O(R²), and operator perturbations of size O(R⁻²) make it eigenvalue-unstable, at Reynolds numbers where eigenvalue analysis predicts stability *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-313](../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md): With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight for every pair of distributions only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus, with Fourier coefficients proportional to e^(−σ‖ω‖₁) and strictly positive Lipschitz densities, is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-336](../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md): An ideal observer is optimal relative to the information it is given, so a constrained ideal is the optimal decoder of a degraded input, not a restricted decoder of the full one; comparing real observers with ideals taken at successive stages of the visual system places losses by stage, and in early-vision tasks human performance is reported often to parallel the retinal-stage ideal across conditions while falling well below it *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-349](../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md): For binary outcomes and a fixed representation of individuals, a predictor can pass every test in a bounded class without being close to nature: outcome indistinguishability to tests that see the sampled prediction is equivalent, with stated losses, to multicalibration over a closely related class of sets, a predictor meeting it exists at size polynomial in the tests' size and the tolerance whatever nature's complexity, and learning one is as hard as weak agnostic learning of the class *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-352](../record/theory.d/THEORY-352.md): A pseudorandom generator exists if and only if a one-way function exists, where both are secure against uniform adversaries and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine, as statements about ensembles indexed by n; the construction from an arbitrary one-way function is only weak-preserving, so security at one length is bought at a much greater one *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-354](../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md): An observer's power to refute a predictor depends on its access to the predictor as well as on its budget: against tests that see only the sampled prediction a predictor of size O(s/ε²) always passes, but if fine-grained clique counting is hard, or BPP ≠ PSPACE, some cheap tests that may query the predictor adaptively pass only predictors about as costly as nature's own *(used by 3; also realizability, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-357](../record/theory.d/THEORY-357.md): Computational indistinguishability is strictly coarser than statistical closeness: without any assumption there are ensembles on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform, though none of them is efficiently samplable, and an efficiently samplable pair of this kind exists if a pseudorandom generator does, since its output covers at most 2^n of the 2^l(n) strings; all of it is about ensembles indexed by n, not single pairs of distributions *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-358](../record/theory.d/THEORY-358.md): In visual search among up to about 36 well-spaced items, a target that alone carries one colour or one distinctive shape part is found in time almost independent of the number of items, while a target identified only by a combination of features its neighbours carry separately takes time that grows linearly with the number of items, about twice as fast when the target is absent, the pattern of a serial self-terminating scan, and practice did not remove it; that conjunctions rather than similarity cause it is the paper's reading, not its result *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-361](../record/theory.d/THEORY-361.md): When every object but one has full grade in exactly one of two attribute-sorted lists and the one has full grade in both, finding it under min takes at least about half the objects' worth of accesses for any algorithm that only reads the lists from the top and looks up objects already seen, and, with the tied objects in random order, about as many in expectation even for algorithms that may look up any object; a query on one attribute alone costs k accesses whatever the number of objects *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-366](../record/theory.d/THEORY-366.md): With a fixed number of data points and a query drawn independently of them, if the variance of the p-th power of the query-to-point distance divided by its mean tends to zero, the farthest point comes within any factor 1 + ε of the nearest with probability tending to one; independent coordinates meet this condition, while data on a low-dimensional subspace, or queries that fall inside well-separated clusters, escape it *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-370](../record/theory.d/THEORY-370.md): On an n × n lattice whose nodes also get long-range links drawn with probability proportional to lattice distance to the power −r, a searcher that knows only the target's position and the links of nodes already reached delivers in expected time polylogarithmic in n only at r = 2: greedy routing then takes O((log n)²) steps, while for 0 ≤ r < 2 every such searcher needs Ω(n^((2−r)/3)) steps and for r > 2 Ω(n^((r−2)/(r−1))), even at r = 0 where short paths exist *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-372](../record/theory.d/THEORY-372.md): For c-approximate near-neighbour search over n points in Euclidean space, space n^{1+ρu+o(1)} and query time n^{ρq+o(1)} are achievable on any data set whenever c²√ρq + (c²−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c²−1) (c√ρq + (c−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c−1) in Hamming space), and no list-of-points structure, the model of known data-independent hashing, does better on random instances; without that model the curve is matched only at query time n^{o(1)} by one or two cell probes *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-384](../record/theory.d/THEORY-384.md): A nearest-neighbour graph built by pruning each point's links against all other points with a factor α > 1, so that from every point some link is α times closer to any other point, lets greedy search from any start reach a ((α+1)/(α−1) + ε)-approximate nearest neighbour in O(log_α(∆/((α−1)ε))) steps of cost O((4α)^d log ∆), for doubling dimension d and aspect ratio ∆; the ratio is tight and the dependence on ∆ cannot be replaced by one on n, and the build takes O(n³) time done naively *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-388](../record/theory.d/THEORY-388.md): Locality-sensitive hashing answers approximate near-neighbour queries over n points with O(n^ρ) hash evaluations in O(dn + n^{1+ρ}) space, where ρ = ln(1/p1)/ln(1/p2) is set by how much more often near pairs collide than far ones and is at most 1/(1+ε) for approximation 1+ε in Hamming space, with constant success probability per query; the paper gives upper bounds only and proves no limit on what organizing can buy *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-390](../record/theory.d/THEORY-390.md): Any distribution of n × N matrices whose norms concentrate as Johnson–Lindenstrauss proofs require gives the restricted isometry property of order k with probability at least 1 − 2e^{−c₂n} for k ≤ c₁n/log(N/k), by a union bound over (12/δ)^k net points on each of the (eN/k)^k sparse supports; this makes k log(N/k) measurements sufficient for Gaussian, ±1 and sparse three-valued matrices, and does not show they are necessary *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-391](../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md): Recovery of a k-sparse vector by ℓ₁ minimization from n random measurements in dimension N switches, as N grows with δ = n/N and ρ = k/n fixed, from near-certain success to near-certain failure across a curve ρ(δ) that, for Gaussian matrices, the authors' earlier face-counting theorems fix; in 2,948,000 optimizations at N = 200, 400 and 1600, eight non-Gaussian ensembles approached that curve in a way consistent with gaps shrinking as N^(−1/2), an exponent fitted on the same data, while at finite N the location depended on the ensemble *(used by 3; also realizability)*
- [THEORY-393](../record/theory.d/THEORY-393.md): Any two families of n vectors of norm at most 1 have images in ⌊C log(2 + ε²n)/ε²⌋ dimensions whose cross inner products ⟨x_i, y_j⟩ are each within an additive ε of the originals, found by a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, which for small ε is below the log n/ε² of the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma; only cross products are kept, the new vectors' norms are not bounded, and whether one set can be embedded that small is open *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-395](../record/theory.d/THEORY-395.md): For ε between about lg^0.5001 n/√min{n, d} and 1, some n-point set in ℝ^d needs Ω(ε⁻² lg(ε²n)) dimensions under any map, linear or not, that keeps its pairwise squared distances within 1 ± ε, so a random projection with a union bound is optimal up to a constant for the worst set; nearly orthogonal sets can need fewer, and the bound says nothing about typical data *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-397](../record/theory.d/THEORY-397.md): A random linear map into k ≥ 4(ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ ln n dimensions keeps every pairwise squared distance of a fixed set of n points in ℓ₂ within 1 ± ε, because each difference vector's squared length concentrates with tails exp(−(k/2)(ε²/2 − ε³/3)) and a union bound over the pairs costs only ln n; the proofs cover a random subspace, Gaussian entries and independent zero-mean ±1 or √3·{+1, 0, −1} entries, and no matrix with nonnegative entries *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-399](../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md): Storing every inner product of n points of the unit ball of R^k to additive error ε takes Θ(n log n/ε²) bits once k ≥ log n/ε² and Θ(nk log(2 + log n/(ε²k))) below, for 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, and comparing these counts across dimensions shows that some n such points cannot be mapped into fewer than Ω(min{k, log(2 + ε²n)/ε²}) dimensions with additive error ε for every ε ≥ 2/√n; this is a worst-case lower bound with unstated constants, the small-ε bit count is open for k above that dimension, and no one-family embedding that small is proved *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-424](../record/theory.d/THEORY-424.md): Mutual-information measures of individuality that read a system's next state off its present one measure association, not propagation: I(S_{t+1}; S_t) can be positive when the environment alone drives the system, and conditioning on the environment does not recover the interventional quantity, which can be zero where the conditional measure is one bit *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-548](../record/theory.d/THEORY-548.md): In generalised Lotka–Volterra dynamics with every interaction delayed by τ, a feasible equilibrium that is stable without delay loses stability at τ_c = min over the community eigenvalues j of arctan(|Re j|/|Im j|)/|j|, where a pair of roots crosses the imaginary axis transversally (a Hopf point), so the critical delay is set by the community spectrum; in Saeedian et al.'s strongly self-regulated setting the oscillating regime's community-level variability falls with diversity (S = 10–70) while species-level variability rises, and the fall matches what summing independently oscillating species gives *(used by 2; also records-of-inquiry)*
- [THEORY-585](../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md): In the Döring–Isham scheme for realising collections of systems in topoi, disjoint sums of quantum systems compose exactly; along a tensor product of finite-dimensional systems, the pull-back of a constituent's quantity agrees with the composite's own quantity at a context exactly when every projection in it with proper support on the first factor has the form P⊗1, so it fails for every non-scalar quantity and no operator on the composite realises the pull-back *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-634](../record/theory.d/THEORY-634.md): In a ring of M chemotactic catalyst species, each making the next one's substrate, the non-reciprocal nearest-neighbour coupling makes the linear stability matrix circulant: the uniform state goes unstable for any M exactly when the species attract themselves, and the parity of M then decides the leading mode, a real alternating mode for even M that sorts species by parity into two static clusters, and a complex pair for odd M that can give persistent oscillation *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-641](../record/theory.d/THEORY-641.md): Under a well-specified, identifiable parametric Markov model of the target given the joint past, with ergodic lagged states, transfer entropy is the limit of the normalised log-likelihood ratio for the null of no dependence on the source's past, so it is Granger-sense predictive improvement; for finite-state chains the plug-in estimator is exactly that statistic, and under the null and the usual regularity it is asymptotically χ² with the difference in parameter counts as degrees of freedom *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-700](../record/theory.d/THEORY-700.md): For jointly Gaussian stationary processes, Granger causality in Geweke's generalized-variance form is exactly twice the transfer entropy, conditional and multivariate, at the regressions' lags, because least-squares residual covariance is the partial covariance and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is half its log-determinant plus a constant *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-702](../record/theory.d/THEORY-702.md): Transfer entropy is the average of a local transfer entropy, the log ratio at each observation of the destination's next-state probability with and without the source given the destination's past, which can be negative where the source misleads; the destination history must be long for it to exclude self-influence routed through the source; and conditioning also on the destination's other causal parents (complete) can differ sharply from conditioning on its past alone (apparent), as in elementary cellular automata, where long-history local transfer entropy picks out gliders and domain walls *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-704](../record/theory.d/THEORY-704.md): In a stationary multivariate time series whose components include every relevant process, with interventions that are isolated exogenous changes and no instantaneous causation, a missing Granger-causal edge from a to b means intervening on a has no effect on b at the next step, non-ancestry means no effect at any horizon, and a set whose observed past blocks every back-door path into b's ancestors identifies the effect from observational data, as a multi-step linear-predictor coefficient in the Gaussian case *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-705](../record/theory.d/THEORY-705.md): For a target and two sources with finite alphabets, if unique information is to depend only on the two source–target pair marginals, then the minimum of the conditional mutual information over all joints with those marginals is an upper bound on every non-negative decomposition's unique information, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds; this unique information vanishes exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient, and the measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate partial-information axioms and the identity property, and do not extend to three sources on the partial-information lattice *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-706](../record/theory.d/THEORY-706.md): Any redundancy function defined on the lattice of antichains of sources, ordered so that a collection precedes another when every source of the latter contains one of the former, has a Möbius inverse that decomposes the information a set of sources gives about a target into partial-information atoms summing to every subset's mutual information; for the I_min redundancy, the expected minimum specific information over sources, every atom is nonnegative, and interaction information is a signed mixture of atoms, synergy minus redundancy for three variables *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-707](../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md): Transfer entropy is not a measure of information flow, if flow means information in the target attributable solely to the source's past: as a conditional mutual information it equals the source's unique information plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a full bit to a source that carries none alone (Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}) and report zero from each of two sources that jointly fix the target (Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}); conditioning on further series, as causation entropy does, has the same fault *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-708](../record/theory.d/THEORY-708.md): The I_min redundancy credits two independent sources with shared information whenever each reduces surprise about the same target outcomes, so it gives two independent bits copied into the target 1 bit of redundancy; a bivariate redundancy built from reverse information projections, each source's information less what is lost when its posteriors are replaced by mixtures of the other's, satisfies symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity and the identity property, gives a nonnegative decomposition, and agrees with I_min on XOR, AND and their compositions but can reverse the state-independent/state-dependent split of a transfer entropy *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-709](../record/theory.d/THEORY-709.md): Mutual information between continuous variables can be estimated from k-nearest-neighbour statistics, with the joint k-th-neighbour distance in the maximum norm fixing the scale at which marginal neighbours are counted, so that the biases of the three entropy estimates largely cancel; the one approximation is a locally constant density, the systematic error scales with k/N, and exactness for independent variables is observed in every tested case but not proved *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-710](../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md): In a finite causal Bayesian network, a set of nodes is causally independent of another, imposing a third, for every choice of mechanisms exactly when every directed path between them passes through the third; information flow, conditional mutual information computed from interventional instead of observational distributions, vanishes under causal independence, and it can differ from transfer entropy and conditional mutual information in either direction *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-711](../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md): Directed information from an input sequence to an output sequence, the sum over time of the information the inputs up to now carry about the current output given the past outputs, is at most their mutual information and equal to it when the channel is used without feedback; in a causal system it bounds what the output reveals about the source, so feedback cannot raise a memoryless channel's capacity; and the usual definition of a memoryless channel holds only without feedback *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-712](../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md): Under any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations, a transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t | X_t) is the unique information of the source's past about the target's next state plus the synergy of source and target pasts, which Williams and Beer call state-independent and state-dependent transfer; time-delayed mutual information is the unique part plus redundancy; with the I_min redundancy the state-independent part alone suffices for perfect open-loop control, and a two-source transfer entropy splits into unique, redundant and synergistic transfer *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-713](../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md): No redundancy measure on the Williams–Beer partial-information lattice can satisfy symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity, the identity axiom and non-negative atoms once there are three sources: for two independent bits, their XOR and a target that copies all three, identity forces three one-bit atoms under a two-bit total, so one atom is at most −1 bit, and a multivariate decomposition that keeps identity must give up non-negativity or the lattice *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-714](../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md): Ince's I_ccs, the expected local co-information over only those events where every source, the joint source and the overlap change the target's surprisal in the same direction, under the maximum-entropy joint that preserves the source–target and joint-source marginals, is symmetric and self-redundant and satisfies the independent identity property; it fails Harder et al.'s identity and monotonicity, so its atoms can be negative, and, though its paper says otherwise, it fails subset equality *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-715](../record/theory.d/THEORY-715.md): The information about a target carried by the Gács–Körner common random variable of the sources is a redundancy defined for any number of sources that is nonnegative, target-monotone and no larger than I_min, and is a lower bound on any reasonable redundancy; but it counts only deterministic shared structure, so it is zero whenever the sources' joint distribution has full support, fails the identity property and continuity, and gives negative synergy already for two sources *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-717](../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md): For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix *(used by 7; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-718](../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md): In a linear-in-parameters model with Gaussian noise and a Gaussian prior, the evidence is exactly the best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor set by the posterior curvature, and when the design grows linearly with n that factor costs (k/2) log n *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-723](../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md): For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-724](../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md): For a linear system du/dt = A(t)u, non-normality is necessary for time dependence to destabilize an operator that is uniformly stable at every instant, and a non-normal operator neutral at every instant can be asymptotically unstable under switching *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-727](../record/theory.d/THEORY-727.md): For a fixed linear operator in an inner-product norm, growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound only from below; it starts at the numerical abscissa, which can be positive when every mode decays; and the forced response is bounded by the condition number of the eigenvectors over the distance to the spectrum *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-733](../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md): For a stable linear Gaussian VAR(p), a linear coarse-graining is exactly dynamically independent iff its row space is invariant under the transpose of every lag matrix, so for p ≥ 2 almost no parameter set has one at any scale, while for p = 1 they are the transpose's invariant subspaces, which exist on open sets but not generically at every scale *(used by 10; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-744](../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md): As the kernel width ε goes to 0, Coifman and Lafon's α-normalized diffusion operator (I − P_{ε,α})/ε, for data sampled with density q = e^{−U} from a compact manifold without boundary, converges uniformly on smooth functions, at rate O(ε), to Δf + 2(1 − α)⟨∇U, ∇f⟩ with Δ the non-negative Laplace–Beltrami operator, which is minus the generator of a reversible diffusion with drift −2(1 − α)∇U and invariant density proportional to q^{2(1−α)}; α = 0 gives potential 2U and invariant density q², α = 1/2 gives the Langevin dynamics whose invariant density is the sampling density itself, and α = 1 gives Brownian motion on the manifold, with no trace of the density *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-756](../record/theory.d/THEORY-756.md): The growth rate of thermodynamic depth is the entropy rate of whichever macrostate process it is computed over, so the choice of macrostates sets it anywhere from zero up; among partitions of a stationary process's past that predict every finite stretch of the future as well as the whole past does, the causal states are the coarsest, so they have the least entropy and the least entropy rate *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-820](../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md): For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement *(used by 8; also distributed-agency, will-organization)*
- [THEORY-822](../record/theory.d/THEORY-822.md): For a Markov chain and a partition of its states, strong lumpability, every state of a block sending the same probability into each block, is the column-equitability of the master-equation operator and makes the block label informationally closed; when the chain is irreducible, an informationally closed label that is itself Markov is strongly lumpable, with no aperiodicity needed; weak lumpability gives a Markov label that need not be closed; and the same holds on the causal-state chain of any stationary process *(used by 4; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-843](../record/theory.d/THEORY-843.md): Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern's approximate abstraction error, the least over surjective context maps of the worst case over allowed interventions and contexts of the high-level distance between the coarse-grained low-level outcome and the high-level outcome, is zero exactly for τ-abstraction; an abstraction followed by an α-approximation of the high-level model is within α, an α-approximation of the low-level model followed by an abstraction only within kα, k the worst-case ratio of high- to low-level distances, and an approximate abstraction need not factor into an exact abstraction and an approximation *(used by 4; also will-organization, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-846](../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md): Information usable by a predictor restricted to a family V can be created by computing on the data, so the data-processing inequality fails for V-information: with Z the exclusive-or of two fair independent bits, linear and one-coordinate families extract nothing about Z from the pair and all of it from their exclusive-or; V-information computed from any function of the source is bounded by the source's Shannon information when the family's input-free predictions can match the marginal of the target, and can exceed it otherwise *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-847](../record/theory.d/THEORY-847.md): In a linear structural equation model whose exogenous micro-causes W₁, …, W_n drive effects Z = AW + F, with interventions that set all of W, all of Z or both, averaging each block is an exact transformation onto Ẑ = (an/m)Ŵ + F̂ if and only if every column of A sums to the same a, the column-equitability of the block of A from W to Z; the transformation is exact only for those whole-block interventions *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-848](../record/theory.d/THEORY-848.md): In an acyclic structural equation model, marginalising a variable that no declared intervention sets is an exact transformation, provided the coarse model's exogenous noises may be dependent; so exactness does not require the dropped variable to be causally idle, and it can drop a variable that decides how its children respond to an intervention that is declared *(used by 5; also will-organization, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-849](../record/theory.d/THEORY-849.md): For deterministic causal models with a countable set of allowed interventions, a high-level model reproduces the coarse-grained interventional law of a low-level one for every distribution on contexts exactly when some map τ_U on contexts commutes with every allowed intervention, τ(M_L(u, i)) = M_H(τ_U(u), ω(i)); exactness for one distribution is strictly weaker, since a well-chosen distribution lets unrelated models match, and τ-abstraction and strong abstraction are strictly stronger; the context map is only required to exist, so high-level exogenous variables may carry what the coarse state drops *(used by 3; also will-organization)*
- [THEORY-852](../record/theory.d/THEORY-852.md): Under Szeidl and Szucs's structural model and its identifying assumptions (an owner's ideology fixed across episodes; the government's online advertising budget not driven by the outlets' slant), both owner ideology and favor exchange drove the Hungarian portal Origo's reduced coverage of corruption in 2013–2016: favor exchange alone cut it by 29–44%, the new owner's ideology alone by 63% after 2016, and the two together by 74%, so they are substitutes; and a ban on targeted government advertising would have raised it by 41–79% *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-860](../record/theory.d/THEORY-860.md): In Szeidl and Szucs's model of two outlets competing for readers and advertisers, where state-owned advertisers reward only the connected outlet's slant, with weight δ, every equilibrium has the slant gap between the connected and the unconnected outlet equal to their owners' ideal-point gap plus a favor-exchange term (βδ/NT)·Σ over government advertisers of masⱼWⱼ, up to measurement noise; readers' preference for slant cancels from the gap, so equal observed gaps can come from different mixes of ideology and exchange *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-884](../record/theory.d/THEORY-884.md): A retained state supports exact answers to a declared family of questions after every finite sequence of a declared family of total deterministic revisions exactly when each of its fibres lies within one class of the coarsest revision-invariant refinement of agreement on current answers; that refinement can be strictly finer than what present answers require, and at most K* − K revision sequences, beyond the current answers, are needed to tell its K* classes apart *(used by 2; also records-of-inquiry)*
- [THEORY-894](../record/theory.d/THEORY-894.md): A flow of pairwise comparisons on a graph splits orthogonally and uniquely into a gradient part, the l2-best global ranking, and a cyclic part, which splits into curl (local) and harmonic (global) inconsistency; a finite game's flow of unilateral payoff differences has no curl part, so every finite game is uniquely a potential game plus a harmonic game plus a nonstrategic remainder, and potential games are exactly those with no harmonic part; the decomposition is cardinal *(used by 6; also distributed-agency, organizational-affect)*
- [THEORY-896](../record/theory.d/THEORY-896.md): A finite game in strategic form has the finite improvement property, every path of strict unilateral improvements being finite, exactly when it has a generalized ordinal potential, a real function on strategy profiles that rises with every strict unilateral improvement; so in a finite game an ordering along which every improving move climbs exists exactly when there is no improvement cycle, and every sequence of improving moves ends at a pure equilibrium *(used by 5; also distributed-agency, organizational-affect)*
- [THEORY-954](../record/theory.d/THEORY-954.md): When the information a design yields depends on the unknown parameter, as in nonlinear models or nonlinear functions of linear ones, Bayesian design criteria are normal approximations to expected utility that average a local criterion over the prior, such as the expected log det of the Fisher information, and locally optimal design is the special case of a point-mass prior; a locally optimal design can leave the quantity of interest inestimable, as for the turning point of a quadratic regression on [−1, 1] with best guess ½, where the locally c-optimal design puts half its mass at 0 and half at 1 and identifies only θ₁ + θ₂ *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-956](../record/theory.d/THEORY-956.md): In the normal linear model with known error variance and a conjugate normal prior of precision R/σ², the design that maximizes the expected Shannon information of the posterior is the one maximizing det(nM(η) + R), Bayes D-optimality, and the design that minimizes expected quadratic loss with weight matrix A is the one minimizing tr A(nM(η) + R)^-1, Bayes A-optimality; both criteria depend on the design and not on the data, so in this model a sequential design gains nothing over the best fixed one *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-962](../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md): In a finite partial-monitoring game, the signals of a set D of actions determine the expected loss difference of actions i and j under every outcome distribution iff ℓ_i − ℓ_j lies in the sum of the row spaces of their signal matrices; when it does not, two outcome distributions differing along a vector in the common kernel give every action in D the same signal law and reverse the preference between i and j, so no amount of play restricted to D can learn the comparison *(used by 4; also distributed-agency, will-organization, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-1082](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md): On a connected graph whose edges carry phase shifts αᵢⱼ = −αⱼᵢ, the edge relations zⱼ = e^{iαᵢⱼ}zᵢ have a common nonzero solution, equivalently the twisted Laplacian Lα = δα*δα has a zero mode, exactly when the phase accumulated around every cycle is 0 mod 2π; otherwise each relation can be met alone but not all together, and the smallest eigenvalue of Lα, positive, measures the residual incompatibility, which on an isolated ℓ-cycle is largest at holonomy π *(used by 7; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1088](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1088.md): When the expression maps of a discourse sheaf diffuse to reduce disagreement, with opinions held fixed they converge to the nearest sheaf, in Frobenius distance, of which the opinions are a global section, so apparent consensus is reached by changing what is said ("learning to lie"); with opinions diffusing too the joint flow is gradient descent on ½‖δx‖², and conserved diagonal blocks of αδᵀδ − βxxᵀ keep the opinions from collapsing to zero; nothing in either flow checks an expression against the opinion it expresses *(used by 6; also distributed-agency, pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-1125](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1125.md): For discrete X and Y, with an intervention on a variable abstraction T of X defined as the mixture of interventions on X weighted by Bayes inversion of the encoder under a protocol prior, no abstraction gains causal information about Y over X itself, and at full weight on causal control the causal information bottleneck is optimised by the partition of X by p(y | do(x)), mapped one class to one value of T, uniquely up to relabelling when T has exactly as many values as there are classes; these are Chalupka et al.'s causal macrovariables *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1140](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1140.md): If every entity's O(d) frame may change independently and relation transports change as Tᵢⱼ ↦ gᵢTᵢⱼgⱼ⁻¹, then functions of the transports alone carry no invariant information except around cycles, a triangle's invariants are exactly the class functions of its holonomy H = TᵢⱼTⱼₖTₖᵢ, and an equivariant update of an edge from one cycle through it is Ψ(H)Tᵢⱼ with Ψ conjugation-equivariant; the symmetry fixes a family of updates, not one mechanism, and says nothing about whether a task has the symmetry *(used by 3; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-1146](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1146.md): Under confounding the partition of a variable X by what it predicts about a target Y can differ from its partition by what setting it does to Y, so the information bottleneck at full sufficiency can learn distinctions no intervention could use and miss ones only intervention reveals, as it did in two confounded toy models, while the causal information bottleneck, computed from observational data through a backdoor set, recovered the causal partition in all three toy models, projected gradient search finding it in 95 to 100 percent of runs *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1158](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1158.md): On synchronization of S4 relations with outliers, an untrained mechanism that composes relations through third vertices gains 26–45 points over the single direct path, and weighting the candidate paths by the Wilson loops of squares that avoid the missing edge adds 0.6–7.8 points, most where clean two-hop paths become a minority; it stays below spectral synchronization with one reweighting pass on every setting and within 2.2 points of plain spectral synchronization either way; its 0.99 AUC for corrupted triangles is the ceiling that exactly flat clean data set, not a measure of detection power *(used by 4; also pragmatic-transport, distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1162](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1162.md): In a consumer-resource model whose species-resource benefits and impacts have correlation rho, the replica-symmetric cavity fixed point loses stability where rho squared equals surviving species over non-depleted resources *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1167](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md): When one intervention distribution over micro states is used at both levels, the effective information of a coarse-graining of a discrete mechanism, with each macro intervention realized by that distribution within its block, cannot exceed the micro effective information; so a positive causal emergence of effective information, scored with a uniform distribution at each level, equals the micro gain from changing the distribution minus a non-negative loss, and is a gain from the change of distribution *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1169](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1169.md): For a discrete mechanism scored with one full-support intervention distribution over micro causes at both levels, a coarse-graining of cause and effect keeps all of the micro effective information if and only if it merges only causes with identical rows P(Y | do(x)) and only effects with proportional columns, whatever the distribution; so the coarsest coarse-graining that ties the micro is the causal partition of causal feature learning, with effects grouped by normalized likelihood, and any merge of causes with different effects loses information under every such distribution *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*

## Readiness and slack

- [THEORY-134](../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md): Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time *(used by 12; also will-organization, nucleating-argument, distributed-agency, realizability)*
- [THEORY-1376](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1376.md): Lawvere shows that a generalized metric space is exactly a category enriched in the extended non-negative reals under addition, with the triangle inequality as composition, so that dropping symmetry and finiteness is natural and enriched-category constructions specialise to metric-space theory *(used by 5; also realizability)*
- [THEORY-1378](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1378.md): Gerardi and Maestri show that when a firm can offer a privately informed worker only short-term contracts, then as both become patient the unique limiting outcome is a pooling contract with no learning if the prior that the worker is low-cost is below a threshold, and immediate firing of the high-cost worker if it is above, both inefficient *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1394](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1394.md): Larson and Odoni's hypercube model represents an urban emergency service's N distinguishable units, each busy or free, as a Markov chain on the vertices of an N-cube under fixed-preference dispatch from point sources of Poisson calls, and from its steady state computes each unit's workload, the inter-district dispatch fractions and the mean travel times *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1396](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1396.md): Mukhopadhyay and colleagues present static coverage models for emergency response as moving from deterministic models that treat a facility as always available, through multiple coverage as a partial hedge against busy stations, to probabilistic models that represent station availability explicitly, beginning with the maximum expected covering and maximum availability models *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1401](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1401.md): Bogetoft and Hougaard hold that an organization's measured technical inefficiency can be a rational choice of on-the-job slack traded against profit, so that under price-based or restriction-based control a rational unit still uses an efficient underlying plan, and its observed inputs reveal partial information about how it values the different kinds of slack *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1404](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1404.md): Oskar and colleagues find that the evidence on procedural skill decay among emergency physicians cannot yet say how long a procedural skill lasts after competence: few studies make decay the primary outcome, almost none follow skills beyond a year, most rely on simulation and checklist scores and study trainees, and many required procedures are unstudied *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1412](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1412.md): Guigues, Kleywegt and Nascimento propose that a per-station steady-state Markov-chain preparedness metric, used inside a one-step integer program for ambulance selection and reassignment, gives a real-time EMS policy whose mean allocation cost is lower than nine published dispatch policies in most simulated Rio de Janeiro configurations *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1416](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1416.md): van Leeuwaarden, Mathijsen and Zwart report that Halfin and Whitt showed that in a many-server queue with Poisson arrivals and exponential service the probability that an arrival waits tends to a value strictly between zero and one exactly when the number of servers exceeds the offered load by a multiple of its square root, and that the scaled number in system then tends to a diffusion that is a negative-drift Brownian motion above full occupancy and an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process below it; they prove the limit of the waiting probability under that scaling *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
