- [THEORY-1418](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1418.md): Stern, Pinson and Murugan find, in zero-temperature simulations of idealized rigid-panel crease patterns designed with one folding motion, distractor branches at the flat state whose number grows exponentially with the sheet's boundary length on random meshes up to 6 × 6, which they trace to frustrated loops of two-branch vertices; and, on one 4 × 4 pattern, that whether the actuated creases' folding islands cover the sheet predicts folding success much better than the number of actuators, and that an added actuator can ruin a folding that succeeded, without a necessary and sufficient condition *(used by 4; also realizability)*
- [THEORY-1423](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1423.md): Berry, Lee-Trimble and Santangelo find that near the flat state a non-intersecting rigid origami vertex with small positive Gaussian curvature has a configuration space split into two components (popped up and popped down) that no rigid, non-tearing motion joins, while for small negative curvature the two stay joined by a neck, except at a degree-four vertex, which is split for both signs *(used by 3; also realizability)*
- [THEORY-1424](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1424.md): Tatel finds that procedural skills with motor components decline roughly linearly with months of infrequent use, by about 0.06 to 0.08 standard deviations a month on average, losing about half of training gains within six to fifteen months, and that accuracy declines more slowly when a performance opportunity, most often an earlier retention test, falls in the interval *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1426](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1426.md): Hua, Luo, Swersey and Wen solve the spatial hypercube queueing model with server-specific service rates by an iteration on a birth–death reformulation, and state a proof that, under their Assumption 3.1, a technical bound on how far the rates differ, it converges to the exact stationary distribution at a geometric rate *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1496](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1496.md): When two Food for Peace projects in India handed their activities to Government of India programmes, activities continued two years after exit where the receiving programme had dedicated resources, functioning infrastructure and a legal commitment and the project's linkage to it was operating before exit, and stopped where the linkage was begun late; results often varied between states by more than they changed over time *(used by 2; also transient-support)*

## Withdrawing transient support

- [THEORY-1048](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md): On the Black Queen Hypothesis of Morris, Lenski and Zinser, losing a costly function whose product leaks to neighbours is favoured by ordinary individual selection in large free-living microbial populations, and the loss proceeds until the remaining producers just supply the community, so that most cells come to depend on a rare few with no relatedness, cooperation or collective required *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1103](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md): On Shigenobu and colleagues' genome of Buchnera sp. APS, the aphid symbiont keeps the genes for the amino acids its host cannot make and has lost almost all of those its host can, uses host-made glutamate and aspartate as precursors, and lacks phospholipid synthesis and nearly all its own transcriptional regulators, so that its metabolism interlocks with the host's and it presumably lives only inside the bacteriocyte, a state reached by gene loss from an E. coli-like ancestor *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1270](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1270.md): Entropy production does not select which of several maintained steady states is the stable one: in the bistable Schlögl model the state the system occupies in the long run can carry either the higher or the lower deterministic entropy production rate, and the mean stochastic entropy production follows whichever state is more probable; in general the most dissipative attractor is the longest-lived only under special conditions, and lifetime tracks relaxation entropy only near detailed balance *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1273](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1273.md): In a driven chemical system with two stable states and a finite number of molecules, each maintained state is metastable: it is left by fluctuation after a time exponential in system size, set by a barrier in a nonequilibrium quasi-potential that closes at the saddle-node, and the long-run share of time in each state is fixed by the parameters and system size, not by the initial condition; the deterministic rate equation, where the initial condition decides, holds only on times short of that escape time *(used by 3; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1458](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1458.md): In Shah, Shafir and Mullainathan's working paper, players given small budgets of seconds or of guesses borrowed a larger share of their budget against later rounds than players given large ones and, when borrowing carried interest, scored lower than when they could not borrow, while large-budget players did not; the authors attribute this to constraint focus, attention shifted toward the binding resource at the cost of others, whose one direct test is a two-grid memory game with 33 players *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1461](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1461.md): Kline and Moretti find that the Tennessee Valley Authority's federal subsidies, peaking at about 10% of household income in 1950–55 and declining sharply after the TVA was made self-financing in 1959, raised both agricultural and manufacturing employment growth in its region by about 10–12 points per decade in 1940–1960, after which the agricultural gain fully reversed while manufacturing kept growing about 3 points per decade faster; but their estimate of a constant agglomeration elasticity, about 0.4–0.47 in labour demand and equal across density ranges, implies a unique steady state, so that the manufacturing gain is slow convergence rather than a big-push shift to a second equilibrium and will eventually die out *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1464](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1464.md): Christie, Marine, French and Blouin show in Hood River steelhead that one generation of hatchery rearing selects for traits that raise reproductive success in captivity and lower it in the wild: offspring of the wild broodstock most successful in the hatchery have about 71% lower per capita reproductive success in the wild, and first-generation hatchery fish nearly double wild fish's success as hatchery broodstock, a difference significant only with one run-year, whose releases were treated very differently, excluded *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1465](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1465.md): Balboni, Bandiera, Burgess, Ghatak and Heil hold that ultra-poor households in rural Bangladesh face an S-shaped asset transition with an unstable threshold near the value of a cow and a small complementary asset, so that a one-off asset transfer that lifts a household above it is followed by accumulation, a shift into self-employment and higher consumption over 11 years while one that leaves it below is followed by asset loss: a poverty trap set by initial wealth and indivisible inputs, not by lower ability or effort *(used by 6)*
- [THEORY-1466](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1466.md): Baird, McKenzie and Özler's structured review of cash transfers in low- and middle-income countries finds that transfers made without an employment focus leave prime-age adults' work and earnings little changed, that pensioners and, in one study, refugees do reduce work, and that business start-up grants raise work and earnings while a job-search subsidy raised employment, significant only at the 10 percent level, which the authors attribute chiefly to easing liquidity and risk constraints; they expect responses to differ where transfers are dependable and permanent *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1467](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1467.md): Mussmann and colleagues argue, from greater prairie chickens in Illinois, that supplying individuals by translocation while the habitat threat persists gives only ambiguous or transitory gains and perpetuates conservation reliance, which can fall below a reliance threshold only if extrinsic threats and intrinsic small-population limits are relieved together *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1468](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1468.md): On Kadowaki and colleagues, restoring the pressure-free conditions of a degraded ecosystem can fail because the degraded phase leaves a reinforcing legacy of its own, such as hardwoods that stop fire spreading, sludge that favours a floating competitor, or eroded beaver sites, so recovery needs direct biotic manipulation, by removal or by reintroduction in the right order, besides abiotic restoration *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1469](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1469.md): In the Social Sciences Replication Project's pre-registered replication of Study 1 of Shah, Mullainathan and Shafir (2012), 619 online players given fewer guesses in a Wheel of Fortune word game did no worse than players given more on a later attention task (pooled p = 0.71, both stages' estimates in the opposite direction); the project tested no other study of the paper, and the original authors, whose own replications reproduced its over-borrowing result, call Study 1 a false positive *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1470](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1470.md): Collins and Shester find that US cities whose states enabled federal urban renewal earlier received more renewal grants and, per $100 of grants per 1950 resident, had about 2.4% higher median family income, 6.9% higher median property value and 9–11% more population and housing units in 1980 than similar cities, gains not explained by a changed racial or educational composition and not faded by 2000, decades after new funding ended, while the projects cleared or planned to clear over 400,000 housing units and relocated over 300,000 families, about 54% nonwhite, whose costs the city-level design does not measure *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1471](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1471.md): Banerjee, Hanna, Kreindler and Olken find, re-analysing seven randomized evaluations of government-run cash transfer programs in six countries, no systematic effect of the transfers on whether adults work or how many hours they work, for men or for women: pooled, a transfer worth 13.6% of household consumption changes participation by −0.4 points (90% interval −2.3 to +1.4) and weekly hours by about −5 minutes (−1.7 to +1.4 hours), ruling out moderate reductions for men while leaving a wide range for women *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1472](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1472.md): Michaels, Nigmatulina, Rauch, Regan, Baruah and Dahlstrand find that greenfield neighbourhoods given formal plots, roads and water mains under Tanzania's 1970s–80s Sites and Services projects, on which residents built their own houses, had by the 2010s larger, more regular and better-connected housing and better-preserved roads and water mains than adjacent land unbuilt at the start, while squatter areas given similar infrastructure spending per square metre were, in a comparison the authors call descriptive, no better than comparison areas, which the authors explain by their infrastructure having deteriorated; they attribute the difference to a feedback in which enough owners able to invest keep up the infrastructure that draws their investment *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1473](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1473.md): Watson finds, across seven Brazilian cities, that condominial sewerage cost a third to a quarter of conventional sewerage and performed as well in about half the cases, that upkeep devolved to residents' blocks rarely worked, and that the systems lasted where agencies kept up trunk maintenance, monitoring, education and backup on feeder lines in face-to-face contact with residents and decayed where agencies withdrew from or refused the networks *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1474](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1474.md): Heins, Unrau and Avram, following Mauss, hold that a gift carries no legal guarantee of return yet obliges one, and that an unreturned gift leaves the recipient inferior and poisons the relation; they report Dillon's reading of the Marshall Plan in France, whose recipients, unable to repay, responded with resentment, and his proposal that circular (kula-like) reciprocity that lets the recipient give back is the better design for aid between nations *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1478](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1478.md): In a global review of 514 conservation translocations of terrestrial vertebrates, practitioner-judged success was similar for captive-bred and wild-sourced stock and for soft and hard release, but population growth after release was negative on average for captive-bred stock and lower for soft than for hard release, and success rose with numbers released up to about 20–50 individuals *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1479](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1479.md): Cesarini, Lindqvist, Notowidigdo and Östling find, in their 2015 working paper, using lottery prizes randomly assigned among Swedish players, that an unconditional wealth shock reduces the winner's gross labour earnings by about 1.1% of the prize a year, beginning in the year of the win and lasting more than ten years, mostly through fewer hours and varying little with age, sex, education or prize size; non-winning spouses reduce theirs by less than half as much, and the authors call the response modest *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1480](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1480.md): Ostrom, Gibson, Shivakumar and Andersson hold that predictable aid weakens the recipient's own upkeep, as in the Samaritan's dilemma, so that assets built and repaired from outside decay and are rebuilt from outside, and that benefits outlast the aid only where beneficiaries state the demand, contribute their own assets, receive the benefits and share in deciding whether to continue *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-1481](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1481.md): Andrews, Pritchett and Woolcock argue that when external funding and legitimacy are granted for adopting the forms of capable states (best-practice laws, agencies and procedures) rather than for demonstrated performance, recipient organizations engage in isomorphic mimicry, producing a capability trap in which state capability stagnates or declines while reform and aid continue, and that it is escaped by locally defined problem-solving through authorized experimentation, tight feedback and broad engagement (PDIA) *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1482](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1482.md): Brown, Donner, Ribic and Bocetti project that the Kirtland's Warbler, recovered on plantation habitat that replaces suppressed wildfire, settles at a lower plateau when the supplied breeding habitat is cut, without going extinct from habitat loss alone, so that the species remains reliant on humans to keep its breeding habitat at its current quantity *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1484](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1484.md): In pre-registered replications of all five experiments of their 2012 paper, with 876 to 997 online participants analysed in each, Shah, Mullainathan and Shafir again found that players given small budgets of shots or of seconds borrow a larger share against later rounds and do worse when they can borrow with interest while players given large budgets do not, with smaller effects than the originals, and that small-budget players aim longer; focus did not predict later borrowing, the previews effect was weaker, and their first study's fatigue effect reversed *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1485](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1485.md): On Schröder, Persson and De Roos, of 35 manipulation experiments testing for alternative stable states, 21 were conclusive over at least one turnover of the longest-lived organisms, 13 of them showing bistability and 8 its absence; positives came mostly from laboratory rather than field systems, and only 3 of 15 tests of non-recovery after a pressure was removed were positive *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1486](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1486.md): Banerjee, Duflo, Goldberg, Karlan, Osei, Parienté, Shapiro, Thuysbaert and Udry find, in six randomized trials, that a time-limited bundle of a productive asset, temporary consumption support, training and coaching raised the consumption, assets, income and working time of the poorest households, and that these gains held one year after all support ended; they read the durability as consistent with the program having unlocked a poverty trap, while noting that persistent but modest effects also fit a 'poverty flat' without one *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1487](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1487.md): Evans holds that state-society synergy combines complementarity, in which government dependably supplies inputs citizens cannot produce and citizens supply local knowledge and labour, with embeddedness, in which officials keep everyday ties with the communities they serve, and that small-scale synergy is constructable even in class-divided societies under disorganized, authoritarian governance, the limits seeming to be set less by prior stocks of social capital than by the difficulty of scaling up *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1488](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1488.md): In ten southern Costa Rican pasture sites where weeding stopped after 2.5 years, planting six tree islands (86 trees per 0.25 ha) or a full plantation (313) still raised later-successional seedling and sapling recruitment and reduced among-site compositional variability relative to natural regeneration after 16–18 years, yet in every treatment the tree layer remained dominated by a few pioneers and the planted cohort, whose own seedlings seldom reached the sapling layer *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1489](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1489.md): Underwood, Silbernagle, Nishimoto and Uyehara report that Hawai'i's endangered Coot, Stilt and Gallinule were stable or rising statewide from 1986 to 2007, with refuges where invasive plants, predators and water levels are actively managed holding on average 34–42% of each species on about 15% of the wetland, and hold that without perpetual active management of those wetlands the birds likely would decline *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1490](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1490.md): Hankins, Hoekstra and Skiba find that Florida lottery winners of 50,000 to 150,000 dollars were about half as likely as winners of under 10,000 dollars to file for bankruptcy in the two years after winning but more likely to file three to five years after, so that over five years no difference in bankruptcy was detected, and that the large winners who filed had similar net assets and unsecured debt, from which the authors conclude that large cash transfers postpone rather than prevent bankruptcy *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1491](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1491.md): Neumark and Simpson's review finds that the US and European evidence on place-based policy shows gains at most while incentives are in force, often offset by relocation from nearby areas or captured in land and house values, and that the one program shown to leave gains after its funding ended, the Tennessee Valley Authority, did so through manufacturing agglomeration while its direct effect faded, with its agglomeration gains estimated to net to about zero nationally *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1492](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1492.md): Coates, Kegode, Galante and Blau report that in three Food for Peace projects in Kenya, followed 2–3 years after exit, impact at exit did not necessarily predict sustained benefit, and they read their within-country contrasts, which have no comparison group, as showing that the activities that continued had, before the project withdrew, their own resource stream, sufficient technical and managerial capacity, motivated participants and substantive linkages formed early, and had operated independently for a time, while activities that relied on project-supplied inputs until the end declined *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-1493](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1493.md): Banerjee, Duflo and Sharma find, in a randomized trial in West Bengal, that the treatment effects of a one-time Targeting the Ultra Poor package on household consumption, income and health grew for seven years after the asset transfer and persisted to year ten, although the implementer had no contact with households after eighteen months; they attribute the persistence mainly to treated households taking better advantage of wage employment and migration, and hold it consistent with, but not proof of, escape from a poverty trap *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1494](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1494.md): Evans and Popova's count by sign and significance of 44 estimates from 19 studies of conditional and unconditional cash transfers in low- and middle-income countries finds that transfers almost never raise spending on alcohol and tobacco: 82% of the estimates are negative, only two are positive and significant, both non-experimental, none of 17 randomized estimates is positive and significant, and the pattern does not differ between conditional and unconditional programs, across regions or with duration of receipt *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1495](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1495.md): Araki, Berejikian, Ford and Blouin find hatchery salmonids generally less fit in the wild than wild fish, worst for nonlocal segregated stocks (lifetime relative fitness 0.02–0.37), and find in a quantitative-genetic model that domestication selection on a single trait can explain a decline of more than 30% per hatchery generation only when selection is strong in both captivity and the wild and heritability is high, while arguing it plausible when selection acts on several traits across the life cycle *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1496](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1496.md): When two Food for Peace projects in India handed their activities to Government of India programmes, activities continued two years after exit where the receiving programme had dedicated resources, functioning infrastructure and a legal commitment and the project's linkage to it was operating before exit, and stopped where the linkage was begun late; results often varied between states by more than they changed over time *(used by 2; also readiness)*
- [THEORY-1497](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1497.md): St John holds that Burning Man's gifting carries no obligation on the recipient to reciprocate, yet sustains circulation through gratitude that recipients return to the community in later labour, a generalized rather than bilateral reciprocity, and that perhaps the most pressing threat to it is non-participation, which the organization answered in part by reforming how theme camps are registered and placed *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1498](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1498.md): Golosov, Graber, Mogstad and Novgorodsky find, from US tax records of 90,731 state-lottery winners aged 21–64 with wins of at least $30,000 compared with later winners, that a windfall reduces work swiftly and persistently over the following five years, each dollar of annuitized unearned income lowering household pre-tax labour earnings by about 52 cents and raising consumption, imputed from the budget identity, by about 58 cents; that winners save and smooth most of the windfall, as imputed from their capital income; that the per-dollar earnings response rises with pre-win income and falls with prize size; and that wealth raises entry into low-profit self-employment but not into self-employment with profits above $15,000 *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1499](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1499.md): Davis and Weinstein find that the Allied bombing of Japanese cities in World War II, which destroyed almost half the structures in the 66 targeted cities, changed relative city size only temporarily: across 303 cities, 1947–60 population growth undid 1940–47 growth instrumented on deaths and buildings destroyed per capita one for one, or by about three-quarters once 1925–40 trend growth is controlled, and wholly by 1965, with Hiroshima and Nagasaki back on their prewar trends; the authors read this as rejecting random growth and as showing that spatial catastrophes from temporary shocks are not a central tendency, favouring locational fundamentals *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1502](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1502.md): For a real scalar field with a potential analytic at its minimum, the only one-parameter family of exactly time-periodic localized solutions that shrinks to the vacuum is the 1+1 dimensional sine-Gordon breather family; small-amplitude oscillons radiate at a rate exponentially small in their amplitude parameter, to leading order a coefficient times an exponential in minus a constant over that parameter, and, since their core energy scales as the parameter to the power 2 − d, in 3+1 dimensions they are stable only above a minimum amplitude and decay suddenly once radiation carries them below it, while in 1 and 2 dimensions small and moderate amplitude oscillons are stable and, their loss falling exponentially with amplitude, never decay *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1503](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1503.md): Davis and Weinstein find, testing unique against multiple equilibria by threshold regression on the Allied bombing of Japanese cities, that city population, the city share of aggregate manufacturing and city-industry output pooled over eight manufacturing industries tend to return after the shock to their prior shares: the Schwarz criterion prefers a single equilibrium for manufacturing and for city-industry output; for population it slightly prefers two equilibria, but that fit, like the best two-equilibrium fit for industries, fails the requirement that larger negative shocks lead to lower equilibria; and pooled city-industry shares were still recovering in 1969, which the authors suggest may be because the hardest-hit places take longer, though without Hiroshima the persistence is indistinguishable from zero *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1504](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1504.md): Grelu and Akhmediev hold that a dissipative soliton differs from a conservative one in being a single attractor rather than a member of a continuous family: a conservative soliton balances nonlinearity against dispersion alone, with its parameters selected by the initial data, whereas a dissipative soliton also needs an exact balance of gain and loss, kept by a continuous energy exchange with the environment and an internal flow from regions that gain energy to regions that lose it, so that its energy, profile and chirp are fixed by the system's parameters, not by its initial conditions; such solitons can bind into robust molecules whose energy scales with the number of constituents *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1505](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1505.md): Bleakley and Lin find that US cities at historical portage sites, whose transport advantage ended with canals and railroads by about 1900, remain 60–100% denser than comparable sites in the same river watersheds, increasingly so relative to 1850, are neither oversupplied nor cheap in housing, infrastructure or other sunk assets conditional on density, and grow like comparably dense places from about 1930, with no effect where the upstream watershed was smallest; they read this as path dependence under strong local increasing returns, with portage a coordination device that selected the high-density equilibrium, rather than slow reversion through sunk capital, while granting that their results are not direct evidence of multiple equilibria *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1508](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1508.md): Chetty, Hendren and Katz find, in the Moving to Opportunity experiment, that a housing voucher requiring a family in high-poverty public housing to move to a low-poverty tract for its first year raised the adult earnings of children who moved before age 13 by about 31% at ages 24 and over, that the gain fell by about $364 a year for each year of age at the move and was absent or negative for those who moved as teenagers, and that their parents’ earnings were unchanged however long they lived in lower-poverty areas; the authors conclude that the effect runs through the amount of childhood exposure, not through family income or exposure in adulthood *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1510](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1510.md): On Suding, Gross and Houseman, where degradation has built biotic–abiotic feedbacks that hold the degraded state, such as invader-driven fire and nitrogen cycles, herbivory on regenerating plants, lost seed sources or bare soil that sheds rain, restoring the historical disturbance regime or abiotic conditions does not return the community; restoration must first disrupt those feedbacks or move the state directly, often by several actions together, before restored conditions suffice *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1512](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1512.md): Alía and Esteban hold, from the randomized weaning trials of the 1990s, that ventilation can be withdrawn abruptly in about three quarters of patients whose cause of respiratory failure has improved, readiness being tested by a trial of unassisted breathing on T-tube or low pressure support, for 30 or 120 minutes alike, and immediate extubation after a passed trial shortening ventilation compared with gradual withdrawal; and that the patients who fail need gradual withdrawal while the causes are corrected, where SIMV was the least efficient method in both trials and once-daily T-tube trials or reductions of pressure support did better *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1513](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1513.md): Broersen, Pereira, Jørgensen and Dekkers find, pooling 74 observational studies of adult corticosteroid users, that biochemically suppressed adrenal function after treatment is common, from about 4% after nasal or topical use to about half after oral or intra-articular use; in asthma it rises with dose (2.4%, 8.5%, 21.5%) and with duration (1.4% under a month, 27.4% over a year); it recedes after stopping but incompletely, from 38.7% to 14.9% four weeks after short high-dose courses and from 56.4% to 25.3% six months after long medium-dose use; and they hold that no route, dose or duration excludes it and that no withdrawal scheme has been shown effective or safe *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1514](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1514.md): Goligher and colleagues hold that mechanical ventilation harms the diaphragm at both ends of effort, atrophy following low effort from over-assistance or sedation and injury possibly following excessive effort, so that ventilation and sedation should be titrated to keep an effort close to that of quiet breathing; that support proportional to the patient's own neural drive makes disuse from over-assistance unlikely, since assist falls as diaphragm activity falls; and that trials confirming the benefit of this approach are still required *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1515](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1515.md): Shah, Hart and Kaltsakas, following the 2007 international consensus, hold that readiness to come off invasive ventilation is tested by withdrawing support for a spontaneous breathing trial of 30 to 120 minutes, since predictors of readiness have low power; that patients are classed as simple, difficult or prolonged weaning by whether the first attempt succeeds and, if not, whether up to three trials or seven days suffice; and that outcomes worsen across these groups, about half of patients whose weaning fails remaining on invasive ventilation at one year *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1516](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1516.md): Beuschlein and colleagues, for the European Society of Endocrinology and the Endocrine Society, hold that exogenous glucocorticoids at anti-inflammatory doses invariably suppress the HPA axis by negative feedback and that prolonged use leads to pituitary hyporesponsiveness and adrenal atrophy; that after withdrawal the axis recovers first centrally and then adrenally, over months to years and incompletely in a minority; that courses under 3–4 weeks can be stopped without taper, while longer ones are tapered, once the disease is controlled, quickly at high doses and slowly near the physiologic dose, with replacement kept low enough to leave a stimulus for recovery; and that no study has compared taper schemes *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1517](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1517.md): Knack finds, across 80 aid-receiving countries from 1982 to 1995, that higher mean aid relative to GNP or to government spending goes with smaller gains in the ICRG governance index, controlling for initial governance, income growth and population growth; the effect roughly doubles when aid is instrumented with recipient need and donor interest, holds within sub-Saharan Africa for aid relative to GNP, is several times larger for technical assistance, does not depend on initial governance, and shrinks as aid becomes less predictable *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1518](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1518.md): Cohen and Levinthal argue that a firm's ability to recognize, assimilate and apply outside knowledge rests on its prior related knowledge, built largely as a byproduct of its own R&D and not quickly bought, and that because this capacity accumulates and shapes what the firm expects of a field, a firm that stops investing in a fast-moving field may be locked out of it even after major advances; with 1975–1977 data on 1,719 business units they test only the static part, that R&D intensity rises more with the relevance of harder-to-learn, less targeted knowledge *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1520](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1520.md): Koedinger and Aleven argue that instruction faces an assistance dilemma, help given buying accuracy and efficiency at the cost of shallow processing and help withheld buying generation and memory engagement at the cost of floundering, and that within tutored problem solving, where the learner does the steps and help is added only on failure, the experiments they review favour more help rather than less, support shifting from worked examples toward problems and as-needed hints as competence grows, learners left to ask for help asking badly, and the point at which to switch between giving and withholding unknown *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1521](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1521.md): Macnamara and colleagues argue that when automation performs a subtask while the operator goes on doing the task, the operator's skill at that subtask decays from disuse, the cognitive part more than the procedural part, and may do so out of the operator's awareness, because the task itself is still done and still succeeds *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1522](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1522.md): Ahn reads Bainbridge's ironies of automation as holding that automation takes the routine work and leaves the operator the atypical cases, recalls the operator at its failure, when the system is least predictable, and leaves the operator's manual and cognitive skills degraded from disuse; and, as his own remedies for medical education, he proposes building core skills in phases free of AI before AI is introduced, and simulations in which AI failures are injected *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1523](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1523.md): Griffith, Redding and Van Reenen find, in a panel of manufacturing industries in twelve OECD countries over 1974–1990, that industries further behind their industry's productivity frontier grow faster the more R&D they do, so that R&D raises the rate at which frontier technology is absorbed as well as the rate of own innovation, and that for a country at about half the frontier's productivity over half of R&D's estimated return comes through this absorption *(used by 1)*

## Resource-bounded realizability and individuation

- [THEORY-032](../record/theory.d/THEORY-032.md): The Yoneda lemma determines an object only up to isomorphism, from its whole hom-functor, among objects the category already has; as a formal version of "an object is determined by its relations" it presupposes the relata *(used by 12; also pragmatic-transport, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-134](../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md): Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time *(used by 12; also will-organization, nucleating-argument, distributed-agency, readiness)*
- [THEORY-247](../record/theory.d/THEORY-247.md): For finite action-free labelled Markov chains, the discounted bisimulation metric, defined as the unique fixed point of Ferns et al.'s equation, is a bicausal optimal-transport distance, and it equals the value of a finite linear program over occupancy couplings *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-354](../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md): An observer's power to refute a predictor depends on its access to the predictor as well as on its budget: against tests that see only the sampled prediction a predictor of size O(s/ε²) always passes, but if fine-grained clique counting is hard, or BPP ≠ PSPACE, some cheap tests that may query the predictor adaptively pass only predictors about as costly as nature's own *(used by 3; also distributed-agency, formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-391](../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md): Recovery of a k-sparse vector by ℓ₁ minimization from n random measurements in dimension N switches, as N grows with δ = n/N and ρ = k/n fixed, from near-certain success to near-certain failure across a curve ρ(δ) that, for Gaussian matrices, the authors' earlier face-counting theorems fix; in 2,948,000 optimizations at N = 200, 400 and 1600, eight non-Gaussian ensembles approached that curve in a way consistent with gaps shrinking as N^(−1/2), an exponent fitted on the same data, while at finite N the location depended on the ensemble *(used by 3; also formal-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-698](../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md): Thresholding linear attribute probes on a language model's embeddings yields a complete concept lattice for any incidence whatever, so the lattice is guaranteed by construction; what the Lattice Representation Hypothesis measured is per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o annotations at F1 70–83, and no lattice law *(used by 2; also pragmatic-transport)*
- [THEORY-1054](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1054.md): One arrangement of harmonic particles on a finite graph, with the same wiring, potential and inverse-mass response, gives the discrete wave equation when the integrator stores position and momentum and the discrete heat equation when it stores position alone; both are governed by the symmetrized graph Laplacian, and the coupling data do not decide between them *(used by 2; also distributed-agency)*
- [THEORY-1060](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1060.md): Robinson's claim that sheaves are the canonical data structure for sensor integration rests on an axiomatization, not a theorem: six axioms are posited as what an integrated sensor system must be and a sheaf is defined as whatever satisfies them, the paper calls sheaves one of many co-universal information representations, and its consistency and fusion tools need only a presheaf *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1063](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1063.md): Black-boxing a passive linear circuit, which keeps only the Lagrangian relation its terminals' potentials and currents can jointly satisfy, is a hypergraph functor from open circuits to Lagrangian relations: the external behaviour of a circuit glued from parts is the relational composite of the parts' external behaviours, so circuits with the same behaviour are interchangeable in every composite, and the effective relation a composite presents at its boundary is fixed by its parts' black boxes alone *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1090](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md): Eliminating an interior vertex of a cellular sheaf on a graph can leave its boundary a space of consistent assignments that no sheaf on the boundary vertices has: the interior can impose a constraint among boundary vertices that no set of pairwise compatibility conditions expresses, so Kron reduction, which turns the Laplacian of a connected graph into a graph Laplacian on any set of boundary vertices, fails for sheaves in general and holds when every vertex stalk has dimension at most one *(used by 6; also distributed-agency, record-as-apparatus)*
- [THEORY-1335](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1335.md): In Juarrero's constraint account, context-independent constraints take conditions away from equiprobability and context-dependent ones away from independence (after Gatlin); enabling constraints couple separate processes into a coherent dynamic whose constitutive constraints then act top down as second-order governing constraints that confine its components to a subregion of state space; a constraint is defined as what raises or lowers barriers to energy flow without transferring kinetic energy, carries no time-scale condition, and the governing regime is held not to be other than the components *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1372](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1372.md): Eppstein shows that folding problems split by question: deciding whether a finite crease pattern folds flat is fixed-parameter tractable in ply and treewidth with an ETH-optimal dependence on treewidth, reaching one flat state from another in a hinged-square toy model is PSPACE-complete and counting its states #P-complete, and flat-foldability of self-similar crease patterns with infinitely many creases on a finite square is undecidable *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-1375](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1375.md): Ito, Demaine, Harvey, Papadimitriou, Sideri, Uehara and Uno show that deciding whether one feasible solution can be turned into another through feasible solutions differing in one element at a time is PSPACE-complete for the reconfiguration versions of many NP-complete problems and polynomial for some problems in P such as matroid bases and matchings, and that minimising or maximising the worst intermediate objective is NP-hard to approximate in some cases and 2-approximable in others *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1376](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1376.md): Lawvere shows that a generalized metric space is exactly a category enriched in the extended non-negative reals under addition, with the triangle inequality as composition, so that dropping symmetry and finiteness is natural and enriched-category constructions specialise to metric-space theory *(used by 5; also readiness)*
- [THEORY-1379](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1379.md): Wille's formal concept analysis, as restated by Ignatov: for any relation between objects and attributes, the two derivation operators form an antitone Galois connection whose closed pairs form a complete lattice, every complete lattice arises so, and an attribute implication A → B holds exactly when every object with all of A has all of B, that is, when B lies in the closure of A *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1381](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1381.md): Foschi, Hull and Ku give closed-form equations in the tangents of half the folding angles, one for opposite and one for adjacent folding angles, that describe the full configuration space of any degree-4 rigid origami vertex, Euclidean or non-Euclidean, as two folding modes, the two branches of a square root, which meet at the flat state of a developable vertex and cannot meet there when the sector angles do not sum to 2π; the arXiv copy prints the opposite-angle equation with two signs wrong *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1389](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1389.md): Connelly and Whiteley prove that for tensegrity frameworks first-order rigidity implies prestress stability, which implies second-order rigidity, which implies rigidity, give bar-framework examples that none of these implications reverses, and prove that whether a first-order flex extends to second order is decided by a Farkas-type test on the framework's proper self-stresses *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1390](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1390.md): Hopkins (2010) holds that all freedom–constraint space pairs of a flexure-guided rigid body fall into 50 types, that only those whose constraint space holds enough pure-force lines can be realised by parallel flexures while the rest need modules stacked in series, and that where linear actuators must act to drive the permitted motions without parasitic error is computed from a stiffness matrix that carries each flexure's location, orientation, geometry and material *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1398](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1398.md): In mesoscopic simulation, DeLuca et al. find that DNA origami folds hierarchically, accessible structures collapsing into a locally ordered precursor that then crystallizes, while larger structures show frequent trapping in metastable states, among them a global topological trap, and early coalescence is not a perfect predictor of their final folding *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1406](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1406.md): Hopkins (2007) holds that for a rigid stage held in parallel by ideal wire-like flexures under small motions, the motions the stage permits and the lines along which a constraint can be added without changing them determine each other uniquely as reciprocal screw spaces, and that for pure-force constraints these pairs fall into 26 types indexed by the number of non-redundant constraints *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1407](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1407.md): Gopalan, Kolaitis, Maneva and Papadimitriou show that, for Boolean constraint languages with constants, deciding whether two solutions are joined by single-variable flips through solutions is either in polynomial time with components of linear diameter or PSPACE-complete with components of possibly exponential diameter, according to a property of the language that properly contains Schaefer's tractable classes and does not follow the boundaries of Boolean clones, a boundary Schwerdtfeger later corrected slightly toward the hard side *(used by 6)*
- [THEORY-1413](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1413.md): Schwerdtfeger shows that Gopalan, Kolaitis, Maneva and Papadimitriou's connectivity dichotomies for Boolean constraint languages overlooked constraints in which a variable occurs twice, and that they hold once tight sets are replaced by safely tight ones, whose relations keep their component properties when variables are identified, which moves the boundary slightly toward the hard side *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1414](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1414.md): Rocks and Mehta show that stating Maxwell–Calladine counting in terms of elastic susceptibilities gives an index theorem that holds with prestress and heterogeneous stiffness, in which the zero-displacement tensions are the states of self-stress while the forces that excite each linear zero mode follow the joint symmetry of geometry and energy, and on two worked networks prestress breaking a geometric symmetry redirects those forces and localizes them to the prestressed bonds without changing the mechanisms *(used by 6)*
- [THEORY-1417](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1417.md): Zang, Zhao, Misseroni and Paulino show that prestressing Kresling origami cells with controllable springs tunes each cell's energy barrier and stability continuously, so that reordering the barriers of cells in an assembly makes folding sequences feasible that the unprestressed assembly cannot follow *(used by 4)*
- [THEORY-1418](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1418.md): Stern, Pinson and Murugan find, in zero-temperature simulations of idealized rigid-panel crease patterns designed with one folding motion, distractor branches at the flat state whose number grows exponentially with the sheet's boundary length on random meshes up to 6 × 6, which they trace to frustrated loops of two-branch vertices; and, on one 4 × 4 pattern, that whether the actuated creases' folding islands cover the sheet predicts folding success much better than the number of actuators, and that an added actuator can ruin a folding that succeeded, without a necessary and sufficient condition *(used by 4; also readiness)*
- [THEORY-1422](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1422.md): Botnan and Lesnick report that multiparameter persistence modules are of wild representation type, so that no barcode-like complete invariant is practical and good barcodes need not exist, while the interleaving distance extends the bottleneck distance with stability and universality but is NP-hard to compute for two or more parameters *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1423](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1423.md): Berry, Lee-Trimble and Santangelo find that near the flat state a non-intersecting rigid origami vertex with small positive Gaussian curvature has a configuration space split into two components (popped up and popped down) that no rigid, non-tearing motion joins, while for small negative curvature the two stay joined by a neck, except at a degree-four vertex, which is split for both signs *(used by 3; also readiness)*
- [THEORY-1427](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1427.md): Chen and Santangelo find that a flat triangulated rigid origami sits at a singular point of its configuration space, where it admits more first-order motions than its generic dimension; in numerical root-finding on random triangulations with four boundary vertices and 2 to 8 internal vertices, 2^Vi folding branches meet there with a few exceptions, two for each pair of a vertex popping pattern and its global reversal, which they prove for triangulations built by Henneberg-1 moves, and they conclude that a generic self-folding structure is likely to become trapped in a misfolded state *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1428](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1428.md): Evans, Silverberg and Santangelo show that a lattice theory of origami tessellations predicts that the inhomogeneous soft deformations of a Miura-ori sheet are edge modes decaying from its boundaries with an analytic decay length, so that its number of degrees of freedom scales with its perimeter, not its area *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1430](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1430.md): Vipond shows that the persistence landscape extends to multiparameter persistence modules as a function that is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and whose weighted versions together determine the rank invariant of a finitely presented module, although no complete discrete invariant exists for such modules *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1432](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1432.md): Murray and Sastry show, with Chow's theorem as they recall it, that locally, where the bracket distributions have constant rank, a driftless system whose input vector fields, with their iterated Lie brackets, span every direction can be steered between configurations even though its constraints forbid instantaneous motion in some directions, and that for first-order, second-order and chained systems sinusoids at integrally related frequencies do the steering, one bracketing level at a time *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1434](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1434.md): Raussen shows that for a concurrent PV program on shared resources of given capacities, a spare capacity computed from the program text bounds from below the connectivity of every space of executions to the target, so that spare capacity zero marks deadlocks, at least one excludes them, and at least two makes all executions equivalent *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1435](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1435.md): Marsden and Zwart propose that quantitative resource theories are categories enriched in a commutative quantale, whose monoid combines the costs, probabilities or strengths of successive conversion steps and whose join selects the best alternative, with costly conversions as profunctors and closure under composition as a free internal monad *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1437](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1437.md): Cumberworth and Reinhardt review simulation results indicating that, in DNA origami, a staple's later domains bind without a second translational entropy penalty once its first domain is bound, while each loop closed with the scaffold adds a penalty that depends on the order of binding, and that in the small designs simulated the first effect outweighs the second, so that staples tend to bind fully once started, while assembly is mostly downhill and needs no nucleation barrier, unlike DNA bricks *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1440](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1440.md): Sobczak reports, from work in the Dietz group, that 3D DNA origami folds cooperatively within a structure-specific window of about 5 °C and can be folded at a constant temperature within it, while folded objects held for two hours above the window unfold only 5–10 °C higher and within seconds, against minutes to hours for folding, and that the brick forms nothing in 48 hours 6 °C above its best folding temperature; the thesis does not pair persistence and non-formation at one temperature *(used by 3)*
- [THEORY-1441](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1441.md): Schneider, Möritz and Dietz show that, in isothermal folding at 50 °C of one multilayer DNA origami brick, staple domains bind in a defined order set more by the scaffold's topology of connectivity than by their binding strength, the two termini of a staple bind independently by a fit that itself assumes their independence, and a set of early-binding nucleating domains forms a compacted intermediate without which the object still folds but hours later by a slower pathway *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1442](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1442.md): Lee Tin Wah and colleagues show, from AFM snapshots of Rothemund's tall rectangle adsorbed out of solution along a slow cooling ramp, that with 52 nM of each staple folding nucleates at the top and bottom ends between about 65 and 55 °C and grows toward the centre, and that raising the central staples to 670 nM while lowering the outermost edge-row staples to 1.2 nM makes folding nucleate at the centre instead, which they attribute to the concentration dependence of staple melting temperatures under thermodynamic rather than kinetic control *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1443](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1443.md): Wagenbauer, Wachauf and Dietz show that a 42-helix multilayer DNA origami bundle with 5 or 15 of its 207 staples omitted looks the same as the complete object under negative-stain TEM averaging and agarose-gel mobility, while a gel-based fluorescent de Bruijn probe for unpaired bases tells them apart and, across five bundle designs, estimates that complete reactions still leave 44 to 263 of 7,560 bases unpaired, 96.5% to over 99% quality, depending on design and folding schedule *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1444](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1444.md): Douglas and colleagues report that custom multilayer DNA origami on a honeycomb lattice folds in one pot at 7 to 44 % of scaffold in monomer, many of the designs only with week-long thermal ramps at about 16 mM MgCl2 and low NaCl, short ramps, low Mg2+ or high Na+ giving slow-migrating, grossly misshapen products, whereas flat origami and simpler nanotube structures fold in 72-minute ramps *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1445](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1445.md): Aksel, Navarro, Fong and Douglas report that choosing DNA origami staple breakpoints by a shortest-path search over a weighted graph, scored by an equilibrium free energy summing staple binding, scaffold loop closure and hybridization at 50 °C, raised the gel-measured yield of accurately folded multilayer blocks from 2-6% to 48-61% in four published designs, three of them with unchanged scaffold route and helix layout, with yields correlating with the model's score *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1446](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1446.md): Majikes and colleagues find, across 34 designs of one 2D DNA origami rectangle annealed under deliberately poor conditions and scored by AFM classification, that defectivity tracks design-level aggregates: the skew of the distribution of loop-entropy penalties each fold would pay if it bound first and the measured melt temperature are its principal correlates, a linear combination of these with a staple-blocking metric collapses 28 of the designs onto one trend, and designs with more short folds at the expense of medium folds are more defective *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1447](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1447.md): Dannenberg and colleagues show, in a thermodynamically self-consistent domain-level kinetic model of planar DNA origami, that cooperativity between staples from scaffold loop closure and coaxial stacking sharpens the folding transition and produces folding/melting hysteresis, and that the hysteresis is asymmetric, faster cooling or fewer staples lowering the annealing temperature far more than they raise or move the melting temperature, because binding rates are nearly temperature-independent while unbinding rates rise steeply with temperature *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1448](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1448.md): Ni and colleagues show that, in DNA origami cross-tile self-replication, binding a monomer tile to a template raises the effective concentration of its tethered sticky ends from about 1 nM to about 0.8 mM by their estimate, about 0.2 mM by a FRET fit, and shifts their melting temperature by about 50 °C, that a two-state model with three entropy terms, fitted once, predicts the melting temperatures of 1- to 4-tile assemblies to about 2 °C, and that with externally supplied tiles, a thermal cycle and UV crosslinking the per-cycle replication rate falls from about 1.9 for dimers to 1.6 for tetramers *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1449](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1449.md): Zhou, Sha, Ni, Seeman and Chaikin show that, in a non-enzymatic DNA origami dimer replicator fed fresh monomers each thermal and UV cycle, a species arising only by a designed mutation of about 3.5% per copy reaches parity within five cycles and dominates after about nine when its growth rate per cycle is higher, growth rate being the only fitness the system has, while two species that grow alike approach equal shares *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1450](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1450.md): Douglas, Bachelet and Church built a DNA-origami barrel whose opening is governed by two aptamer locks forming a logical AND gate over cell-surface antigen inputs, so that the device stays closed and reconfigures to expose its payload only when both designated keys are present, shorter locks also opening spontaneously more often, with the key concentration needed to open set by the lock-duplex length, activation at about 10 pM for 16 to 23 bp against about 1 nM for 30 to 44 bp *(used by 2)*
- [THEORY-1451](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1451.md): Winfree and Bekbolatov show, in kinetic Tile Assembly Model simulation and kinetic-trap theory, that replacing each tile of a tile set with a K×K block whose internal bonds are unique keeps the logical assembly unchanged but forces any mismatch to stall until it dissociates, raising the optimal speed for a target error ε from r ≈ βε² to r ≈ βε at K = 2; their thermodynamic argument predicts an error rate exponential in K, and the simulated gain beyond K = 2 falls short of it, which they attribute to facet-roughening errors that proofreading does not correct *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1452](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1452.md): Scheckenbach, Schubert, Forthmann, Glembockyte and Tinnefeld show that folded DNA origami can be repaired from strands supplied in solution, transiently bound labels regenerating indiscriminately after photobleaching and added staples being taken up only where shorter staples left a scaffold toehold of 4 or 8 nt, which they take to be how damaged sites are repaired, so that a matching staple pool keeps 76 % of nanorulers intact over 11 days in 0.2 % serum against 12 % without; such self-healing fails to outpace damage at higher nuclease levels, and damage to the scaffold cannot be repaired *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1453](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1453.md): Cumberworth, Frenkel and Reinhardt show, in Monte Carlo free-energy calculations of a domain-level lattice model of small planar DNA origami, that typical designs with two-domain staples and edge or single-domain staples assemble downhill with no nucleation barrier, that a maximum-crossover design with three-domain staples has a barrier of about 10 kBT, about 20 kBT at domain resolution, at its melting temperature which vanishes a few degrees below it, and that the presence and height of the barrier are set mainly by coaxial stacking between adjacent staples, not by hybridization strength *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1454](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1454.md): Majikes and colleagues find, in a single-fold DNA origami model measured by FRET melting with affine baseline correction, that closing a fold with an already anchored staple is unimolecular and more stable than bimolecular binding of the same domain, and that the fold's melting temperature falls as fold distance grows, by up to more than 10 °C from short to long, through a configurational-entropy cost; from this they infer, without testing it, that origami folds by nucleation and growth, a staple's longest domain binding first and short, entropically cheap folds then making neighbouring folds cheaper *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1455](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1455.md): Shirt-Ediss, Torelli and colleagues report that, for four DNA origami designs each folded from three scaffold sequences with fully complementary staples under one protocol, the sequence that their energy model scored highest in off-target staple–scaffold, scaffold–scaffold, staple–staple and hairpin binding gave the fewest well-folded AFM objects in every design (0–20% against up to about 66–75%), and they attribute the loss to kinetic trapping and scaffold aggregation *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1456](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1456.md): Rothemund shows that a 7-kilobase single-stranded scaffold routed through a shape, with about 200 unpurified staple strands in excess designed to bind only the scaffold, folds in one two-hour anneal from 95 °C to 20 °C into designed shapes about 100 nm across, with AFM-judged yields of well-formed structures from about 1% to 90% by design and at least 70% for rigid designs on circular scaffold; he proposes, without testing, that strand invasion, staple excess and cooperative staple binding account for this *(used by 1)*
- [THEORY-1457](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1457.md): Majikes, Patrone, Kearsley, Zwolak and Liddle find, in a single-fold DNA origami model with a topology-reporting fluorophore and quencher, that the folded-state yield after annealing rises with staple excess to a turnover between about 1x and 5x and then falls, below 50 % at high excess for fold distances of 131, 1187 and 3407 bases, independent of staple motif at the one fold distance where motif was tested and, by the authors' report of a supplementary control, unchanged by a twofold slower anneal, as an equilibrium model predicts when each fold domain can be occupied by a separate staple, the blocked state, with folded over blocked equal to the fold's j-factor over the free staple concentration; they propose, without testing it, that whole origami escapes this through cooperativity and strand displacement along a nucleation front *(used by 2)*

## Readings no line uses

Readings in force that no entry of the record's argument grounds on, is
corroborated or bounded by, asks about, takes a case from or draws on, by
primary topic. They are
where the argument has not yet built on what the record has read.
### agency

- [THEORY-636](../record/theory.d/THEORY-636.md): In vignette studies of US online participants, judgements that an outcome happened because the agent wanted it move with judgements that it was done intentionally when luck is manipulated, and predict them better than know-how or probability-raising do; but they account for only about half of the luck effect, and in one morally neutral case the two come apart

### causality

- [THEORY-580](../record/theory.d/THEORY-580.md): On any cover of a space of input histories, the empirical models compatible with a causal structure are exactly the points of a polytope cut from a product of simplices by linear causality equations, so how much of a model a causal structure can explain is a linear program; causal separability is relative to an assumed ambient structure, and the causally separable fraction is never less than the separable local fraction
- [THEORY-1025](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1025.md): The inputs causal scrubbing samples for a treeified hypothesis are the unique maximum-entropy distribution, on finite inputs, among those that give the inputs of every interpretation node the joint distribution they have on the data, so whatever the hypothesis does not claim is resampled as independently as the claims allow
- [THEORY-1123](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1123.md): In COTA's formulation of causal abstraction learning as multi-marginal optimal transport, the term meant to impose do-calculus relations between the transport plans of comparable interventions depends only on the plans' marginals and on normalisers built from them, which the transport constraints fix to the empirical distributions, so it is constant on the feasible set; its weight changes the solution only by rescaling the cost and entropy weights, and the paper's evidence that the constraints help, a sweep over that weight, cannot separate the two

### cognition

- [THEORY-471](../record/theory.d/THEORY-471.md): Psychological states are not the machine-table states of an organism's unique best description as a probabilistic automaton, because some are never occurrent, several hold at once, there are indefinitely many and they contain one another, none of which a machine-table state can be; this leaves open that they are computational states of such a system
- [THEORY-547](../record/theory.d/THEORY-547.md): A language model idealized as continuing any text with a plausible next word from the collection of all plausible texts follows narrative coherence and not truth, so its false statements are confabulations within the story the context sets up; whether trained and aligned chat models keep that nature is an open empirical question the idealization does not settle
- [THEORY-609](../record/theory.d/THEORY-609.md): When implementing an automaton requires reliable, counterfactual-supporting transitions for every formal state, Putnam's construction fails, but any system with a clock and a dial still implements every inputless finite-state automaton, and any system with the right input–output dependencies, an input memory and a dial implements every finite-state automaton with those dependencies, so finite-state automata cannot carry computational sufficiency; combinatorial-state automata are argued, not proved, to escape
- [THEORY-1519](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1519.md): Simkute, Tankelevitch and colleagues argue that generative AI shows task-complexity polarization, the pattern Human Factors research calls clumsy automation: it makes easy tasks easier and hard tasks harder, which for automation in general they explain by easy tasks being easier to automate, leaving the user the hard share with the added task of monitoring, and for generative AI by the shift to evaluating output, disrupted workflows, interruptions and subtle errors in long suggestions, all of which weigh most on demanding tasks

### complex-systems

- [THEORY-581](../record/theory.d/THEORY-581.md): Two exactly consistent descriptions of one system, at different scales and with equal past–future mutual information, can differ in how that information divides between redundancy and synergy; in small generated Boolean networks under the Williams–Beer redundancy measure the coarser scale was more synergy-biased in every random stochastic system, by at most about 0.07, and the direction mostly reversed for redundancy-biased deterministic ones
- [THEORY-608](../record/theory.d/THEORY-608.md): On one physical piano-movers puzzle scaled to the solver, ant groups solve better as they grow, while human groups barred from speech and gesture solve worse than individuals and talking groups only about as well as one; large ant groups keep speed and heading through wall contact, and the human mechanisms offered are fitted or observed informally, not tested
- [THEORY-696](../record/theory.d/THEORY-696.md): Under multiplicative noise, members that pool their resources and split them equally every step each grow faster in the long run than they would alone, with no complementarity, relatedness or reciprocity: N independent geometric Brownian motions that share keep their drift μ and cut their volatility to σ/√N, raising each one's time-average growth rate from μ − σ²/2 to μ − σ²/(2N); the gain vanishes as their noise becomes perfectly correlated, and a sufficiently superior member does better alone
- [THEORY-1122](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1122.md): Weiss's mark of a system, that the whole varies far less than the summed variances of its parts, is met by any aggregate of independent parts when the whole is measured as their average; when it is measured as their sum, it holds only if the parts' fluctuations compensate one another, with ∑ᵢ<ⱼ Cov(xᵢ, xⱼ) close to −½ ∑ᵢ Var(xᵢ)
- [THEORY-1301](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1301.md): In the Haken–Kelso–Bunz potential V(φ) = −a cos φ − b cos 2φ, switching the parameters in time from no landscape (a = b = 0) to two wells (a = b = 1) to one well (a = 1, b = 0) makes the spread of the relative phase across trials rise while both wells are open and fall after one is removed, the pattern Sánchez-Cañizares compares qualitatively with post-stimulus quenching of trial-to-trial variability in decision tasks; under Gaussian white noise of the stated strength q = 1 the spread of cos φ settles near 0.40, not at 0

### compositionality

- [THEORY-1057](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1057.md): Gradient descent with backpropagation, weight decay and Newton's method are one discrete-time semantics of an operad of potential-carrying lenses, in which the state moves by subtracting the sharpened sum of three pulled-back covectors (from the output, from the input wiring and from the potential); the semantics is an operad functor, so a composite's update is assembled from its parts' updates, and backpropagation is that functoriality

### consciousness

- [THEORY-498](../record/theory.d/THEORY-498.md): A mathematical structure whose domains are aspects of experience and whose axioms hold there is not thereby a structure of experience, because that test passes incompatible topologies on one set and every rescaling of a metric without consulting experience; requiring, for each relation, an aspect that changes exactly when a variation of experience breaks the relation removes those automatic passes, and has so far been met only by relative similarity and a visual topology, each on an assumed premise
- [THEORY-597](../record/theory.d/THEORY-597.md): Meditation-related experiences that Western Buddhist practitioners report as challenging span 59 kinds in seven domains, from fear and sleep change to altered self-other boundaries, and they are reported in daily practice, at under an hour a day and in the first days of practice, not only on intensive retreat; the frequencies come from a sample chosen for difficulty, and the causal link is the practitioners' own attribution

### contextuality

- [THEORY-309](../record/theory.d/THEORY-309.md): If contexts are defined by joint measurability alone, every nondisturbing correlation, maximally contextual ones included, is realized by trivial measurements on a one-dimensional quantum system, so Kochen–Specker contextuality needs a stronger operational notion of context
- [THEORY-524](../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md): On cyclic measurement scenarios, where the contexts' overlaps form one chordless N-cycle, the ℤ/2 Čech obstruction computed on the (N−1)-th iterated joint model is exact for logical and strong contextuality, the bound N − 1 being tight; beyond cycles no such result is established, the published extension is false on its own example, and the completeness conjecture fails on a Kochen–Specker cover that is never detected at any level
- [THEORY-526](../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md): The Čech cohomology obstruction of a support section is a sound but incomplete witness of contextuality: it vanishes exactly when the section lies in a compatible family of integer combinations of support sections, so it is non-zero on every section of every All-vs-Nothing model, over any coefficient ring, on a connected cover, yet it misses the Hardy model entirely, part of a strongly contextual Kochen–Specker cover, and every section of a strongly contextual model on the fully symmetric (2,2,4) Bell cover

### control-theory

- [THEORY-1254](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1254.md): A controller that must stay safe under every model it has not ruled out cannot use the evidence its committing action produces: if the information it can gather before its first action that forecloses a safe continuation under an alternative is bounded by β, every such controller forfeits at least about ½e^{−β} of the value reachable only by committing, so a linear oracle gap gives linear regret, and acting on an exclusion at risk α needs about log(1/(2α)) nats gathered beforehand
- [THEORY-1256](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1256.md): When a conservative experiment is safe under every plausible model, can be repeated from a common state and keeps informing, a controller that acts on the lower end of an anytime confidence sequence stays safe with probability 1 − δ and approaches the safe oracle, at O(√(T log T)) regret in a braking example; a certainty-equivalent controller in the same example is unsafe with probability ½ in every episode however much data it has

### emotion-and-affect

- [THEORY-1282](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1282.md): Affect, in Massumi's sense, is the felt transition of a body's power to affect and be affected toward a diminished or augmented capacitation, offered as a proposition to be regenerated in each use rather than a definition to apply

### epistemology

- [THEORY-422](../record/theory.d/THEORY-422.md): In the standard formal models of group learning, no communication network is best for every epistemic problem: costly transmission favours minimally connected or star networks, pooling of estimates by averaging favours regular networks, and learning by trying in bandit problems can favour sparse ones, so a group's network cannot be judged until its learning problem is known
- [THEORY-649](../record/theory.d/THEORY-649.md): When agents holding uniformly random consistent theories over two or three atomic sentences each average their theories once, bit by bit, with all peers within a Hamming bound of confidence, an individual agent ends up with the inconsistent theory at most 1.81% of the time, but the chance that some agent in the group does reaches 6.4% for two sentences and 16.9% for three

### ethics

- [THEORY-677](../record/theory.d/THEORY-677.md): Under uncertainty about which beings are sentient, an appeal to precaution does not by itself fix which error is worse to make: precaution on behalf of a possibly sentient being and precaution on behalf of human liberty point opposite ways, and judging which mistake costs more turns on the very science in doubt

### game-theory

- [THEORY-835](../record/theory.d/THEORY-835.md): When two firms each hire the best available candidate by a noisy ranking, and the ranking model makes an independent re-ranking worth more to the second mover than its own next choice and makes a weaker first mover better for it, then for every accuracy of the private rankings there is a more accurate shared algorithmic ranking that each firm strictly prefers to use whatever the other does, and with which both firms, and total welfare, do worse than if neither used it
- [THEORY-930](../record/theory.d/THEORY-930.md): In empirical games built from about a thousand sampled search agents in eight OpenSpiel board games, most on 3×3 or 4×4 boards, and in the AlphaStar league, Nash clusters taken from maximum-entropy equilibria are, read against a fitted skew-normal curve with no test, largest at intermediate transitive strength and narrower toward the strongest and the weakest strategies, while Blotto, the disc game, Kuhn poker and noisy Elo games do not show that profile
- [THEORY-945](../record/theory.d/THEORY-945.md): When each agent's Q-function is approximated as an average of pairwise terms and expanded about the mean action of its neighbours, the first-order term vanishes and the approximation error is a second-order remainder bounded by the curvature of the pairwise Q-function, leaving a two-body problem between an agent and its neighbours' average; Yang et al. state that with homogeneous agents mean field Q-learning converges to the Nash Q-value under three assumptions, one of which they call a strong constraint, by a proof whose contraction step needs a temperature above K/2 while its greedy-in-the-limit assumption needs the temperature to fall to zero; in their Gaussian Squeeze runs with 500 and 1000 agents, mean field Q-learning and actor-critic learned the optimal allocation where independent learners, FMQ, Rec-FMQ and a MADDPG variant failed

### information-geometry

- [THEORY-427](../record/theory.d/THEORY-427.md): For gradient matrices of rank at most r, the Kronecker product of the square roots of the accumulated row and column gradient second moments dominates the full-matrix AdaGrad statistic up to the factor r, so preconditioning each side of a weight matrix by a fourth root, as Shampoo does, preconditions at least as strongly as full-matrix AdaGrad and has O(√T) regret for convex Lipschitz losses
- [THEORY-731](../record/theory.d/THEORY-731.md): For softmax cross-entropy with balanced classes, the Gauss–Newton matrix splits exactly into four positive semidefinite second-moment terms, the class-centre term has rank at most C with eigenvectors in the span of the class centres and the spectrum of a C × C Gram matrix, and so the k-th eigenvalue of the whole is never below the k-th eigenvalue of the class-centre term

### information-theory

- [THEORY-237](../record/theory.d/THEORY-237.md): The critic-based variational lower bounds on mutual information, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE's and InfoNCE, are relaxations of one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound, and, when the joint and the product of the marginals are mutually absolutely continuous, each attains its supremum over critics only at a critic equal to the log density ratio up to a term its normalization leaves free, where every bound but InfoNCE equals the mutual information
- [THEORY-308](../record/theory.d/THEORY-308.md): The neural Donsker–Varadhan estimator of mutual information is strongly consistent as an extremum estimator over compact families of critics, and, for critics bounded by M and L-Lipschitz in their d parameters, its uniform deviation from the population bound needs a number of samples set by d, M, L and the parameter radius, not by the data dimension
- [THEORY-479](../record/theory.d/THEORY-479.md): Shannon's chain rule is the 1-cocycle equation of a cohomology of finite probability spaces whose action is averaged conditioning, and on connected, sufficiently rich structures of partitions every measurable 1-cocycle is a constant multiple of Shannon entropy, with no symmetry or continuity axiom assumed; in the unitary-invariant quantum version the first cohomology vanishes and von Neumann entropy is the 0-cochain whose coboundary is minus Shannon entropy
