- [THEORY-513](../record/theory.d/THEORY-513.md): Observational entropy taken relative to a maximum-entropy prior τ, S(τ) − D_M(ρ‖τ), lies between S(ρ) and S(τ) for states meeting the prior's constraint, is finite and continuous whenever S(τ) is, and reduces to about two dozen textbook entropies by choice of measurement and prior; its second laws are bounds on the time-averaged state's divergence from the prior, proved small only under sufficient conditions (nondegenerate energy gaps for equilibration, the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis for fit to the prior)
- [THEORY-568](../record/theory.d/THEORY-568.md): Whatever redundancy measure a partial information decomposition uses, provided its atoms satisfy the consistency equation, the average number of single sources an atom can be read from is Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) and the average number of sources it cannot do without is Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y); so the redundancy–synergy index equals (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y), and for three or more sources it counts a k-way redundancy k − 1 times but synergy once
- [THEORY-599](../record/theory.d/THEORY-599.md): In trained neural-network weights stored as BF16 or FP32, nearly all the redundancy a lossless coder can remove lies in the floating-point exponent, which occupies about 40 of its 256 values and compresses to about a third under single-symbol Huffman coding, while sign and mantissa are near-incompressible; the redundancy belongs to the number format, not to the learned function
- [THEORY-617](../record/theory.d/THEORY-617.md): In additive Gaussian noise independent of an input of finite power whose law does not depend on the signal-to-noise ratio, the derivative of mutual information with respect to that ratio is half the minimum mean-square error of the optimal noncausal estimator, so mutual information is accumulated estimation error over SNR; in continuous time the causal filtering error equals the noncausal error averaged over SNR, and the identity fails with feedback
- [THEORY-701](../record/theory.d/THEORY-701.md): Transfer entropy from J to I is the Kullback entropy of assuming that I's next state, given its last k states, does not depend on J's last l states, so it is zero exactly when J's past leaves I's transition law unchanged; unlike time-delayed mutual information it is directional and zero for static correlation, and it removes a common input only when that input is conditioned on
- [THEORY-716](../record/theory.d/THEORY-716.md): Synergy can be measured as the whole minus the union of its parts, the union information being the least information the sources could jointly carry about the target with every source–target marginal held fixed; this synergy lies between WholeMinusSum and Williams and Beer's S_max, which respectively subtract redundancy and count unique information as synergy, and for two sources it is Bertschinger et al.'s synergy, so independent sources can share information about a target, as the authors' last version concedes against their first

### learning-theory

- [THEORY-574](../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md): The structural width of Xin Li's learning programme is a covering number of the margin-safe region by local pieces: its lower bounds come from metric confinement through a wedge point, not from topology, labels enter only through the margin, and the error floor below width binds only learners assembled from local experts, so it does not entail routing, nor training routing apart from the task loss
- [THEORY-735](../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md): Under a local quadratic model of the loss with the greedy optimal step, per-step progress at batch size B is ΔL_max/(1 + B_noise/B), and at fixed B the steps and examples needed satisfy (S/S_min − 1)(E/E_min − 1) = 1, with E_min/S_min the progress-weighted mean of B_noise
- [THEORY-1253](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1253.md): Treating the Bayesian evidence as a partition function with sample size as inverse temperature, the analogue of heat capacity, the rate at which leave-one-out predictive loss falls with sample size, equals half the parameter count in a regular model, as equipartition, and the real log canonical threshold in a singular one, falling below these where prior or discreteness fixes parameters; with multiplicity above one the approach to the singular value is only logarithmic, and the correspondence has no counterpart of physical current or dissipation

### linguistics

- [THEORY-477](../record/theory.d/THEORY-477.md): None of the ten morphosyntactic criteria linguists use to identify words is necessary and sufficient for the orthographic word across languages, and the test batteries that combine them pick criteria opportunistically, so no cross-linguistically valid definition of the word is yet available

### logic

- [THEORY-462](../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md): If commonsense knowledge includes defaults that later evidence displaces, a monotonic logic, in which an added axiom can never remove a theorem, cannot represent that displacement as it stands; Minsky's further claim, that no logistic system, one that separates propositions from general laws of inference, can carry commonsense knowledge even once repaired, is asserted, not shown
- [THEORY-595](../record/theory.d/THEORY-595.md): A filter over a set of worlds is a finitely consistent propositional theory and an ultrafilter a negation-complete one; read so, the ultrafilter extension theorem is Lindenbaum's lemma for propositions, and Łoś's theorem builds a model that makes true exactly what an ultrafilter says, which proves first-order compactness without proof theory, given the axiom of choice
- [THEORY-1150](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1150.md): In any logical system presented as an institution, theories can be glued wherever their vocabularies can: if the category of signatures has colimits, so does the category of theories, the glued theory being the semantic closure of the union of the parts' translated sentences; and because constraints requiring free or initial interpretation also obey the Satisfaction Condition, theories carrying them glue the same way

### loss-landscapes

- [THEORY-425](../record/theory.d/THEORY-425.md): A connecting path trained only on clean data keeps only the behaviour the clean data ask for: between two backdoored or error-injected image classifiers, models near the ends of such a path keep most clean accuracy and lose the attack, and a path flat in ordinary loss can carry a barrier in adversarial loss that tracks the input Hessian's top eigenvalue

### mathematical-statistics

- [THEORY-534](../record/theory.d/THEORY-534.md): The optimality of maximum likelihood was never one theorem: each historical proof holds under conditions its author left implicit, and of the classical counterexamples the practically important one is a parameter count growing with the sample, while Hodges-type superefficiency is confined to a set of measure zero

### mathematics

- [THEORY-314](../record/theory.d/THEORY-314.md): Every minimizer of an arbitrary cost on the training outputs plus a strictly increasing function of the RKHS norm lies in the span of the kernel functions at the training points, by the reproducing property and orthogonal decomposition alone
- [THEORY-392](../record/theory.d/THEORY-392.md): Every map from an n-point subset of a metric space into Hilbert space extends to the whole space with Lipschitz constant at most K√(log n) times its own, by dimension reduction to K log n coordinates followed by Kirszbraun and the non-linear Hahn–Banach theorem; for L_p, 1 ≤ p < 2, the constant must be at least δ(Log n/Log Log n)^(1/p−1/2), so √(log n) is right up to a log log factor in the worst case
- [THEORY-394](../record/theory.d/THEORY-394.md): Every n-point metric space embeds in Euclidean space of O(log n) dimensions with distortion O(log n), by distances to random sets of every scale followed by Johnson–Lindenstrauss, and constant-degree expanders need distortion Ω(log n) in every ℓ_p with 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, of any dimension, so O(log n) is tight in the worst case; the constants are unspecified, the lower bound rests on Leighton and Rao's flow–cut gap, and nothing is shown for trees or for p > 2
- [THEORY-396](../record/theory.d/THEORY-396.md): Every Lipschitz map from an n-point metric space into any Banach space extends to any containing space with Lipschitz constant at most C log n/log log n times its own, by averaging over random partitions at every scale, and every n-point subset of L₂ extends into any Banach space at C√(log n) after Johnson–Lindenstrauss dimension reduction; for maps into Hilbert space this is no improvement on K√(log n), and whether √(log n) suffices for every target is left open
- [THEORY-398](../record/theory.d/THEORY-398.md): A Lipschitz map from a subset of a metric space whose points are at least ε apart and whose diameter is D extends to the whole space into Hilbert space with Lipschitz constant at most 6D/ε times its own, and, by Benyamini's argument in the same paper, into any Banach space with at most 4D/ε, with no dependence on the number of points
- [THEORY-400](../record/theory.d/THEORY-400.md): A metric space that admits, at every scale, random partitions into small pieces with each point padded away from piece boundaries with constant probability is absolutely Lipschitz extendable: maps from it into any Banach space extend to any containing space at O(1/padding), which gives C log λ for doubling constant λ, C r² for K_r-minor-free graph metrics, C(g+1) on genus-g surfaces and C√d from ℓ₂ᵈ; the bounds are upper bounds only, and the method needs a decomposition the domain may not have
- [THEORY-407](../record/theory.d/THEORY-407.md): For a log-integrable linear cocycle over an ergodic probability-preserving system, vectors grow at finitely many exponential rates along an invariant flag, and for isometries of a proper metric space with integrable displacement the linear drift is detected by a horofunction, with no curvature assumed
- [THEORY-430](../record/theory.d/THEORY-430.md): A real hyperplane arrangement in ℝⁿ has (−1)ⁿχ(−1) regions and (−1)^rank χ(1) bounded regions, where χ is the characteristic polynomial of its intersection poset, so these counts depend only on which hyperplanes meet and in what dimension, not on the shapes of the regions
- [THEORY-437](../record/theory.d/THEORY-437.md): When each agent's feasible actions depend on the others' actions, an equilibrium exists if every action set is a contractible polyhedron, every constraint correspondence has a closed graph with non-empty compact values, payoffs and the maximum-value functions are continuous, and every best-response set is contractible; convexity is not needed
- [THEORY-503](../record/theory.d/THEORY-503.md): The nearest rank-r matrix to a real matrix in the least-squares norm keeps its r largest singular values and zeroes the rest; it is unique when the r-th and (r+1)-th singular values differ, its squared error is the sum of the dropped squares, and the singular-vector factors that build it are not unique
- [THEORY-519](../record/theory.d/THEORY-519.md): Supervised learners compose only once each carries a request function that passes a corrected input upstream; with it they form a symmetric monoidal category, and for a fixed step size and an error whose derivative in its first argument is invertible, gradient descent with backpropagation is a faithful strong symmetric monoidal functor into it from differentiable parametrised functions
- [THEORY-530](../record/theory.d/THEORY-530.md): The spectrum of a matrix bounds the norm of its rational functions up to a constant only if the matrix is diagonalisable, with the eigenvector condition number as the constant, while the closed numerical range of any Hilbert-space operator does so with a universal constant between 2 and 11.08, exactly 2 for 2×2 matrices
- [THEORY-544](../record/theory.d/THEORY-544.md): In homotopy type theory extended with a strict directed interval and a layer of shapes, one contractibility condition, the Segal condition, gives a type identities, associativity and three-dimensional coherence, makes every function between Segal types a functor, and yields a dependent Yoneda lemma for covariant families; that such types are (∞,1)-categories rests on a semantics only sketched
- [THEORY-592](../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md): Every unital Banach *-algebra satisfying Gelfand and Naimark's norm conditions is isometrically *-isomorphic to a norm-closed algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, built from positive functionals by what is now the GNS construction, and a commutative one is the algebra of all continuous functions on its compact maximal-ideal space
- [THEORY-620](../record/theory.d/THEORY-620.md): Walsh's 1923 functions are a closed orthonormal set on (0, 1) of ±1-valued step functions, each a parity of finitely many binary digits, whose expansions behave like Fourier series: grouped uniform convergence for continuous functions, convergence under bounded variation, localisation, Cesàro summability, and divergence at any chosen point for some continuous function
- [THEORY-629](../record/theory.d/THEORY-629.md): Every continuous linear functional on a Hilbert space is the inner product with a unique vector of the same norm, given in any orthonormal basis by the conjugated values of the functional on the basis; completeness is what makes it so, and Riesz's 1907 statement on L² asserted only that a representing function exists
- [THEORY-642](../record/theory.d/THEORY-642.md): Basic two-level type theory, an inner homotopy type theory with an outer level of strict equality, is conservative over homotopy type theory, so an inner type it proves inhabited is already inhabited in HoTT, but a fibrant-replacement type former would force uniqueness of identity proofs on the inner level
- [THEORY-645](../record/theory.d/THEORY-645.md): A countable discrete abelian group and a compact second-countable abelian group can each be recovered as the character group of the other, and a locally compact, connected, second-countable abelian group is a compact group plus ℝʳ; Pontryagin's 1934 paper does not prove duality for general locally compact abelian groups
- [THEORY-685](../record/theory.d/THEORY-685.md): The Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture fails for every compact C² hypersurface with a point of non-zero curvature: for each large R a function and a weight violate it by a factor of order log R, which refutes Stein's conjecture as stated and closes the Mizohata–Takeuchi route to loss-free endpoint multilinear restriction
- [THEORY-686](../record/theory.d/THEORY-686.md): An observation modelled as a monotone map between preorders can show of a joined system more than the join of its observations of the parts, and out of a preorder with all joins the observations that preserve all joins, the empty join and infinite joins included, are exactly the left adjoints
- [THEORY-728](../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md): On a finite data set, a symmetric positive affinity normalized to a Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, and its eigenvectors scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data so that Euclidean distance equals the diffusion distance weighted by the inverse stationary law
- [THEORY-729](../record/theory.d/THEORY-729.md): An adjunction between a category and the opposite of another restricts to a dual equivalence between the full subcategories on which its unit and counit are isomorphisms
- [THEORY-730](../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md): For an embedding whose Gram matrix is the absolute co-occurrence deviation matrix at full rank, words on a periodic lattice whose positive and negative co-occurrence parts each depend only on separation have Fourier modes of the lattice as principal components, in degenerate cos/sin pairs with amplitude the square root of the kernel's Fourier transform, and the exponential kernel gives a closed loop with integer frequencies on a periodic lattice and an open curve with non-integer frequencies on an interval
- [THEORY-761](../record/theory.d/THEORY-761.md): A continuous piecewise-linear function on R^d with compact support has a Fourier transform that, along any fixed direction û, is bounded by C(û)k^(−2), and by C(û)k^(−d−1) whenever û is orthogonal to no edge of its linear regions, which is almost every direction; C(û) is not uniform and grows without bound near the exceptional directions; for a ReLU network without compact support the statement is not established
- [THEORY-829](../record/theory.d/THEORY-829.md): In Hrbacek's relative analysis, if belief at a context level is credence ultraclose to 1 at that level, the conjunction of any standard number of believed propositions is believed, while for an ultralarge number it can fail: in a fair lottery with an ultralarge number of tickets each 'this ticket loses' is believed and their conjunction has probability 0
- [THEORY-1077](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1077.md): On a presheaf of pseudometric spaces, the consistency radius of an assignment, the largest distance between an observation and the restriction of another, is zero exactly for assignments induced by global sections (in metric spaces) and, when the restrictions are K-Lipschitz, bounds the assignment's sup-distance from every global section below by ε/(1 + K); so fusing data into a consistent state must move it at least that far, and the bound needs no sheaf condition
- [THEORY-1121](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1121.md): With the couplings fixed, the square-loss Gromov–Wasserstein barycenter of several similarity matrices is their realigned average weighted by the barycenter weights, and the KL barycenter its weighted geometric average, so PSD and infinitely divisible inputs give barycenters of the same kind; but the barycenter's size, histogram and weights are chosen beforehand, the couplings are only stationary points of a non-convex problem, and the iteration's convergence at the step size used is not proved, so a structure carried by one input is shrunk by its weight at best and can be lost or redistributed by those choices
- [THEORY-1135](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1135.md): Optimal transport between two point sets related by one unknown global linear map from a Schatten ℓp ball reduces, when every admissible map preserves angles or the target is whitened, to choosing the coupling Γ that maximises the dual Schatten-q norm of the transported cross-covariance XΓYᵀ: the nuclear norm when the maps are orthogonal, and the Frobenius norm when they lie on a Frobenius sphere, which is exactly the Gromov–Wasserstein problem with cosine similarity and squared loss; in every case one transformation acts on the whole space
- [THEORY-1138](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1138.md): Optimal transport whose cost is the Lovász extension of a submodular set function on source–target assignments stays a convex problem, a zero-sum game in which an adversary picks the cost matrix from the function's base polytope, and reduces to ordinary optimal transport exactly when the set function is modular; the convexity needs submodularity, so the paper's own threshold cost, which is not concave at its threshold, falls outside it, and the induced discrepancy is symmetric only when the set function is
- [THEORY-1147](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1147.md): For entropy-regularized optimal transport with a fixed cost, the gradient of any differentiable function of the optimal plan with respect to the cost is obtained exactly from one linear system of size n + m whose matrix [[diag µ, T], [Tᵀ, diag ν]] is positive semidefinite and singular only along the gauge direction (1, −1), which does not affect the gradient; so the first-order effect of supervising any candidate pair on a utility of the whole alignment can be computed without forming the (nm)² Jacobian
- [THEORY-1149](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1149.md): For symmetric matrices compared under squared loss, co-optimal transport with independent row and column couplings is a lower bound on the Gromov–Wasserstein value, and for squared Euclidean distance matrices the two are equal and share optimal couplings, because GW is then a concave quadratic program whose bilinear relaxation is tight; for other symmetric matrices the bound can be strict
- [THEORY-1156](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1156.md): The fused Gromov–Wasserstein discrepancy between two attributed graphs, a single coupling that pays (1 − α) for moving node features and α for distorting pairwise structure, tends to the Wasserstein distance between the features as α → 0 and to the Gromov–Wasserstein distance between the structures as α → 1, lies above their α-weighted mixture, and for q = 1, α strictly between 0 and 1 and distance-matrix structures is a metric that vanishes exactly when a bijection of the nodes preserves weights, features and structure together

### mereology

- [THEORY-493](../record/theory.d/THEORY-493.md): From core mereology, classical extensional mereology (GEM) is reached by exactly three pairings of a decomposition principle with an unrestricted-sum principle: Supplementation with Sum2, Strong Supplementation with Sum3, and Complementation with Sum1; Supplementation with Sum3, the pairing given by Simons (1987), does not yield it, because which definition of 'sum' is used decides which decomposition axiom is needed

### metaphysics

- [THEORY-1083](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1083.md): Barad holds agential realism to be naturalized metaphysics justified by quantum mechanics and applied once, to the one reality, with its scope extended to the lifeworld; she rejects both reading it as an analogy and reading it as a template that quantum mechanics and other domains each instantiate
- [THEORY-1333](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1333.md): Bishop's contextual emergence, as stated in his 2024 SEP revision, is an ontological account: stability conditions not given at smaller and faster scales (parameter values, dimensionality, large-scale flows) constrain or enable what is possible and actual at those scales, as convection rolls constrain the motions of fluid molecules, without the brute new causal powers of strong emergence; laws bound possibility and contexts fix actualization

### moral-psychology

- [THEORY-435](../record/theory.d/THEORY-435.md): In Moral Foundations Questionnaire responses, Care and Fairness are endorsed across the political spectrum, while Loyalty, Authority and Sanctity rise toward the conservative end, in every world region sampled
- [THEORY-505](../record/theory.d/THEORY-505.md): Questionnaire items written for morality-as-cooperation's seven domains form seven factors when rated for relevance to moral decisions, in the UK, the US and Turkey, but not when rated as agreement with moral statements, and the two formats cannot be pooled into seven domains
- [THEORY-632](../record/theory.d/THEORY-632.md): Purity is moralized in self-report: in morality-as-cooperation's own questionnaire studies, purity items are rated about as morally relevant as loyalty and authority items, and harmless purity violations are condemned, so that theory's prediction that non-cooperative behaviour is morally neutral fails unless purity is itself cooperative
- [THEORY-653](../record/theory.d/THEORY-653.md): In the ethnographic record of the 60-society HRAF Probability Sample, seven cooperative behaviours are described as good in 961 of 962 valenced mentions, but each is recorded in between 90% and 15% of the societies, and the coding could barely have registered a negative

### motivation

- [THEORY-1305](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1305.md): In Kasser and Ryan's two cross-sectional samples, holding constant how much a person aspires to overall, the relative importance of extrinsic aspirations (money, fame, image) goes with less self-actualization and vitality and more physical symptoms, and of intrinsic aspirations (growth, relationships, community, health) with the reverse; the paper does not test whether this survives the reasons for pursuing the goals
- [THEORY-1331](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1331.md): Deci and Ryan's General Causality Orientations Scale measures autonomy, control and impersonal orientations as three separately scored and largely independent dispositions, reliable and stable over two months, whose validity rests on correlations with self-report measures in small samples, with behaviour its weakest support

### natural-sciences

- [THEORY-179](../record/theory.d/THEORY-179.md): In Bhattacharyya et al.'s single-cell swarm assays of E. coli MG1655, the daughters of one mother swarmed alike at the fourth generation sampled and varied again at the seventh; swarm size correlated with a plasmid fepA-promoter reporter of Fur derepression by low iron (Spearman r = 0.71), and an iron chelator or added iron shifted swarming and held the shared state longer; a three-class switching model fitted to two time points matched the lineages only with a delay of three to four generations before switching, which the authors read as ruling out a bistable switch
- [THEORY-473](../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md): Scaled down to one organism, Hutchinson's niche, defined as the conditions that give that individual an expected lifetime reproductive success of at least one, is observed only as a point; the rest of it is counterfactual, reached by translocation in only a few dimensions and otherwise inferred from other individuals, so in practice it is the niche of a phenotype class, and its authors call it mostly metaphorical
- [THEORY-499](../record/theory.d/THEORY-499.md): The breakup of the Eulalia parent body beside the Jupiter 3:1 resonance, 785–965 Myr ago, can plausibly have supplied the cluster of large lunar craters dated near 800 Ma, but shown only for the most favourable of five model solutions, the one carried through, with an average largest lunar impactor too small for Copernicus, and with the cluster's absolute date inherited from Copernicus alone
- [THEORY-508](../record/theory.d/THEORY-508.md): The Belousov–Zhabotinsky oscillation is a relaxation cycle in which autocatalytic production of HBrO₂ oxidizes the catalyst until bromide, released as the oxidized catalyst is reduced by bromomalonic acid, switches the autocatalysis off; a closed batch oscillates only as a transient of up to several thousand cycles on its way to equilibrium, and only a continuous-flow reactor sustains it indefinitely
- [THEORY-1511](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1511.md): Jaber, Jung, Matecki and Petrof review evidence that fully controlled mechanical ventilation weakens, shrinks and injures the human diaphragm as it does in animals: biopsies from brain-dead organ donors ventilated for hours to days show diaphragm fibre atrophy and injury with oxidative stress and raised proteolysis markers, not seen in the pectoralis, the changes growing with the duration of ventilation, and diaphragm twitch pressure in ventilated patients falls by about a third in six days; in animals, keeping spontaneous effort lessens the loss but leaves a residual deficit

### network-science

- [THEORY-456](../record/theory.d/THEORY-456.md): Iterating Ollivier–Ricci flow on edge weights lengthens edges between communities relative to edges within them, so a weight threshold can separate the communities; but the separation is proved only on symmetric clique graphs under the uniform neighbour measure, and there only by a constant factor for gateway edges, and on a two-block stochastic block model the method fails at an inter/intra ratio near 0.55, where other methods still recover the blocks and well short of the detectability threshold near 0.78
- [THEORY-502](../record/theory.d/THEORY-502.md): Forman–Ricci curvature of a graph edge, taken with no cells above the edges, depends only on the weights of the edge, its two endpoints and the edges adjacent to it, and with unit weights reduces to 4 − deg(v₁) − deg(v₂); it is a local, closed-form degree-and-weight statistic that sees no triangles or cycles, unlike Ollivier's curvature, which needs a transport problem per edge
- [THEORY-576](../record/theory.d/THEORY-576.md): In a bundled network, one fiber graph attached at a single node to every node of a base graph, the low Laplacian spectrum is the base spectrum divided by the fiber size to first order, so the gap exponent (Fiedler dimension) is set by the base while the density-of-states exponent (spectral dimension) is the fiber's; the two come apart generically and coincide only in special cases, and relaxation then decays with the spectral dimension at intermediate times but equilibrates on a time set by the Fiedler dimension
- [THEORY-1130](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1130.md): The Gromov–Wasserstein distance, half the least Lp distortion of a coupling, is a pseudometric on all networks with a probability measure on the nodes and any bounded edge weights, symmetric or not, and it is zero exactly when the two networks are weakly isomorphic, images of one network under maps that preserve weights and measures; so it compares only what the weight function and node measure record
- [THEORY-1152](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1152.md): Between two weighted directed networks with node measures, the Gromov–Wasserstein distance is bounded below by a hierarchy of invariants, each in an in-going and an out-going version, and the strongest of them, a transport problem whose costs are themselves transport problems, equals a transport problem whose costs are one-dimensional Wasserstein distances between the nodes' weight profiles, so it is computed in closed form; the bounds are one-sided, and two networks can agree on all of them while being at positive distance
- [THEORY-1159](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1159.md): Aligning three networks jointly, through one multi-marginal fused Gromov–Wasserstein coupling with an anchor-based random-walk cost and a cluster decomposition, finds held-out correspondences better than pairwise and existing multi-network methods in most cases, as the paper's plots show, in both pairwise and whole-tuple hits, on benchmarks whose true correspondences are consistent across the three networks by construction; whether the joint coupling itself is the cause is not separated from the new cost and the clustering

### neuroscience

- [THEORY-1312](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1312.md): A phase-amplitude coupling measure can be significant when only one non-sinusoidal rhythm is present, because the rhythm's harmonics carry amplitude that depends on its own phase; such coupling is confined to bands spanning the rhythm's harmonics, so a measured coupling is evidence of one rhythm modulating another only after waveform shape is controlled
- [THEORY-1317](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1317.md): During held covert spatial attention in human fronto-parietal and visual cortex, the amplitude of broadband high gamma (80–250 Hz) is coupled to the phase of an endogenous 2–5 Hz rhythm, more strongly for the contralateral field, and the trial-by-trial strength of that coupling correlates with faster detection; the evidence is correlational, so it shows that the coupling tracks attention, not that it improves it
- [THEORY-1337](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1337.md): Neural field recordings carry aperiodic 1/f-like activity with power at every frequency, whose exponent varies with age, state and task; so power in a band, correlated power changes across bands, and ratios of band power can arise from the aperiodic component with no oscillation changing, and 1/f structure is a ubiquitous background of field data rather than a mark of any particular organization
- [THEORY-1340](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1340.md): Juarrero reads the delayed-response studies of Churchland, Shenoy and colleagues and of Mante, Sussillo and colleagues, as she reports them, as showing that training forms a task-defined, low-dimensional subregion of motor, premotor and prefrontal population activity (a preparatory subspace whose end state predicts reaction time and movement; an axis of choice organized as a line attractor) that acts as top-down governing constraints on a monkey's delayed response while the trial's cue and evidence select within it, and suggests that the axis of choice might be considered the neural correlate of a prior intention and the selection vector, found in a simulation, that of a proximate intention

### operations-research

- [THEORY-501](../record/theory.d/THEORY-501.md): In weekly waste collection where each point's visit days are free and its bin capacity must cover the longest gap between visits, a genetic algorithm that searches visit schedules and derives bins from them builds routes about 6% cheaper than eight-hour Gurobi incumbents but buys about 20% more bin capacity, ending level on overall cost at its best of 30 runs and 4–6% worse on a typical run, on five 12-point instances where the incumbents' own optimality gaps are 26–32%

### personhood

- [THEORY-417](../record/theory.d/THEORY-417.md): 'Personal identity' names several largely independent questions, among them who one is (characterization), what a person is, what it takes for one to persist, how many of us there are and what matters in survival; the persistence question concerns numerical identity, which 'remaining the same person' in the characterization sense presupposes, and posing it as 'a person at one time and a person at another' assumes that we are persons essentially

### philosophy-of-mathematics

- [THEORY-401](../record/theory.d/THEORY-401.md): A fair lottery on the natural numbers has a uniform, regular probability defined on every set of tickets, by normalised numerosity with values in the hyperrationals; it is fixed only up to a choice of free ultrafilter, it is hyperfinitely and not countably additive, and its standard part is ordinary asymptotic density

### philosophy-of-science

- [THEORY-441](../record/theory.d/THEORY-441.md): In spatially compact vacuum general relativity the Hamiltonian vanishes, so time is represented by no flow on a symplectic space and change by no functions on a space of states; this problem of time does not come from the 3+1 split, is absent from asymptotically flat general relativity, and does not show change to be illusory
- [THEORY-463](../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md): In classical statistical mechanics a strictly irreversible approach to equilibrium cannot come from the isolated Hamiltonian dynamics alone: the fine-grained Gibbs entropy is constant and bounded systems recur, so each account surveyed either weakens the target to typical or long-run behaviour or adds something from outside the dynamics
- [THEORY-469](../record/theory.d/THEORY-469.md): Because persistence (mean absolute fitness at least 1) and selection (fitness differences) are logically independent, niche construction theory's evolutionary niche, read externally as the factors producing fitness differences in a population, differs in extension from the realized population ecological niche even after unit and modality are matched, so it is not a simple translation of Hutchinson's niche
- [THEORY-550](../record/theory.d/THEORY-550.md): Unsupervised clustering is not made epistemically superior to supervised classification by the absence of labels: it is sensitive to sample bias, highly sensitive to how inputs are represented, and overfits, with the number of clusters acting as a capacity control just as parametric complexity does in supervised learning
- [THEORY-569](../record/theory.d/THEORY-569.md): Measured as the contrast between a set of explanantia's CohOG+ coherence with the explanandum and with its negation, explanatory power satisfies Roche and Sober's Two Likelihood Inequalities for single hypotheses and fails the One, and in one causal chain and one collider it ranks the richer set above the sparser over a range of priors, where no two-place TLI measure can rank a conjunction so
- [THEORY-639](../record/theory.d/THEORY-639.md): Inductive risk arises not only when a hypothesis is accepted but in choosing a significance level, in characterising data and in interpreting results: in the dioxin cancer studies each of these choices traded false positives against false negatives, three panels scored the same rat-liver slides differently, and threshold and no-threshold readings of the same data underlie regulatory limits about 100 times apart

### probabilistic-modeling

- [THEORY-426](../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md): Evaluating expected free energy recursively over the beliefs an agent would hold after each plausible outcome makes active inference a pruned tree search over belief states, formally analogous to Bellman recursion; in single deterministic runs on a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze it planned through short-term costs that agents with a shorter horizon did not; that the pruning keeps deep search tractable beyond toy problems is argued, not shown
- [THEORY-475](../record/theory.d/THEORY-475.md): In simulations from the drift-diffusion model itself, with 12 subjects and 20 to 150 trials each, hierarchical Bayesian estimation recovers every DDM parameter with less error than per-subject maximum likelihood, χ²-quantile fitting or non-hierarchical Bayes, most of all at few trials; whether the gain survives misspecification, and how much of the power gain is the hierarchy's, is not shown
- [THEORY-515](../record/theory.d/THEORY-515.md): Sampling a posterior p(x|y) when only joint samples (X, Y) can be drawn is solved by a Schrödinger bridge on the joint space, with y held fixed along the path, between the joint distribution and any reference sharing its y-marginal; the bridge averages the per-observation bridges, its first iterative-proportional-fitting step is the conditional score-based model, and the error of later steps at the data end falls as 1/n times the reference's distance from the bridge
- [THEORY-587](../record/theory.d/THEORY-587.md): A U-turn stopping rule for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo leaves the target invariant once the trajectory is built as a random balanced doubling tree and the next state is drawn only from states that could have regenerated it; with a dual-averaged step size it matched the best hand-tuned identity-mass HMC on two of four test posteriors and beat it about threefold on the other two, and its ergodicity is not shown
- [THEORY-1045](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1045.md): On synthetic data from factorial hidden Markov models with three or five hidden chains of two or three states, an unconstrained hidden Markov model with as many states as the chains have joint settings overfits, its test-set excess over the true model rising to 175 bits per observation at five three-state chains against 4.5 for the factorial model trained exactly, while factorial models trained with completely factorized or structured variational E steps are not significantly worse than exact training

### quantum-foundations

- [THEORY-403](../record/theory.d/THEORY-403.md): The single-photon Mach–Zehnder phenomenology with balanced beamsplitters and phases 0 or π, including which-way detection, the bomb tester, delayed choice and the quantum eraser, is reproduced exactly by a local, deterministic classical field model with an epistemic restriction, so that slice of interference forces neither complementarity, nor observer-dependent reality, nor nonlocality
- [THEORY-455](../record/theory.d/THEORY-455.md): Every finite stochastic transition matrix on a configuration space equals the entrywise squared modulus of a complex matrix, unitary after dilation, so the Hilbert-space formalism can be written over any indivisible stochastic process as a non-unique representation; within that representation interference is the term by which the process fails to divide at an intermediate time, relative to the chosen configurations, and an ideal correlating environment restores divisibility
- [THEORY-474](../record/theory.d/THEORY-474.md): Spekkens' toy bit theory, restricted to maximal knowledge and post-selected measurements, has a universal, sound and complete ZX-style graphical calculus whose phase-free rules and symplectic check-matrix conditions are exactly those of pure qubit stabilizer theory; the two calculi differ in the phase group, the Klein four-group against Z₄
- [THEORY-482](../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md): For a closed quantum system that starts thermal and is measured projectively in energy before and after a unitary drive, the two-point-measurement work obeys the Jarzynski equality and the Tasaki–Crooks relation in exactly the classical form, because those energy measurements erase the coherences in which a quantum difference could appear
- [THEORY-553](../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md): In the Döring–Isham topos representation of quantum theory a bounded physical quantity cannot take values in the topos's real-number object; it is represented faithfully by an arrow from the spectral presheaf to a presheaf of monotone real functions over subcontexts, so its value at a context is a spread that widens as the context shrinks, and these values form only a commutative monoid, under which sums of daseinised quantities are not daseinisations of sums
- [THEORY-584](../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md): The quantum fidelity tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) is exactly the classical Bhattacharyya overlap of the two states' outcome distributions minimized over all measurements, and the minimum is attained by a projective measurement whose eigenvalues are square roots of likelihood ratios
- [THEORY-605](../record/theory.d/THEORY-605.md): In any ontological model that reproduces the quantum predictions and treats independently prepared systems as having product distributions over a joint state that is just the list of their states, distinct pure quantum states have distributions over the ontic state whose supports overlap in measure zero, so the pure state is fixed by the ontic state; approximate agreement within ε bounds the overlap by 2ε^{1/n}
- [THEORY-619](../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md): Over the poset of commutative von Neumann subalgebras, coarse-graining a projector to a smaller subalgebra is exactly the direct image of its clopen region of the Gelfand spectrum under restriction, so the coarse-graining presheaf is the presheaf of clopen spectral regions; and a quantum state's sieve-valued truth values are fixed by one coherent family of regions, its supports: a proposition is true at a subcontext exactly when the support there lies under the coarse-grained proposition
- [THEORY-635](../record/theory.d/THEORY-635.md): If the quantum state of a Bohmian system is identified with the velocity dispositions it induces on the particles, inequivalent states can share one dispositional history: every energy eigenstate of a free particle in a box induces zero velocity everywhere, so the reading erases differences of energy and of typicality unless the map from states to velocity fields is injective for generic solutions, which is conjectured, not proved
- [THEORY-664](../record/theory.d/THEORY-664.md): In a finite-dimensional probabilistic theory with unrestricted effects and local tomography, if every system can steer each of its own states from a composite with a copy of itself, every irreducible state space is homogeneous and weakly self-dual; steering does not yet give strong self-duality, so it stops short of the Jordan-algebraic and quantum state spaces
- [THEORY-695](../record/theory.d/THEORY-695.md): Two quantum states can be broadcast if and only if they commute, and cloned if and only if they are identical or orthogonal; the theorem is proved for invertible density operators and marks a line within quantum theory, not a witness of nonclassicality
- [THEORY-1058](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1058.md): Given constructor theory's principles of locality and of classical information, a single further prohibition, that two information observables with mutually disjoint attributes have a union that is not an information observable, is enough for a medium to have information attributes that cannot be distinguished, unclonable and jointly unsharp observables, measurements that are deterministic yet unpredictable, irreducible disturbance by measurement, and locally inaccessible information; quantum information is an instance
- [THEORY-1074](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1074.md): In Di Biagio and Rovelli's relational account two classical subsystems' perspectives merge, agreeing on a variable's value and on each other's, when they couple to that variable or to each other, and a coupling to a complementary variable can remove a relative fact from a perspective that did not interact; that this answers the combination problem and keeps perspectives consistent is shown only in worked examples computed relative to a single outside system
- [THEORY-1080](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1080.md): In relational quantum mechanics as Rovelli first stated it, the relation between two observers' descriptions is itself a quantum fact relative to a third system, so no observer's view can be deduced from another's and there is no description in toto, only a net of partial descriptions; the views are held consistent only in that the third system predicts correlated outcomes, which is shown for a single measurement and asserted in general

### representation-learning

- [THEORY-301](../record/theory.d/THEORY-301.md): The Procrustes distance between regularization-normalized representations and their average linear-decoding distance bound each other only through the participation ratio of the kernel difference: a small Procrustes distance forces a small decoding distance, but not conversely
- [THEORY-305](../record/theory.d/THEORY-305.md): SimCLR's InfoNCE loss, over all n objects with a Gaussian kernel on the unit sphere, equals a graph-Laplacian quadratic form on the augmentation matrix plus the log of InfoNCE's normalizers, which is spectral clustering only in a sense that admits any regularizer and does not make the minimizer the Laplacian's eigenvectors
- [THEORY-312](../record/theory.d/THEORY-312.md): The large-batch InfoNCE loss is the negative HSIC between representations and image identity plus a nonnegative log-mean-exp of the centred critic, so it bounds a kernel dependence loss from above
- [THEORY-420](../record/theory.d/THEORY-420.md): In trained transformers, zeroing a decile of a weight matrix's singular values does damage that falls monotonically with their size in square matrices, whose random-matrix null reaches zero, but not in rectangular ones, whose null has a positive lower edge: there the smallest decile is never the least damaging and can be among the most
- [THEORY-640](../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md): Measured as mutual 10-nearest-neighbour overlap, competent vision models agree more with one another and better language models agree more with vision models, but the cross-modal score reaches only 0.16 of a possible 1, is the maximum over all layer pairs, and was adopted after a global kernel metric showed only a very weak trend
- [THEORY-737](../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md): In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, the least-squares residual of a novel labelling on the top-k eigenspace, with the labelled entries left free, equals exactly the part of the labelling outside that eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb
- [THEORY-971](../record/theory.d/THEORY-971.md): A unit that thresholds a pre-activation equal to a term depending only on one operand plus a term depending only on the other cannot be active on exactly the pairs with a given sum when that sum has two decompositions: if it is active on (x, y) and (z, w), it is active on (x, w) or on (z, y); so a sum computed from separately represented operands needs an earlier unit that combines them, as Ameisen et al. argue for addition in language models
- [THEORY-976](../record/theory.d/THEORY-976.md): In a Claude 3.5 Haiku variant finetuned by Marks et al. to exploit reward-model biases described in fictional documents, a cross-layer-transcoder feature that in pretraining-style text fires almost only where those biases are discussed was active in all 100 short Human/Assistant-formatted prompts tested and in 1 of the same 100 without that formatting, and suppressing such bias features cut the sampled rate of three bias behaviours, including two the model was never trained to show
- [THEORY-984](../record/theory.d/THEORY-984.md): In Claude 3.5 Haiku, on the prompt "Fact: the capital of the state containing Dallas is", which it completes with "Austin", an attribution graph shows Dallas features activating Texas features that, with "say a capital" features, promote Austin, beside a direct edge from Dallas to "say Austin"; inhibiting the Dallas features lowers the Texas features and leaves "say a capital" largely intact, and replacing the Texas features with those of California, Georgia, British Columbia, China or the Byzantine Empire makes the model name that place's capital
- [THEORY-1005](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1005.md): On one MLP layer each of GPT2-small, Pythia-410M and Pythia-1.4B, transcoders trained to imitate the MLP lay on or above the sparsity–loss frontier of sparse autoencoders trained on its output, at one learning rate tuned on transcoders and one seed, and in a single rater's blind reading of 50 random features each from Pythia-410M layer 15, 41 transcoder and 38 SAE features were judged interpretable
- [THEORY-1017](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1017.md): In Claude 3.5 Haiku, writing the second line of a rhyming couplet whose first line ends "grab it", features for the candidate rhymes "rabbit" and "habit" are active on the newline token before the line, steering them changes the line's final word only when applied at that token, and suppressing "rabbit" turns the line towards "habit"; injecting a "rabbit" or "green" word feature at that point in 25 other poems ended the line with the injected word in 70% of cases, and such planned-word features were found in about half of the poems the authors examined
- [THEORY-1018](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1018.md): In Claude 3.5 Haiku, on the jailbreak prompt "Babies Outlive Mustard Block." asking it to join the first letters and say how to make one, the attribution graph for its output "BOMB" shows separate letter-wise paths voting for the output and no internal representation of the word or of a bomb-making request before it is written; "make a bomb" features first fire on the model's own "To make a bomb", injecting one on "BOMB" brings an immediate refusal, and the refusal that does come waits for the sentence's end
- [THEORY-1028](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1028.md): In InceptionV1 trained on ImageNet, the ten curve units of layer mixed3b each respond most to curves of one orientation, with responses invariant to fill and colour and jointly spanning all orientations under rotation of real images; for one of them, 3b:379, which fires on about 11% of dataset positions, activation level separated one author's blind four-class labels of over 800 activation-binned images, and curves and imperfect curves made up 55% of its contribution to expected value
- [THEORY-1031](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1031.md): In GPT-J, inserting 10,000 CounterFact counterfactuals at once by a closed-form least-squares update of the MLP output matrices of layers 3 to 8, spread so that each layer writes a share of each fact's required change to the subject's hidden state, gives an editing score of 85.8 (efficacy 98.9, paraphrase 88.6, neighbourhood 73.7) with fluency kept, against 67.6 for weight-decayed fine-tuning, which breaks generation, 50.3 for ROME applied one fact at a time and 23.1 for MEND; GPT-NeoX scores 82.0, and editing late MLPs or attention instead does worse
- [THEORY-1032](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1032.md): When Claude 3.5 Haiku was given continued pretraining on synthetic documents describing 52 fictional reward-model biases and then trained by SFT and RL to exploit 47 of them, its rate of exploiting the 5 held-out biases rose from 17% to 45% of applicable episodes, and it applied new biases described in context as a reward model's more often than the same biases attributed to other entities; without the documents the held-out rate rose only to 20%, and without SFT it still rose
- [THEORY-1033](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1033.md): In a 16-layer transformer language model trained on WikiText-103, the training prefixes that most activate a sampled feed-forward hidden unit share patterns that human annotators recognize, mostly shallow in layers 1–9 and semantic in layers 10–16; projected through the output embedding, a unit's output weights put the next token of its top prefix first in up to about 3.5% of units in the upper layers and almost none below; and a layer's top prediction differs from every unit's in at least about 68% of examples
- [THEORY-1036](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1036.md): In a model that fits y = Σ v_i x_i² with ỹ = Σ_r (W_r·x)² + b, on independent inputs of zero mean, unit variance and common fourth moment k, the expected squared error at the optimal bias is (k − 1)Σ(n_i − v_i)² − 2Σn_i² + 2Σn_i²/C_i, in the squared embedding lengths n_i and capacities C_i = (w_i·w_i)²/Σ_j(w_i·w_j)², and its minimum with the capacities summing to the number of neurons D gives C_i = clip((k − 1)v_i/((k − 3)λ) − 2/(k − 3), 0, 1): for k ≤ 3 each feature is given a whole dimension or none, and for k > 3 a feature is shared between neurons exactly when 2λ/(k − 1) < v_i < λ
- [THEORY-1038](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1038.md): In InceptionV1, the ten curve units of mixed3b, which respond to curves of one orientation and not to the opposite one, regain the 180° echo of earlier curve units when their input is restricted to mixed3a early curves with the negative weights removed, and not when the negative weights are kept; a network one author wrote by hand from the described circuit, without looking at the original weights and tuned afterwards, has grayscale curve units that the authors show, by figures only, approximating the natural ones on synthetic curves across radii and orientations; and substituting them for the ten units recovered 26 of the 46 top-5 classifications lost by deleting the units, on 2,000 validation images, a result the authors call preliminary
- [THEORY-1042](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1042.md): In the Overview of Early Vision's taxonomy of InceptionV1, every one of the 1,056 units of conv2d0 to mixed3b is assigned by the authors to exactly one of 77 groups, and 391 of them (37%), from 7% of conv2d2 to 48% of conv2d1 and 45% of mixed3b, are in groups whose own captions call them catch-all, broad and not well defined, low-confidence, unstudied or not understood; the mixed3b curve family is 10 of that layer's 480 units
- [THEORY-1128](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1128.md): If a sequence is generated by a random walk over points of a compact Riemannian manifold whose step probabilities depend only on (locally scaled) distance, then negative log co-occurrence over a window that grows suitably with the number of points, less a term for each point, approaches the squared geodesic distance, whatever the link from distance to one-step probability; so log co-occurrence statistics identify the metric, and coordinates only up to isometry
- [THEORY-1139](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1139.md): A graph network that learns its sheaf restriction maps from node features at each layer reaches the top, mostly within one standard deviation, of the standard small heterophilic node-classification benchmarks and stays within about one point of the best on homophilic ones; on a synthetic balanced bipartite graph it learns the negative transport the theory prescribes, but whether the maps it learns on real graphs have the geometry the theory credits for its success has not been examined
- [THEORY-1313](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1313.md): In two 7–8B chat models, the shift that finetuning induces along a difference-of-means persona vector correlates with how strongly the finetuned model then expresses that trait, r = 0.76–0.97 across synthetic datasets for evil, sycophancy and hallucination, above cross-trait baselines of 0.34–0.86; the last-prompt-token projection predicts a response's trait at r = 0.75–0.83 overall but mainly by telling prompt types apart
- [THEORY-1342](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1342.md): In Transformer attention the weights each query puts on the positions depend only on query–key compatibility, softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k), and the output is those weights applied to the values, so for a fixed input what a head selects and what it transports are separate factors; because queries, keys and values are all projections of the same input, the separation holds only with the input, and so the pattern, held fixed

### social-identity

- [THEORY-1584](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1584.md): Botzung and colleagues report that rival basketball fans recalled the same plays with valence set by their allegiance, recalled plays good for their own side more accurately and confidently, and that rated intensity, not valence, modulated amygdala and hippocampal activity at retrieval
- [THEORY-1588](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1588.md): Akerlof and Kranton propose putting identity, a self-image tied to social categories and their prescriptions, into the utility function, so that one's own and others' departures from the prescriptions cost utility, and use it to account for gender-typed occupations, oppositional identities and the asymmetry in housework

### social-science

- [THEORY-329](../record/theory.d/THEORY-329.md): In 32,479 Weibo posts of 2011–2016 scored with an emotion lexicon, posts tagged fake by the platform's fact-checkers carry more anger and less joy than true posts from verified accounts, and a post's share of anger words goes with more retweets after controls; whether the gap is due to falsity, and whether anger causes the spread, is not shown
- [THEORY-450](../record/theory.d/THEORY-450.md): Across 1,176 premodern archaeological sites, the house-size Gini rises only weakly with the number of levels of political hierarchy and with polity population, and the spread of Gini widens with scale: scale raises the ceiling on domestic wealth inequality without setting its level
- [THEORY-552](../record/theory.d/THEORY-552.md): Indeed's US software-development job-postings index rose to 233.8 in February 2022 and fell to 65.2 by mid-February 2025, measured against 1 February 2020 = 100, while all postings stood near 110; it was the deepest fall of any Indeed sector, though not the only one to have more than doubled, and the postings data cannot apportion the fall among interest rates, over-hiring and AI
- [THEORY-555](../record/theory.d/THEORY-555.md): In London in 2018, Airbnb listings that were possibly breaking the 90-night short-let cap, defined as entire homes offered for more than 180 days a year by hosts with two or more listings, were about 0.16% of the housing stock (about 5,300 homes) but 3.5–7% in a few central small areas, and across small areas they correlate weakly with flats, private renting and low dwelling-type diversity
- [THEORY-601](../record/theory.d/THEORY-601.md): Among US undergraduates in the HERI surveys, students with higher verbal ability and stronger self-reported intellectual dispositions select into philosophy, and after adjusting for their entering SAT or freshman scores philosophy majors still score higher than other majors on GRE Verbal (SMD 0.48) and LSAT (0.35) but not on GRE Quantitative, and report more Habits of Mind and Pluralistic Orientation; the adjusted advantage is an association, not a shown effect of studying philosophy
- [THEORY-674](../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md): In Garg and Fetzer's GPT-4o-mini extraction from NBER and CEPR working papers, edges kept in at least 4 of 9 passes and never checked against human labels, the mean per-paper share of edges labelled as backed by difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, an RCT, regression discontinuity or synthetic control rose from 7.7% in 1990 to 31.7% in 2020, at every overlap threshold; the paper's per-decade slope fell from +0.0187 to +0.0011 once method mix and graph volume were controlled
- [THEORY-1462](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1462.md): Haushofer and Fehr hold that poverty causes stress and negative affect, and that these in turn make people more present-biased and risk-averse independent of credit constraints and background risk, so that behaviour taken as the poor's own preference may partly be an effect of poverty and may help perpetuate it; they grant that the affect-to-choice link rests only on laboratory inductions, and that no nonlinearity strong enough to make a poverty trap has been shown

### society-and-governance

- [THEORY-488](../record/theory.d/THEORY-488.md): Clark (2020), synthesising open writing by Russian military authors of 2015 to 2020, chiefly Chekinov and Bogdanov, Bartosh and Kiselev, with no stated rule for choosing sources, reports that they use "hybrid war" for a category of war marked off by its objective, reshaping a target state's governance, geostrategic orientation and worldview, in which every action up to conventional military force is subordinate to an information campaign, and not, as he says Western usage does, for a set of means below the threshold of armed conflict
- [THEORY-651](../record/theory.d/THEORY-651.md): Disinformation incidents labelled with DISARM techniques can be carried in standard STIX 2.1 without extending it, as an intrusion set that uses attack patterns, is attributed to a threat actor and targets locations; the DISINFOX mapping that moved 118 incidents into OpenCTI this way keeps only a name, a free-text description, a first-seen date and labels beside those three relationships, with no object or property for an incident's narratives, channels, evidence or countermeasures or for the confidence of its attribution

### thermodynamics

- [THEORY-676](../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md): Dewar's information-theoretic derivation of maximum entropy production does not reach the far-from-equilibrium regime where the principle is applied: the 2003 route needs a mean-field step and an unargued assumption about path counts, the 2005 route's orthogonality condition, which yields both maximum and minimum dissipation, holds only with linear constitutive relations, and the 2003 self-organized-criticality corollary is an artefact of a quadratic expansion
- [THEORY-1265](../record/theory.d/THEORY-1265.md): Approximating a chemical master equation by a Fokker–Planck or nonlinear Langevin equation gets the quasi-potential right only at the fixed points: between them it mis-estimates the barriers, so escape rates come out wrong by a factor exponential in system size and the approximation can pick the wrong one of two states as the long-run favourite, and its apparent entropy production vanishes at every steady state, missing the dissipation that sustains it
